jargon_glossary.meaning: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.

jargon_glossary.meaning: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.

jargon_glossary.term: Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)
jargon_glossary.meaning: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.

jargon_glossary.meaning: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP).
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.

jargon_glossary.term: TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)
jargon_glossary.meaning: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.

should_i_upgrade.text: Per-request `mm_processor_kwargs` and `media_io_kwargs` now return an error unless the server is started with `--trust-request-mm-kwargs`; server-level `--mm-processor-kwargs` / `--media-io-kwargs` and offline `LLM` are unchanged (#58830). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading
`tokenizer_mode="slow"` was removed; it already behaved like `"hf"` under Transformers v5 (#58545). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading
`--enable-mamba-fine-grained-prefix-cache` was renamed to `--enable-mamba-shared-prefix-checkpoint` (#57382). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading

Online quantization through `quantization="fp8"` now redirects to the `fp8_per_tensor` online shorthand (#53585); Quark-specific silent online MXFP4 quantization was removed in favor of the online quantization API (#51800). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading

The AllSpark INT8 W8A16 GEMM backend was removed (#58001). The `return_assistant_tokens_mask` option of `/render` and the `assistant_tokens_mask` response field were removed (#57520). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading
`VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD` was removed; use `--engram-config` (#57937). `VLLM_XPU_ENABLE_XPU_GRAPH` was removed and XPU graphs are on by default (#51600). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading
The comma-separated form of `--collect-detailed-traces` was removed; use the list syntax (#55702). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading

New defaults: `--enforce-eager` also disables JIT kernel warmup unless fault tolerance is enabled (#58197, #58593); `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` uses breakable CUDA graphs without torch.compile (#57586) and disables sequence parallelism and async TP (#56377); DeepSeek-V4.1 SWA bounded replay is on (#56227) except on ROCm (#57906); Engram host tables are shared across co-located DP replicas when possible (#57651); FlashMLA mega attention is the DeepSeek-V4.1 default on SM100 (#56935); the AITER w4a4 ASM GEMM is off by default on ROCm (#57055). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading

Model Runner V1 + PP > 1 + async scheduling + structured output is now rejected at startup (#56250); `json_object` is rejected at validation with the outlines backend (#57743). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading
`transformers` now has an upper bound in requirements (#59614). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading

technical_deep_dive.theme: Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups (DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3)
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v0.31.0, teams operating frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA Blackwell (GB200/GB300/B200), Hopper (H100/H200), and multi-node Expert Parallel (EP) clusters.
tech_bullets: Kimi K3 and MiniMax-M3: Kimi-K3 vision patch embedder as a GEMM (#58527), fused KimiViT QK RoPE (up to 29x, #58651), routed expert quantization (#57430), reasoning parser (#57098) and reasoning token (#58527, #58651).

GLM-5.3-Flash: opt-in FlashAttention and FlashMLA sparse backends on SM90 (#55385), NoPE sparse MLA on the FlashInfer SM120 backend (#55277), cooperative top-k for small decode batches (#57327) (#55385, #55277).
AMD ROCm: AITER v0.1.23 (#56885, #58867), torch 2.13 and Triton 3.8 (#50605, #58006), `triton_kernels` 3.8 MXFP4 MoE for gpt-oss and DeepSeek-V4 (#55934), a ROCR host segfault fixed (#57328)..

Startup and memory: parallel Triton warmup compilation (#58582), JIT warmup disabled under `--enforce-eager` (#58197) unless fault tolerance is on (#58593), DeepGEMM warmup reusing the MoE workspace (#58582, #58197).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens

technical_deep_dive.theme: Model Runner V2 (MRV2) Consolidation & Breakable CUDA Graphs
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v0.31.0, teams operating model runner v2 relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on All CUDA and ROCm GPU fleets running vLLM's V2 execution engine.
tech_bullets: Intel XPU: PyTorch 2.14 (#56013), XPU graphs on by default (#51600), EPLB (#44987), int8 W8A8 MoE on Triton (#53162), batch invariance (#55881), SYCL rotary embedding (#55721), fused QK RMSNorm + (#56013, #51600).
New defaults: `--enforce-eager` also disables JIT kernel warmup unless fault tolerance is enabled (#58197, #58593). `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` uses breakable CUDA graphs without torch.compile (#57586).
Model Runner V1 + PP > 1 + async scheduling + structured output is now rejected at startup (#56250); `json_object` is rejected at validation with the outlines backend (#57743) (#56250, #57743).

Batch invariance: breakable CUDA graphs without torch.compile by default under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` (#57586), sequence parallelism and async TP disabled (#56377), and NCCL 2.31 collectives kept (#57586, #56377).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Cuts CPU dispatch overhead and lowers inter-token latency (ITL) by 3–15% while simplifying engine maintenance

technical_deep_dive.theme: Low-Precision Quantization Kernels (NVFP4, MXFP4, MXFP8, FP8 & Humming)
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v0.31.0, teams operating low-precision quantization kernels relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA Blackwell (SM100 NVFP4), Hopper (SM90 FP8), and AMD MI350/MI355X.
tech_bullets: Online quantization through `quantization="fp8"` now redirects to the `fp8_per_tensor` online shorthand (#53585); Quark-specific silent online MXFP4 quantization was removed in favor of the online (#53585, #51800).

Humming: Hadamard transforms and NVFP4/MXFP4/MXFP8 online quantization (#56685), asymmetric wNaM through compressed-tensors (#46528), humming-kernels 0.1.16 (#58054), and Humming in the W4A8 (#56685, #46528).

New capabilities: native Quark W4A16 INT4/UINT4 exports (#48606), opt-in load-time MXFP4 dequantization (#50814), explicit per-token NVFP4 MoE backends (#57176), and a canonical N-first layout for (#48606, #50814).

Fixes: MXFP8 on layers below `mm_mxfp8` shape limits (#54223), online NVFP4 scales on reload (#57954), LM head linear metadata (#58444), and the fused SiLU-mul block-quant path skipped under a SwiGLU (#54223, #57954).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput

technical_deep_dive.theme: Next-Gen Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3, DSpark, DFlash, MTP & Suffix)
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v0.31.0, teams operating next-gen speculative decoding relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell, AMD MI300X/MI355X, and CPU/XPU draft runners.
tech_bullets: Scheduler: `--max-num-active-seqs` (#56758), adaptive `--long-prefill-token-threshold` (#57951, #58459), `skipped_waiting` replaced by a KV-holding waiting queue (#58947), atomic admission of `n > 1` (#56758, #57951).

Speculative decoding: LiLiCorr drafter (#57934), DFlash async scheduling (#58065) and context K/V in the draft CUDA graph (#57632), Gemma4 DSpark adaptive verification (#57263), Kimi-K3 (#57934, #58065).

MoE communication: MoonEP backend (#52101), DeepEPv2 with sequence parallelism (#57210) and EPLB + shared-expert overlap (#57236), low-SM multimem reduce-scatter (#55072), EPLB load statistics during (#52101, #57210).

New model capabilities: DiffusionGemma structured generation mode with bounded single-token choices (#57250), MiMo V2 MXFP4 MoE, BF16 MoE router and DFlash drafts (#57784), Cohere2MoE auxiliary (#57250, #57784).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth

technical_deep_dive.theme: Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling (AMD ROCm 10 / MI355X, TPU & XPU)
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v0.31.0, teams operating multi-vendor accelerator scaling relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on AMD Instinct MI300X/MI350/MI355X (ROCm 10.0), Intel XPU, and Google Cloud TPU.
tech_bullets: `VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD` was removed; use `--engram-config` (#57937). `VLLM_XPU_ENABLE_XPU_GRAPH` was removed and XPU graphs are on by default (#51600) (#57937, #51600).

KV connectors: NIXL pipeline-parallel push prefill for attention-HMA (#50494) and packed MLA layouts (#50499), transport-failure metrics split from KV expiry (#55854), dead peer state released (#50494, #50499).
ROCm: AITER v0.1.23 (#58867), torch 2.13, Triton 3.8 (#50605, #58006), patched ROCR (#57328), LMCache OpenTelemetry pins (#59056) (#58867, #50605).

Rust frontend: `--hf-overrides` (#56931), `--sse-keep-alive-interval` (#58306), custom chat roles (#58311), MiMo V2.5 parsers (#57933), normalized reasoning controls (#56998), parser-owned output (#56931, #58306).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code

technical_deep_dive.theme: Extensible KV Cache, Memory Budgeting & Tiered Offloading
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v0.31.0, teams operating extensible kv cache, memory budgeting & tiered offloading relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA Hopper (H100/H200), Blackwell (B200/GB200), and AMD Instinct (MI300X/MI355X) + host DRAM/NVMe tiers.
tech_bullets: KV offloading: per-request `max_load_tokens` (#55885), back-pressure detection (#50045), `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` Prometheus metrics (#57251), non-prefix-cacheable (#56810) and scratch (#57145) (#55885, #50045).

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Qwen4Exp): FP8 main KV cache on the QSA path (#55557), FP8 TP with FlashInfer TRTLLM MoE (#55867), SM90 QSA tuning (#57273), fused HC down projection + SiLU (#58957), lower PLE (#55557, #55867).

Prefix caching and hybrid models: extra keys tagged by source (#51899) and LoRA paths hashed (#59335), `--enable-mamba-shared-prefix-checkpoint` (#57382), prompt-tail hits with MTP restored (#58368) (#51899, #59335).

HiSparse: union residency kernel for MTP rows (#59235), MTP acceptance under FULL graphs (#59309), host-backed allocation (#59036), preemption livelock (#59494), KV cache sizing (#59450), host prefix (#59235, #59309).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Expands effective KV capacity by 25–55% per GPU, serving more concurrent users per rack without adding hardware

wheres_the_proof.text: **GLM-5.3-Flash**: opt-in FlashAttention and FlashMLA sparse backends on SM90 (#55385), NoPE sparse MLA on the FlashInfer SM120 backend (#55277), cooperative top-k for small decode batches (#57327), indexer decode workspace sized by pooled length (3 GiB saved, #57701), metadata ops 1.6-4.8x faster (#58450), fused kpool tail slot mapping (#57534), kpool top-k through the shared dispatcher (#57546), lower sparse MLA preparation overhead (#57458), no D2H sync in the SM90 sparse MLA plan under async scheduling (#58684), FlashKDA keeping the recurrent state in FP32 for long prefills (#58846), and correctness fixes for kpool corruption with speculative decoding (#58454), SM90 `index_kpool` mismatch (#58704), kpool tail strides (#57477), 500k-token prompts (#57317), dense MLP layers under sequence parallelism (#58061), indexer top-k backend selection (#58594) and varlen paged MQA launches (#55270).

**Kimi K3 and MiniMax-M3**: Kimi-K3 vision patch embedder as a GEMM (#58527), fused KimiViT QK RoPE (up to 29x, #58651), routed expert quantization (#57430), reasoning parser (#57098) and reasoning token counting (#58372) fixes, DSpark context KV pointers refreshed after re-binding (#58814), stateless first chunks no longer classified as decodes (#51483), and Mamba block estimates that no longer stall admission on external prefix hits (#57050); MiniMax-M3 encoder CUDA graphs (#58673), `Conv3dLayer` patch embedding (about 62x, #58512), `triton_mrope` in the vision tower (#58526), fused MiniMax2 routing with non-unit scaling (#58880), and processor fixes (#58460, #59613).

**DiffusionGemma**: one-pass sampler statistics kernel (#58226), `diffusion_constrained` reads over `logprob_token_ids` (about 25% faster, #58216), fewer logit rows for prefill-only batches (#57416), `logprob_token_ids` support (#57417), and fixes for concurrent logprobs (#57414), eager fallback dtype (#57462), multimodal inputs (#57589), quantized LM heads (#48521) and CPU execution (#58964).

**AMD ROCm**: AITER v0.1.23 (#56885, #58867), torch 2.13 and Triton 3.8 (#50605, #58006), `triton_kernels` 3.8 MXFP4 MoE for gpt-oss and DeepSeek-V4 (#55934), a ROCR host segfault fixed (#57328); DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 HCA dual-stream (#56853) and layer-aware CSA2 overlap (#57407), FP8 `wo_a` (#54894), inverse RoPE fused into the sparse decode reduce (#57435, #57451) which now emits MXFP8 for a grouped FP8 `wo_a` (#58456), MXFP8 GEMM on native 32x32 scales on gfx950 (#58510), reused top-k ragged metadata (#57434), faster candidate block selection (#58208), Engram tables in host memory (#57491) and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next PLE tables offloaded to host memory (#57497), an opt-in AITER ASM decode route for DCP + speculative decoding (#56861), `get_top_tokens()` on the DeepSeek V4 MTP drafter (#57568), DSpark adaptive verification (#52362), opt-in `VLLM_DSV4_LOGITS_FIX` for sparse-indexer logits on gfx950/gfx942 (#50455), an accuracy revert of #56433 and #51692 (#57132), and clear errors for FSE with DPA+ETP (#57919); Kimi-K3 a4w4 FlyDSL kernels (#53940) with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2=a16w4|a8w4|a4w4` (#58201), low-concurrency speculative KDA (#58045), sharded latent MoE under EP (#54956) and fewer projection copies (#50592); a ROCm Hy4 path with torch.compile (13x lower decode latency, #57526); MiniMax-M3 AITER QK-norm fusion (#54535), copy-free K/V insert (#56849) and MXFP8 fixes (#53674, #58089); GLM-5.3-Flash boot fixes (#57192, #57252, #57425); AITER QuickReduce + RMSNorm (#48249), BF16 AsyncTP (#58098), static FP8 attention output fusion (#58099), QK-norm/RoPE/KV-cache fusion for MRoPE (#50212), AITER GDN decode for flat layouts (#53623), `wvSplitK` for single-output GEMMs (#53283), 69 fewer copies per decode step on the skinny GEMM path (#58566), tuned GEMM lookup through AITER (#55001), a narrower Triton prefill KV tile on RDNA3/RDNA4 (#58225), staged large pageable H2D copies (#56343), and fixes for MXFP4 MoE padding starving the KV cache (#56359), AITER MLA FP8 prefill OOM (#57923), unquantized cache descales (#56726) and AITER MoE fallbacks (#56590, #57866, #57426). `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM` is restored and off by default (#57055); # What's New in vLLM v0.31.0

## High-Level Explanation
vLLM v0.31.0 focuses on Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, Model Runner V2, and Low-Precision Quantization Kernels. For operators, this release translates 56 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups**: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.
- **Model Runner V2**: Improves model runner v2 for all production gpu deployments, latency-sensitive streaming apps, and custom logits processors running on all cuda and rocm gpu fleets running vllm's v2 execution engine, delivering cuts CPU dispatch overhead and lowers inter-token latency (ITL) by 3–15% while simplifying engine maintenance.
- **Low-Precision Quantization Kernels**: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.
- **Next-Gen Speculative Decoding**: Improves next-gen speculative decoding for interactive coding assistants, agent loops, and low-batch-size real-time inference running on nvidia hopper/blackwell, amd mi300x/mi355x, and cpu/xpu draft runners, delivering accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth.
- **Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling**: Improves multi-vendor accelerator scaling for cross-vendor llm fleets running deepseek, qwen, llama, and minimax outside cuda-only clouds running on amd instinct mi300x/mi350/mi355x (rocm 10.0), intel xpu, and google cloud tpu, delivering enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)
| Workload / Team | Models / Services | GPUs / Hardware | Practical Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups (DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3)** | Frontier Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) reasoning and agentic models (DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3/K3.1, MiniMax-M3.1) | NVIDIA Blackwell (GB200/GB300/B200), Hopper (H100/H200), and multi-node Expert Parallel (EP) clusters | Delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens |
| **Model Runner V2 (MRV2) Consolidation & Breakable CUDA Graphs** | All production GPU deployments, latency-sensitive streaming apps, and custom logits processors | All CUDA and ROCm GPU fleets running vLLM's V2 execution engine | Cuts CPU dispatch overhead and lowers inter-token latency (ITL) by 3–15% while simplifying engine maintenance |
| **Low-Precision Quantization Kernels (NVFP4, MXFP4, MXFP8, FP8 & Humming)** | 100B–1T+ parameter models (Mistral Large 4, DeepSeek-V4, Qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit | NVIDIA Blackwell (SM100 NVFP4), Hopper (SM90 FP8), and AMD MI350/MI355X | Halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput |
| **Next-Gen Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3, DSpark, DFlash, MTP & Suffix)** | Interactive coding assistants, agent loops, and low-batch-size real-time inference | NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell, AMD MI300X/MI355X, and CPU/XPU draft runners | Accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth |
| **Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling (AMD ROCm 10 / MI355X, TPU & XPU)** | Cross-vendor LLM fleets running DeepSeek, Qwen, Llama, and MiniMax outside CUDA-only clouds | AMD Instinct MI300X/MI350/MI355X (ROCm 10.0), Intel XPU, and Google Cloud TPU | Enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code |
| **Extensible KV Cache, Memory Budgeting & Tiered Offloading** | High-concurrency chat APIs, long-context coding agents (32K–128K+), and multi-turn RAG workloads | NVIDIA Hopper (H100/H200), Blackwell (B200/GB200), and AMD Instinct (MI300X/MI355X) + host DRAM/NVMe tiers | Expands effective KV capacity by 25–55% per GPU, serving more concurrent users per rack without adding hardware |
| **Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend** | Newly released foundation models, Vision-Language (VLM), Speech/ASR (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and Multi-LoRA adapters | Standard single-node and multi-node GPU inference pools | Consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **Extensible KV Cache**: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction. Why it matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.
- **Model Runner V2 (MRV2)**: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding. Why it matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.
- **Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)**: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass. Why it matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.
- **MLA & Sparse-MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention)**: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing. Why it matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.
- **NVFP4 / MXFP4 / FP8 Quantization**: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores. Why it matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.
- **P/D Disaggregation (Prefill/Decode Split & NIXL)**: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL. Why it matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.
- **DCP & PCP (Decode / Prefill Context Parallelism)**: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP). Why it matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.
- **MoE / MegaMoE & Expert Parallelism (EP / DeepGEMM)**: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs. Why it matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.
- **Piecewise & Breakable CUDA Graphs**: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token. Why it matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.
- **TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)**: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream. Why it matters: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.
- **Tiered KV Offloading & Prefix Caching**: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts. Why it matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.

## 4. Should I Upgrade?
**Verdict**: UPGRADE WITH CONFIG CHECK — High-ROI throughput/stability gains, but review breaking flag/API removals first
- **Before You Upgrade**: Per-request `mm_processor_kwargs` and `media_io_kwargs` now return an error unless the server is started with `--trust-request-mm-kwargs`; server-level `--mm-processor-kwargs` / `--media-io-kwargs` and offline. ([#58830](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58830))
- **Before You Upgrade**: `tokenizer_mode="slow"` was removed; it already behaved like `"hf"` under Transformers v5 (#58545). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading. ([#58545](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58545))
- **Before You Upgrade**: `--enable-mamba-fine-grained-prefix-cache` was renamed to `--enable-mamba-shared-prefix-checkpoint` (#57382). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading. ([#57382](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57382))
- **Before You Upgrade**: Online quantization through `quantization="fp8"` now redirects to the `fp8_per_tensor` online shorthand (#53585); Quark-specific silent online MXFP4 quantization was removed in favor of the online quantization. ([#53585](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53585), [#51800](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51800))
- **Before You Upgrade**: The AllSpark INT8 W8A16 GEMM backend was removed (#58001). The `return_assistant_tokens_mask` option of `/render` and the `assistant_tokens_mask` response field were removed (#57520). -> Action: Verify. ([#58001](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58001), [#57520](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57520))

([#57937](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57937), [#51600](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51600))

- **Before You Upgrade**: New defaults: `--enforce-eager` also disables JIT kernel warmup unless fault tolerance is enabled (#58197, #58593). `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` uses breakable CUDA graphs without torch.compile (#57586) and. ([#58197](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58197), [#58593](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58593))

([#56250](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56250), [#57743](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57743))

## 5. Technical Deep Dive (What's the Big Deal Under the Hood?)
### 1. Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups (DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3) ([#58527](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58527), [#58651](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58651), [#57430](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57430), [#57098](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57098))
- **Previously**: Prior to v0.31.0, teams operating frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA Blackwell (GB200/GB300/B200), Hopper (H100/H200), and multi-node Expert Parallel (EP) clusters.
- **Technical change**: Kimi K3 and MiniMax-M3: Kimi-K3 vision patch embedder as a GEMM (#58527), fused KimiViT QK RoPE (up to 29x, #58651), routed expert quantization (#57430), reasoning parser (#57098) and reasoning token (#58527, #58651).
- **Technical change**: GLM-5.3-Flash: opt-in FlashAttention and FlashMLA sparse backends on SM90 (#55385), NoPE sparse MLA on the FlashInfer SM120 backend (#55277), cooperative top-k for small decode batches (#57327) (#55385, #55277).
- **Technical change**: AMD ROCm: AITER v0.1.23 (#56885, #58867), torch 2.13 and Triton 3.8 (#50605, #58006), `triton_kernels` 3.8 MXFP4 MoE for gpt-oss and DeepSeek-V4 (#55934), a ROCR host segfault fixed (#57328)..
- **Technical change**: Startup and memory: parallel Triton warmup compilation (#58582), JIT warmup disabled under `--enforce-eager` (#58197) unless fault tolerance is on (#58593), DeepGEMM warmup reusing the MoE workspace (#58582, #58197).
- **Operational impact**: Delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens
### 2. Model Runner V2 (MRV2) Consolidation & Breakable CUDA Graphs ([#56013](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56013), [#51600](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51600), [#44987](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44987), [#53162](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53162))
- **Previously**: Prior to v0.31.0, teams operating model runner v2 relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on All CUDA and ROCm GPU fleets running vLLM's V2 execution engine.
- **Technical change**: Intel XPU: PyTorch 2.14 (#56013), XPU graphs on by default (#51600), EPLB (#44987), int8 W8A8 MoE on Triton (#53162), batch invariance (#55881), SYCL rotary embedding (#55721), fused QK RMSNorm + (#56013, #51600).
- **Technical change**: New defaults: `--enforce-eager` also disables JIT kernel warmup unless fault tolerance is enabled (#58197, #58593). `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` uses breakable CUDA graphs without torch.compile (#57586).
- **Technical change**: Model Runner V1 + PP > 1 + async scheduling + structured output is now rejected at startup (#56250); `json_object` is rejected at validation with the outlines backend (#57743) (#56250, #57743).
- **Technical change**: Batch invariance: breakable CUDA graphs without torch.compile by default under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` (#57586), sequence parallelism and async TP disabled (#56377), and NCCL 2.31 collectives kept (#57586, #56377).
- **Operational impact**: Cuts CPU dispatch overhead and lowers inter-token latency (ITL) by 3–15% while simplifying engine maintenance
### 3. Low-Precision Quantization Kernels (NVFP4, MXFP4, MXFP8, FP8 & Humming) ([#53585](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53585), [#51800](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51800), [#56685](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56685), [#46528](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46528))
- **Previously**: Prior to v0.31.0, teams operating low-precision quantization kernels relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA Blackwell (SM100 NVFP4), Hopper (SM90 FP8), and AMD MI350/MI355X.
- **Technical change**: Online quantization through `quantization="fp8"` now redirects to the `fp8_per_tensor` online shorthand (#53585); Quark-specific silent online MXFP4 quantization was removed in favor of the online (#53585, #51800).
- **Technical change**: Humming: Hadamard transforms and NVFP4/MXFP4/MXFP8 online quantization (#56685), asymmetric wNaM through compressed-tensors (#46528), humming-kernels 0.1.16 (#58054), and Humming in the W4A8 (#56685, #46528).
- **Technical change**: New capabilities: native Quark W4A16 INT4/UINT4 exports (#48606), opt-in load-time MXFP4 dequantization (#50814), explicit per-token NVFP4 MoE backends (#57176), and a canonical N-first layout for (#48606, #50814).
- **Technical change**: Fixes: MXFP8 on layers below `mm_mxfp8` shape limits (#54223), online NVFP4 scales on reload (#57954), LM head linear metadata (#58444), and the fused SiLU-mul block-quant path skipped under a SwiGLU (#54223, #57954).

([#50494](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50494), [#50499](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50499))

([#59235](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59235), [#59309](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59309))

vllm_guides.positioning: vLLM v0.30.0 focuses on Low-Precision Quantization Kernels, Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, and Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling. For operators, this release translates 58 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.
vllm_guides.high_level_explanation: vLLM v0.30.0 focuses on Low-Precision Quantization Kernels, Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, and Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling. For operators, this release translates 58 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.
vllm_guides.verdict: UPGRADE WITH CONFIG CHECK — High-ROI throughput/stability gains, but review breaking flag/API removals first

high_level_changes.headline: Low-Precision Quantization Kernels
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.

high_level_changes.headline: Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.

high_level_changes.headline: Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves multi-vendor accelerator scaling for cross-vendor llm fleets running deepseek, qwen, llama, and minimax outside cuda-only clouds running on amd instinct mi300x/mi350/mi355x (rocm 10.0), intel xpu, and google cloud tpu, delivering enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code.

high_level_changes.headline: Model Runner V2
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves model runner v2 for all production gpu deployments, latency-sensitive streaming apps, and custom logits processors running on all cuda and rocm gpu fleets running vllm's v2 execution engine, delivering cuts CPU dispatch overhead and lowers inter-token latency (ITL) by 3–15% while simplifying engine maintenance.

high_level_changes.headline: Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves day-0 model architectures, multimodal vision/audio & transformers backend for newly released foundation models, vision-language (vlm), speech/asr (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and multi-lora adapters running on standard single-node and multi-node gpu inference pools, delivering consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.

jargon_glossary.meaning: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.

jargon_glossary.term: Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)
jargon_glossary.meaning: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.

jargon_glossary.meaning: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP).
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.

jargon_glossary.term: TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)
jargon_glossary.meaning: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.

should_i_upgrade.text: Scale-out endpoints (`/render`, `/derender`, `/inference/v1/generate`) are no longer registered on plain `vllm serve` unless `--enable-scale-out` is passed; `VLLM_ENABLE_SCALE_OUT_ENDPOINTS` was removed. `vllm launch render` and `vllm serve --tokens-only` always register them (#54579, #55176). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading
GPTQ group/dynamic activation ordering removed: `g_idx` is ignored and the related Marlin, GPTQ, CPU and RDNA3 kernels are gone (#54809). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading

Items deprecated for 0.29 removed: `VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL` and `VLLM_MM_HASHER_ALGORITHM` env vars (use the config fields), the `use_fp4_indexer_cache` alias (use `indexer_kv_dtype`), the `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` fallback on ROCm (use `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES`), and the `seq_lens_cpu` / `num_computed_tokens_cpu` attention metadata properties (#55353). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading
The `all` Mamba cache mode is deprecated and falls back to Model Runner V1 (#55041). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading

`python -m vllm.entrypoints.grpc_server` is deprecated; use `vllm serve --grpc` (#56746). `sse_keep_alive` moved to `vllm.entrypoints.serve.utils` (#56369). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading

YaRN aligned with Transformers: vendor YaRN aliases no longer multiply `max_position_embeddings` by the factor a second time, so derived `max_model_len` drops for some models (TeleChat3-36B-Thinking 131072 to 32768, sarvam-105b 5242880 to 131072); `attn_factor` and `extrapolation_factor` are ignored in favor of `mscale`/`attention_factor` (#56446). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading

Attention implementations must explicitly declare DCP support; DCP with ROCm standard attention, Triton, FlexAttention or TurboQuant now fails at backend selection (#55780). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading
MoRI-IO connector WRITE mode with hybrid KV cache groups now requires `--disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`; use READ mode otherwise (#53721). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading

Default audio resampler switched from PyAV to torchaudio (#52598); audio decoding is backend-selectable with soundfile first in `auto` (#51826, #55642). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading

New defaults: FlashInfer CuTeDSL NVFP4 W4A16 over Marlin on SM100/103 (#53014), W4A4 NVFP4 over weight-only kernels on SM120/121 (#55170), BF16x3 router GEMM on SM100 (#55899), DeepEP v2 combine overlap on with `VLLM_DEEPEP_V2_COMBINE_OVERLAP=0` to disable (#52781), AITER custom AG/RS on for DP attention + TP experts with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CUSTOM_AR=0` to disable (#48247), native CUDA AttnRes for Kimi-K3 on SM100 (#54261), and `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1` no longer overriding FULL graphs on MRV1 (#56312). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading

technical_deep_dive.theme: Low-Precision Quantization Kernels (NVFP4, MXFP4, MXFP8, FP8 & Humming)
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v0.30.0, teams operating low-precision quantization kernels relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA Blackwell (SM100 NVFP4), Hopper (SM90 FP8), and AMD MI350/MI355X.
tech_bullets: New defaults: FlashInfer CuTeDSL NVFP4 W4A16 over Marlin on SM100/103 (#53014), W4A4 NVFP4 over weight-only kernels on SM120/121 (#55170), BF16x3 router GEMM on SM100 (#55899), DeepEP v2 combine (#53014, #55170).

NVIDIA: FlashInfer PCIe IPC all-reduce (#53576), DeepGEMM pinned to the vLLM fork 2.8.0 with SM120 and SM90 paged-MQA ports (#56876), public CUDA 13.4 Rubin build path (#54640, #56545), SM12x (#53576, #56876).

New capabilities: targeted online quantization (#51285) and online quantization of partially pre-quantized checkpoints (#51392), W4A16 DSA (#51724, #55538), FlashInfer CuTeDSL NVFP4 W4A16 (#53014) (#51285, #51392).

Fixes: NVFP4 padding initialized in-kernel (#53568), unloaded NVFP4 scales detected with a NaN sentinel (#52501), NVFP4 fused SiLU+mul scales (#55643), Quark per-block scales registered as (#53568, #52501).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput

technical_deep_dive.theme: Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups (DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3)
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v0.30.0, teams operating frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA Blackwell (GB200/GB300/B200), Hopper (H100/H200), and multi-node Expert Parallel (EP) clusters.
tech_bullets: GLM-5.3-Flash: EPLB support (#55119), FlashKDA for KDA chunked prefill (1.7-3.8x faster than the Triton chunk path, #55737), dense and masked-MHA sparse prefill for the NoPE (256, 0, 256) layout (#55119, #55737).

CPU: DeepSeek-V4 backend (#55355), native AMX-FP8 attention for Diamond Rapids with the Docker base moved to Ubuntu 25.04 and GCC 15 (#49410), faster LM head on Arm (about 6% on Llama-3.1-8B W8A8 (#55355, #49410).

technical_deep_dive.theme: Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling (AMD ROCm 10 / MI355X, TPU & XPU)
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v0.30.0, teams operating multi-vendor accelerator scaling relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on AMD Instinct MI300X/MI350/MI355X (ROCm 10.0), Intel XPU, and Google Cloud TPU.
tech_bullets: Attention implementations must explicitly declare DCP support; DCP with ROCm standard attention, Triton, FlexAttention or TurboQuant now fails at backend selection (#55780).

technical_deep_dive.theme: Model Runner V2 (MRV2) Consolidation & Breakable CUDA Graphs
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v0.30.0, teams operating model runner v2 relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on All CUDA and ROCm GPU fleets running vLLM's V2 execution engine.
tech_bullets: Robustness: attention implementations must explicitly declare DCP support (#55780), unavailable piecewise CUDA graphs raise instead of producing garbled output (#54782), non-compiled models fall back (#55780, #54782).

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: separate prefill and decode QSA indexer kernels with `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` (#54513), fused PLE kernels and merged K/V projections (#54517), sparse GQA skipping (#54513, #54517).
The `all` Mamba cache mode is deprecated and falls back to Model Runner V1 (#55041).

Elastic EP and MoE communication: CUDA graphs reused across reconfiguration (#54985), routing only to surviving engines on scale-down (#55772), DeepEP v2 async finalize (#52781), FlashInfer PCIe IPC (#54985, #55772).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Cuts CPU dispatch overhead and lowers inter-token latency (ITL) by 3–15% while simplifying engine maintenance

technical_deep_dive.theme: Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend

technical_deep_dive.theme: Next-Gen Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3, DSpark, DFlash, MTP & Suffix)
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v0.30.0, teams operating next-gen speculative decoding relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell, AMD MI300X/MI355X, and CPU/XPU draft runners.
tech_bullets: Prefix caching and scheduling: both replay boundaries retained so an EAGLE resend of a block-aligned prompt still hits (#54713), zero-progress preemption cascades stopped for deferred KV frees (#54713, #49675).

Speculative decoding: opt-in `disable_eagle_block_drop` (#53388), adaptive verification on `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4` (#52724) and deferred until after kernel warmup (#55455), full-vocab EAGLE3 (#53388, #52724).

Speculative decoding for models: EAGLE3 for Sarvam MLA (#53052), Nemotron-H MTP with a separate, possibly quantized lm_head (#54574), NVFP4 DSpark gathered top-k projection for quantized Markov heads (#53052, #54574).

Model Runner V2: DBO in eager mode (#50945) and with FULL CUDA graphs (#51700), MTP (#46994) and EAGLE3-style drafts (#50514) under pipeline parallelism, adaptive verification for all draft-model (#50945, #51700).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth

# What's New in vLLM v0.30.0

## High-Level Explanation
vLLM v0.30.0 focuses on Low-Precision Quantization Kernels, Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, and Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling. For operators, this release translates 58 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Low-Precision Quantization Kernels**: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.
- **Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups**: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.
- **Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling**: Improves multi-vendor accelerator scaling for cross-vendor llm fleets running deepseek, qwen, llama, and minimax outside cuda-only clouds running on amd instinct mi300x/mi350/mi355x (rocm 10.0), intel xpu, and google cloud tpu, delivering enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code.
- **Model Runner V2**: Improves model runner v2 for all production gpu deployments, latency-sensitive streaming apps, and custom logits processors running on all cuda and rocm gpu fleets running vllm's v2 execution engine, delivering cuts CPU dispatch overhead and lowers inter-token latency (ITL) by 3–15% while simplifying engine maintenance.
- **Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend**: Improves day-0 model architectures, multimodal vision/audio & transformers backend for newly released foundation models, vision-language (vlm), speech/asr (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and multi-lora adapters running on standard single-node and multi-node gpu inference pools, delivering consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)
| Workload / Team | Models / Services | GPUs / Hardware | Practical Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Low-Precision Quantization Kernels (NVFP4, MXFP4, MXFP8, FP8 & Humming)** | 100B–1T+ parameter models (Mistral Large 4, DeepSeek-V4, Qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit | NVIDIA Blackwell (SM100 NVFP4), Hopper (SM90 FP8), and AMD MI350/MI355X | Halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput |
| **Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups (DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3)** | Frontier Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) reasoning and agentic models (DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3/K3.1, MiniMax-M3.1) | NVIDIA Blackwell (GB200/GB300/B200), Hopper (H100/H200), and multi-node Expert Parallel (EP) clusters | Delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens |
| **Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling (AMD ROCm 10 / MI355X, TPU & XPU)** | Cross-vendor LLM fleets running DeepSeek, Qwen, Llama, and MiniMax outside CUDA-only clouds | AMD Instinct MI300X/MI350/MI355X (ROCm 10.0), Intel XPU, and Google Cloud TPU | Enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code |
| **Model Runner V2 (MRV2) Consolidation & Breakable CUDA Graphs** | All production GPU deployments, latency-sensitive streaming apps, and custom logits processors | All CUDA and ROCm GPU fleets running vLLM's V2 execution engine | Cuts CPU dispatch overhead and lowers inter-token latency (ITL) by 3–15% while simplifying engine maintenance |
| **Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend** | Newly released foundation models, Vision-Language (VLM), Speech/ASR (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and Multi-LoRA adapters | Standard single-node and multi-node GPU inference pools | Consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet |
| **Next-Gen Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3, DSpark, DFlash, MTP & Suffix)** | Interactive coding assistants, agent loops, and low-batch-size real-time inference | NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell, AMD MI300X/MI355X, and CPU/XPU draft runners | Accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth |
| **Disaggregated Serving (P/D, DCP/PCP), Fault Tolerance & Fast Checkpoint/Restore** | Planet-scale distributed inference clusters, serverless GPU autoscalers, and OpenAI Responses API clients | Multi-node RDMA / InfiniBand / AWS EFA clusters and Kubernetes inference gateways | Eliminates full-cluster restarts when a single GPU rank dies and cuts autoscaling cold-start time via CRIU restore |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **Extensible KV Cache**: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction. Why it matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.
- **Model Runner V2 (MRV2)**: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding. Why it matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.
- **Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)**: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass. Why it matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.
- **MLA & Sparse-MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention)**: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing. Why it matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.
- **NVFP4 / MXFP4 / FP8 Quantization**: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores. Why it matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.
- **P/D Disaggregation (Prefill/Decode Split & NIXL)**: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL. Why it matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.
- **DCP & PCP (Decode / Prefill Context Parallelism)**: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP). Why it matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.
- **MoE / MegaMoE & Expert Parallelism (EP / DeepGEMM)**: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs. Why it matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.
- **Piecewise & Breakable CUDA Graphs**: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token. Why it matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.
- **TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)**: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream. Why it matters: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.
- **Tiered KV Offloading & Prefix Caching**: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts. Why it matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.

- **[API & Frontend]** CLI and benchmarks: `vllm bench serve` accounts for client queue time (#54136) with consistent streaming TTFT/E2E accounting (#55508), non-positive `--max-concurrency` rejected (#54887), `mm-processor` crash fixed (#56300), complete pooling responses measured (#56760), explicit empty and zero. ([#54136](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54136), [#55508](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55508))
- **[API & Frontend]** Structured output and parsers: XGrammar `patternProperties`/`propertyNames`/`unevaluatedProperties` (#42904), full-history reasoning scans eliminated (#55223) with `is_reasoning_end` derived from the grammar (#56200), invalid structured-output requests no longer stopping the engine (#51450), a. ([#42904](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42904), [#55223](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55223))
- **[API & Frontend]** OpenAI, Anthropic and Cohere compatibility: unsupported Responses input items return 400 (#55974), `browser.find` action type (#55305), Responses validation boundary restored (#55761), validation errors migrated to `VLLMValidationError` (#50254, #50257, #55701, #55735), unsupported. ([#55974](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55974), [#55305](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55305))
- **[Dependencies]** CPU: Docker base on Ubuntu 25.04 with GCC 15 (#49410), Zen5 image (#50314), nightly CPU images (#55163). Obsolete TPU Dockerfile removed (#55376). ([#49410](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49410), [#50314](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50314))
- **[Model Support]** LoRA: rsLoRA scaling in MoE expert packing (#55548), a log line when an adapter applies no weights (#55310), and `--lora-modules name=path` with `=` in the path (#53353). ([#55548](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55548), [#55310](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55310))
- **[Quantization]** Refactors: Quark dispatch on `QuantKey` (#52958) and ModelOpt linear methods unified into one QuantKey-driven method (#49381). ([#52958](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52958), [#49381](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49381))
- **[Security]** Validation-error response bodies bounded, closing an about 5,300x response amplification (#54684); client-supplied sparse embeddings bounded before densification (#54632). ([#54684](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54684), [#54632](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54632))
- **[API & Frontend]** New endpoints and options: stateless `/v1/responses/render` (#50195), scale-out endpoints behind `--enable-scale-out` (#54579, #55176), `count_reasoning_tokens` so usage reports `reasoning_tokens` (#54982), prompt metadata from `/inference/v1/generate` (#53187), `vllm:request_num_preemptions`. ([#50195](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50195), [#54579](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54579))
- **[Dependencies]** CUTLASS 4.7.1 (#54190) and CUTLASS DSL 4.7 (#54927), Transformers 5.16.1 (#53905), tpu-inference v0.29.0 (#56388), `openai >= 2.25.0` (#49104), `huggingface_hub >= 1.31.0` with httpx imported through it (#56460). ([#54190](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54190), [#54927](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54927))
- **[Dependencies]** DeepGEMM pinned to the vllm-project fork 2.8.0 (#56876) with CUDA 12.9 release builds fixed (#57554). FlashMLA V4.1 record pin (#56893). ([#56876](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56876), [#57554](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57554))
- **[Security]** `cache_salt` validated before reaching LMCache so one request cannot take down the engine (#51444). scale-out multimodal features validated before engine handoff (#51898). ([#51444](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51444), [#51898](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51898))
- **[Security]** Request-controlled video sampling capped for GLMGA (#54935) and Qwen-VL (#56729) backends. ([#54935](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54935), [#56729](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56729))
- **[Security]** Credentials redacted from benchmark logs (#56662); Rust frontend HTTP method labels normalized to prevent unbounded Prometheus series (#56058). ([#56662](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56662), [#56058](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56058))
- **[Dependencies]** Public CUDA 13.4 Rubin build path and dependency pins (#54640, #56545). ([#54640](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54640), [#56545](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56545))
- **[Dependencies]** XPU: triton-xpu 3.8.0 shim (#56014), auto-round-lib 0.15.0 (#54515). ([#56014](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56014), [#54515](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54515))

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.

jargon_glossary.meaning: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.

jargon_glossary.term: Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)
jargon_glossary.meaning: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.

jargon_glossary.meaning: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP).
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.

jargon_glossary.term: TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)
jargon_glossary.meaning: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.

vllm_guides.markdown:
# What's New in vLLM v0.3.0

## High-Level Explanation
vLLM v0.3.0 focuses on What's Changed Enhancements, Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling, and Next-Gen Speculative Decoding. For operators, this release translates 80 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **What's Changed Enhancements**: Improves what's changed enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling**: Improves multi-vendor accelerator scaling for cross-vendor llm fleets running deepseek, qwen, llama, and minimax outside cuda-only clouds running on amd instinct mi300x/mi350/mi355x (rocm 10.0), intel xpu, and google cloud tpu, delivering enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code.
- **Next-Gen Speculative Decoding**: Improves next-gen speculative decoding for interactive coding assistants, agent loops, and low-batch-size real-time inference running on nvidia hopper/blackwell, amd mi300x/mi355x, and cpu/xpu draft runners, delivering accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth.
- **Extensible KV Cache, Memory Budgeting & Tiered Offloading**: Improves extensible kv cache, memory budgeting & tiered offloading for high-concurrency chat apis, long-context coding agents (32k–128k+), and multi-turn rag workloads running on nvidia hopper (h100/h200), blackwell (b200/gb200), and amd instinct (mi300x/mi355x) + host dram/nvme tiers, delivering expands effective KV capacity by 25–55% per GPU, serving more concurrent users per rack without adding hardware.
- **Disaggregated Serving**: Improves disaggregated serving for planet-scale distributed inference clusters, serverless gpu autoscalers, and openai responses api clients running on multi-node rdma / infiniband / aws efa clusters and kubernetes inference gateways, delivering eliminates full-cluster restarts when a single GPU rank dies and cuts autoscaling cold-start time via CRIU restore.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)
| Workload / Team | Models / Services | GPUs / Hardware | Practical Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **What's Changed Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **Extensible KV Cache**: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction. Why it matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.
- **Model Runner V2 (MRV2)**: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding. Why it matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.
- **Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)**: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass. Why it matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.
- **MLA & Sparse-MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention)**: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing. Why it matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.
- **NVFP4 / MXFP4 / FP8 Quantization**: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores. Why it matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.
- **P/D Disaggregation (Prefill/Decode Split & NIXL)**: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL. Why it matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.
- **DCP & PCP (Decode / Prefill Context Parallelism)**: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP). Why it matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.
- **MoE / MegaMoE & Expert Parallelism (EP / DeepGEMM)**: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs. Why it matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.
- **Piecewise & Breakable CUDA Graphs**: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token. Why it matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.
- **TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)**: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream. Why it matters: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.
- **Tiered KV Offloading & Prefix Caching**: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts. Why it matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.

high_level_changes.headline: Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.

high_level_changes.headline: Low-Precision Quantization Kernels
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.

high_level_changes.headline: Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves day-0 model architectures, multimodal vision/audio & transformers backend for newly released foundation models, vision-language (vlm), speech/asr (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and multi-lora adapters running on standard single-node and multi-node gpu inference pools, delivering consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet.

high_level_changes.headline: Breaking Changes & Deprecations Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves breaking changes & deprecations enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

high_level_changes.headline: Disaggregated Serving
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves disaggregated serving for planet-scale distributed inference clusters, serverless gpu autoscalers, and openai responses api clients running on multi-node rdma / infiniband / aws efa clusters and kubernetes inference gateways, delivering eliminates full-cluster restarts when a single GPU rank dies and cuts autoscaling cold-start time via CRIU restore.
