jargon_glossary.meaning: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.

jargon_glossary.meaning: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.

jargon_glossary.term: Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)
jargon_glossary.meaning: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.

jargon_glossary.meaning: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP).
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.

jargon_glossary.term: TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)
jargon_glossary.meaning: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.

technical_deep_dive.theme: Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups (DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3)
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v0.29.0, teams operating frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA Blackwell (GB200/GB300/B200), Hopper (H100/H200), and multi-node Expert Parallel (EP) clusters.
tech_bullets: Kernels: fused embedding kernel (#53677), FA4 re-enabled for head_size=256 on Blackwell (#52980), vectorized sparse MLA mask loads (#52217), masked MHA prefill for GLM-5 head dimensions (#53785) (#53677, #52980).

RL workflows: `sharded_rdt` P2P weight sync (#43375), rank-local IPC updates (#52497), sparse checkpoint updates (#50723, #53751), gpt-oss routed expert loading (#52209), stable DeepSeek V4 mHC (#43375, #52497).

AMD ROCm: dual-stream decode with hipgraphs (#52033), W4A4 preshuffled asm GEMM by default (+15% throughput on Llama-3.3-70B MXFP4, #53141), ROCr/CLR update fixing graph replay segfaults with up to (#52033, #53141).

Correctness: PaliGemma stale image scaling removed (#52692), Mistral3 placeholder grid with processor size overrides (#52874), MiniCPM-o on Transformers v5 (#54501), JinaVL cache order (#53553) (#52692, #52874).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens

wheres_the_proof.text: **Determinism**: `trace_decode_token_ids` for deterministic decode replay (#46701), per-arch tuned batch-invariant matmul configs (about 3x decode kernels on RTX 4090D/H20, #53247), Blackwell autotuning with 33.6% E2E latency reduction (#53649), deterministic MoE combine under DP+EP (#45683), and `fuse_allreduce_rms` disabled under batch invariance (#51292).

# What's New in vLLM v0.29.0

## High-Level Explanation
vLLM v0.29.0 focuses on Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, Low-Precision Quantization Kernels, and Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend. For operators, this release translates 50 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups**: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.
- **Low-Precision Quantization Kernels**: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.
- **Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend**: Improves day-0 model architectures, multimodal vision/audio & transformers backend for newly released foundation models, vision-language (vlm), speech/asr (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and multi-lora adapters running on standard single-node and multi-node gpu inference pools, delivering consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet.
- **Breaking Changes & Deprecations Enhancements**: Improves breaking changes & deprecations enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **Disaggregated Serving**: Improves disaggregated serving for planet-scale distributed inference clusters, serverless gpu autoscalers, and openai responses api clients running on multi-node rdma / infiniband / aws efa clusters and kubernetes inference gateways, delivering eliminates full-cluster restarts when a single GPU rank dies and cuts autoscaling cold-start time via CRIU restore.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)
| Workload / Team | Models / Services | GPUs / Hardware | Practical Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups (DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3)** | Frontier Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) reasoning and agentic models (DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3/K3.1, MiniMax-M3.1) | NVIDIA Blackwell (GB200/GB300/B200), Hopper (H100/H200), and multi-node Expert Parallel (EP) clusters | Delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens |
| **Low-Precision Quantization Kernels (NVFP4, MXFP4, MXFP8, FP8 & Humming)** | 100B–1T+ parameter models (Mistral Large 4, DeepSeek-V4, Qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit | NVIDIA Blackwell (SM100 NVFP4), Hopper (SM90 FP8), and AMD MI350/MI355X | Halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput |
| **Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend** | Newly released foundation models, Vision-Language (VLM), Speech/ASR (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and Multi-LoRA adapters | Standard single-node and multi-node GPU inference pools | Consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet |
| **Breaking Changes & Deprecations Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **Disaggregated Serving (P/D, DCP/PCP), Fault Tolerance & Fast Checkpoint/Restore** | Planet-scale distributed inference clusters, serverless GPU autoscalers, and OpenAI Responses API clients | Multi-node RDMA / InfiniBand / AWS EFA clusters and Kubernetes inference gateways | Eliminates full-cluster restarts when a single GPU rank dies and cuts autoscaling cold-start time via CRIU restore |
| **Model Runner V2 (MRV2) Consolidation & Breakable CUDA Graphs** | All production GPU deployments, latency-sensitive streaming apps, and custom logits processors | All CUDA and ROCm GPU fleets running vLLM's V2 execution engine | Cuts CPU dispatch overhead and lowers inter-token latency (ITL) by 3–15% while simplifying engine maintenance |
| **Extensible KV Cache, Memory Budgeting & Tiered Offloading** | High-concurrency chat APIs, long-context coding agents (32K–128K+), and multi-turn RAG workloads | NVIDIA Hopper (H100/H200), Blackwell (B200/GB200), and AMD Instinct (MI300X/MI355X) + host DRAM/NVMe tiers | Expands effective KV capacity by 25–55% per GPU, serving more concurrent users per rack without adding hardware |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **Extensible KV Cache**: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction. Why it matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.
- **Model Runner V2 (MRV2)**: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding. Why it matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.
- **Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)**: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass. Why it matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.
- **MLA & Sparse-MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention)**: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing. Why it matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.
- **NVFP4 / MXFP4 / FP8 Quantization**: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores. Why it matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.
- **P/D Disaggregation (Prefill/Decode Split & NIXL)**: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL. Why it matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.
- **DCP & PCP (Decode / Prefill Context Parallelism)**: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP). Why it matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.
- **MoE / MegaMoE & Expert Parallelism (EP / DeepGEMM)**: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs. Why it matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.
- **Piecewise & Breakable CUDA Graphs**: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token. Why it matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.
- **TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)**: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream. Why it matters: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.
- **Tiered KV Offloading & Prefix Caching**: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts. Why it matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.

## 4. Should I Upgrade?
**Verdict**: UPGRADE WITH CONFIG CHECK — High-ROI throughput/stability gains, but review breaking flag/API removals first
- **Before You Upgrade**: Ten deprecated architectures removed: Arctic, Chameleon, Cheers, Fairseq2Llama, FireRedLID, GritLM, HCXVision, MPT, the `RWForCausalLM` and `StableLMEpochForCausalLM` aliases, and `PrithviGeoSpatialMAE`. ([#53608](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53608))
- **Before You Upgrade**: FlexOlmo, Olmo3, Hunyuan V1 and Hunyuan VL are now served through the Transformers modeling backend (#53615). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading. ([#53615](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53615))
- **Before You Upgrade**: PyAV video decoder backend removed; use OpenCV or Torchcodec (#54231). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading. ([#54231](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54231))
- **Before You Upgrade**: `python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server` is deprecated; use `vllm serve` (#52131). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading. ([#52131](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52131))
- **Before You Upgrade**: Model Runner V2 is the default runner for all models (#53183). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading. ([#53183](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53183))
- **Before You Upgrade**: `prefix_cache_retention_interval` default changed from dense to 0 for SWA/SSM models; the env var is deprecated in favor of the argument (#52216). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading. ([#52216](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52216))
- **Before You Upgrade**: FlashInfer all-reduce enabled by default (#52998). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading. ([#52998](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52998))
- **Before You Upgrade**: `VLLM_TEST_FORCE_FP8_MARLIN` removed in favor of `--linear-backend` / `--moe-backend` (#52182). `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM` removed (#53141). ([#52182](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52182), [#53141](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53141))
- **Security**: `api_key` and `hf_token` redacted from startup logs, compile cache factors, and the Rust frontend launch log (#52523, #53625, #53738). ([#52523](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52523), [#53625](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53625))
- **Security**: Oversized media rejected before full download (#51896); `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_CLIP_FILESIZE_MB` enforced on all audio paths (#53561). ([#51896](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51896), [#53561](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53561))

## 5. Technical Deep Dive (What's the Big Deal Under the Hood?)

- **[Model Support]** Transformers modeling backend: FlexOlmo, Olmo3 and Hunyuan V1/VL migrated off native implementations (#53615), multimodal path hardened (#51827), and `RMSNormFuser.fuse` performance fixed (#52766). ([#53615](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53615), [#51827](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51827))
- **[Large Scale Serving]** Elastic EP: reduced eager-mode reconfiguration downtime (#51885), AOT cache reuse preserved during scaling (#53378), and scale-below-minimum rejected (#52702). ([#51885](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51885), [#53378](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53378))
- **[Dependencies]** InstantTensor added to CUDA dependencies; the loader is not enabled by default (#52801). CuPy constraint relaxed to exclude only 14.1.0 (#44284). ([#52801](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52801), [#44284](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44284))
- **[API & Frontend]** New endpoints & options: `/v1/messages/render` for the Anthropic Messages API (#45803), `/cohere/v2/chat/render` (#53219), SSE keep-alive comments for idle streams (#51034), per-request spec decode metrics (#48915), video embeds input (#54242), `--max-num-queued-reqs` / `--max-num-queued-tokens`. ([#45803](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45803), [#53219](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53219))
- **[API & Frontend]** Anthropic & Cohere: `vllm_xargs` forwarded to sampling params (#53308), `stop_sequence` stop reason reported (#45807), Cohere citation/tool 500s fixed (#52175), and stop string limit applied (#53750). ([#53308](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53308), [#45807](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45807))
- **[Security]** `api_key` and `hf_token` redacted from startup logs, compile cache factors, and the Rust frontend launch log (#52523, #53625, #53738). ([#52523](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52523), [#53625](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53625))
- **[Security]** Oversized media rejected before full download (#51896); `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_CLIP_FILESIZE_MB` enforced on all audio paths (#53561). ([#51896](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51896), [#53561](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53561))
- **[Security]** Decoder prompt-length validation enforced for processors that skip the check (#46588); PyNvVideoCodec decoder slot limit bypass fixed (#52126). ([#46588](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46588), [#52126](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52126))
- **[Dependencies]** XPU: vllm_xpu_kernels 0.1.14.1 (#54203), UCX install updated (#53817). ([#54203](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54203), [#53817](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53817))
- **[Security]** `cache_salt` length bounded to 1024 to prevent scheduler CPU exhaustion (#54353). ([#54353](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54353))

vllm_guides.positioning: vLLM v0.28.0 focuses on Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, Next-Gen Speculative Decoding, and Low-Precision Quantization Kernels. For operators, this release translates 48 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

high_level_changes.headline: Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.

high_level_changes.headline: Next-Gen Speculative Decoding
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves next-gen speculative decoding for interactive coding assistants, agent loops, and low-batch-size real-time inference running on nvidia hopper/blackwell, amd mi300x/mi355x, and cpu/xpu draft runners, delivering accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth.

high_level_changes.headline: Low-Precision Quantization Kernels
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.

high_level_changes.headline: Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves day-0 model architectures, multimodal vision/audio & transformers backend for newly released foundation models, vision-language (vlm), speech/asr (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and multi-lora adapters running on standard single-node and multi-node gpu inference pools, delivering consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet.

high_level_changes.headline: Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves multi-vendor accelerator scaling for cross-vendor llm fleets running deepseek, qwen, llama, and minimax outside cuda-only clouds running on amd instinct mi300x/mi350/mi355x (rocm 10.0), intel xpu, and google cloud tpu, delivering enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.

jargon_glossary.meaning: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.

jargon_glossary.term: Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)
jargon_glossary.meaning: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.

jargon_glossary.meaning: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.

technical_deep_dive.theme: Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups (DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3)
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v0.28.0, teams operating frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA Blackwell (GB200/GB300/B200), Hopper (H100/H200), and multi-node Expert Parallel (EP) clusters.
tech_bullets: AMD ROCm: torch 2.12 / triton 3.7 stack bump (#50607), AITER and FP8 inference enabled on GFX120x (#43615), DeepSeek-V4 on gfx11 (#47017), optimized Triton sparse-MLA decode on gfx950 (#52212) (#50607, #43615).

CPU: an MLA backend so DeepSeek-V2/V3 can run on CPU (#49453), a triton-cpu wheel (#52092), GPTQ and AWQ enabled on s390x (#51148) along with tcmalloc (#50841), BF16 MoE routed through zentorch on (#49453, #52092).
DeepGEMM pinned to the deepseek-ai nv_dev tip (#52035), DeepEP pinned by full commit hash (#52028), FlashAttention 3 built with the torch stable API (#49599) (#52035, #52028).
MoE: extended EPLB support for Mistral Large 3 and additional MoE backends (#48355), CuTe DSL skinny GEMM extended to GLM-5.2 (#49791) (#48355, #49791).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens

technical_deep_dive.theme: Next-Gen Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3, DSpark, DFlash, MTP & Suffix)
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v0.28.0, teams operating next-gen speculative decoding relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell, AMD MI300X/MI355X, and CPU/XPU draft runners.
tech_bullets: NVIDIA: FlashInfer XQA decode support on SM12x (#49718), a CuTeDSL fused query kernel on SM100 (#49792), programmatic dependent launch for the DSA decode kernels (#50230), the native DSA decode path (#49718, #49792).

Qwen: Qwen3.8 enabled on AMD ROCm (#50068), fused CUDA post-conv MTP decode kernel for Qwen3.5 GDN (#51674), GDN gates aligned with speculative tokens (#51812), and Qwen3.5 fixes for text-only (#50068, #51674).

Speculative decoding: DSpark confidence-scheduled verification (#47808), top-k DSpark Markov projection (#49969), DFlash2 with local convolution and a candidate selector (#52816), async scheduling (#47808, #49969).
Speculative decoding coverage: EAGLE3 support declared on KimiLinear (#52171), Qwen3.6 dSpark acceptance coverage (#51310) (#52171, #51310).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth

technical_deep_dive.theme: Low-Precision Quantization Kernels (NVFP4, MXFP4, MXFP8, FP8 & Humming)
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v0.28.0, teams operating low-precision quantization kernels relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA Blackwell (SM100 NVFP4), Hopper (SM90 FP8), and AMD MI350/MI355X.
tech_bullets: Fixes: dynamic INT8 W8A8 MoE config no longer built as W8A16 (#50833) and a TritonExperts crash (#51411), MXFP4 conversion for FlashInfer CUTLASS (#51038), fp32 weight scales and per-expert (#50833, #51411).

New models: Muse Glimmer (#51655), Ling 3.0 Flash with BF16, MTP, and parser support (#51045) plus an FP8 variant (#51265) and hybrid MXFP4 routed experts (#52114), Dots3 NOTE native multimodal (#51655, #51045).

Correctness: MiniMax-M3 NVFP4 inference (#48929) and compressed-tensors FP8 MoE SwiGLU params (#46845), Gemma3n/Gemma4 variable-length audio batch padding (#50958), Gemma 4 compatibility with the (#48929, #46845).
Intel XPU: a torch linear backend including blockwise GEMM (#49664, #50826), MXFP8 linear weights for the INC DeepSeek V4 model (#48476), async-scheduling PP sampled-token broadcast overlapped with.
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput

technical_deep_dive.theme: Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v0.28.0, teams operating day-0 model architectures, multimodal vision/audio & transformers backend relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on Standard single-node and multi-node GPU inference pools.
tech_bullets: E/P/D disaggregation: Model Runner V2 E/P/D support (#38390), duplicate image preprocessing removed with GPU-side preprocessing (#50390), KV consumers may omit multimodal embeddings (#52697) (#38390, #50390).

Hybrid/Mamba: prefix caching on by default (#50991), the final part of the Mamba attention module refactor (#44857), 3D-grid tiling of the state-copy Triton kernels (#49436), and Mamba alignment (#50991, #44857).

RL workflows: stateful trainer send over NCCL and sparse NCCL (#50902), `CuMemAllocator.discard()` for tag-selective GPU memory release (#52514), level-2 sleep/wake/reload fixed with LoRA enabled (#50902, #52514).
LoRA: vision tower LoRA for Gemma4 (#42662), tower/connector LoRA for Keye (#51780) and Ultravox (#48215) (#42662, #51780).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet

technical_deep_dive.theme: Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling (AMD ROCm 10 / MI355X, TPU & XPU)
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v0.28.0, teams operating multi-vendor accelerator scaling relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on AMD Instinct MI300X/MI350/MI355X (ROCm 10.0), Intel XPU, and Google Cloud TPU.
tech_bullets: Connectors: transfer mode (push/pull) included in the NIXL compatibility hash (#50620), a MoRIIO per-layer READ-completion barrier (#48534), 2P2D wide-EP with mori-ep/mori-io at dp=ep=16 (#45043) (#50620, #48534).
`reasoning_content` output removal is documented as a breaking client change (#50624).
ROCm: torch 2.12, triton 3.7, torchaudio, torchvision (#50607).

New capabilities: request priority parsed from an HTTP header (#51089), session ID plumbing into requests (#48048), `count_reasoning_tokens` in the streaming parser engine (#45802), `content_parts` (#51089, #48048).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code

# What's New in vLLM v0.28.0

## High-Level Explanation
vLLM v0.28.0 focuses on Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, Next-Gen Speculative Decoding, and Low-Precision Quantization Kernels. For operators, this release translates 48 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups**: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.
- **Next-Gen Speculative Decoding**: Improves next-gen speculative decoding for interactive coding assistants, agent loops, and low-batch-size real-time inference running on nvidia hopper/blackwell, amd mi300x/mi355x, and cpu/xpu draft runners, delivering accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth.
- **Low-Precision Quantization Kernels**: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.
- **Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend**: Improves day-0 model architectures, multimodal vision/audio & transformers backend for newly released foundation models, vision-language (vlm), speech/asr (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and multi-lora adapters running on standard single-node and multi-node gpu inference pools, delivering consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet.
- **Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling**: Improves multi-vendor accelerator scaling for cross-vendor llm fleets running deepseek, qwen, llama, and minimax outside cuda-only clouds running on amd instinct mi300x/mi350/mi355x (rocm 10.0), intel xpu, and google cloud tpu, delivering enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)
| Workload / Team | Models / Services | GPUs / Hardware | Practical Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups (DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3)** | Frontier Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) reasoning and agentic models (DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3/K3.1, MiniMax-M3.1) | NVIDIA Blackwell (GB200/GB300/B200), Hopper (H100/H200), and multi-node Expert Parallel (EP) clusters | Delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens |
| **Next-Gen Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3, DSpark, DFlash, MTP & Suffix)** | Interactive coding assistants, agent loops, and low-batch-size real-time inference | NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell, AMD MI300X/MI355X, and CPU/XPU draft runners | Accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth |
| **Low-Precision Quantization Kernels (NVFP4, MXFP4, MXFP8, FP8 & Humming)** | 100B–1T+ parameter models (Mistral Large 4, DeepSeek-V4, Qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit | NVIDIA Blackwell (SM100 NVFP4), Hopper (SM90 FP8), and AMD MI350/MI355X | Halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput |
| **Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend** | Newly released foundation models, Vision-Language (VLM), Speech/ASR (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and Multi-LoRA adapters | Standard single-node and multi-node GPU inference pools | Consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet |
| **Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling (AMD ROCm 10 / MI355X, TPU & XPU)** | Cross-vendor LLM fleets running DeepSeek, Qwen, Llama, and MiniMax outside CUDA-only clouds | AMD Instinct MI300X/MI350/MI355X (ROCm 10.0), Intel XPU, and Google Cloud TPU | Enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code |
| **Breaking Changes & Deprecations Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **Extensible KV Cache, Memory Budgeting & Tiered Offloading** | High-concurrency chat APIs, long-context coding agents (32K–128K+), and multi-turn RAG workloads | NVIDIA Hopper (H100/H200), Blackwell (B200/GB200), and AMD Instinct (MI300X/MI355X) + host DRAM/NVMe tiers | Expands effective KV capacity by 25–55% per GPU, serving more concurrent users per rack without adding hardware |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **Extensible KV Cache**: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction. Why it matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.
- **Model Runner V2 (MRV2)**: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding. Why it matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.
- **Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)**: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass. Why it matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.
- **MLA & Sparse-MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention)**: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing. Why it matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.
- **NVFP4 / MXFP4 / FP8 Quantization**: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores. Why it matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.
- **P/D Disaggregation (Prefill/Decode Split & NIXL)**: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL. Why it matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.
- **MoE / MegaMoE & Expert Parallelism (EP / DeepGEMM)**: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs. Why it matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.
- **Piecewise & Breakable CUDA Graphs**: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token. Why it matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.
- **Tiered KV Offloading & Prefix Caching**: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts. Why it matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.

## 4. Should I Upgrade?
**Verdict**: UPGRADE WITH CONFIG CHECK — High-ROI throughput/stability gains, but review breaking flag/API removals first

## 5. Technical Deep Dive (What's the Big Deal Under the Hood?)
### 1. Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups (DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3) ([#50607](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50607), [#43615](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43615), [#47017](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47017), [#52212](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52212))
- **Previously**: Prior to v0.28.0, teams operating frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA Blackwell (GB200/GB300/B200), Hopper (H100/H200), and multi-node Expert Parallel (EP) clusters.
- **Technical change**: AMD ROCm: torch 2.12 / triton 3.7 stack bump (#50607), AITER and FP8 inference enabled on GFX120x (#43615), DeepSeek-V4 on gfx11 (#47017), optimized Triton sparse-MLA decode on gfx950 (#52212) (#50607, #43615).
- **Technical change**: CPU: an MLA backend so DeepSeek-V2/V3 can run on CPU (#49453), a triton-cpu wheel (#52092), GPTQ and AWQ enabled on s390x (#51148) along with tcmalloc (#50841), BF16 MoE routed through zentorch on (#49453, #52092).
- **Technical change**: DeepGEMM pinned to the deepseek-ai nv_dev tip (#52035), DeepEP pinned by full commit hash (#52028), FlashAttention 3 built with the torch stable API (#49599) (#52035, #52028).
- **Technical change**: MoE: extended EPLB support for Mistral Large 3 and additional MoE backends (#48355), CuTe DSL skinny GEMM extended to GLM-5.2 (#49791) (#48355, #49791).
- **Operational impact**: Delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens
### 2. Next-Gen Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3, DSpark, DFlash, MTP & Suffix) ([#49718](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49718), [#49792](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49792), [#50230](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50230), [#52164](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52164))
- **Previously**: Prior to v0.28.0, teams operating next-gen speculative decoding relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell, AMD MI300X/MI355X, and CPU/XPU draft runners.
- **Technical change**: NVIDIA: FlashInfer XQA decode support on SM12x (#49718), a CuTeDSL fused query kernel on SM100 (#49792), programmatic dependent launch for the DSA decode kernels (#50230), the native DSA decode path (#49718, #49792).
- **Technical change**: Qwen: Qwen3.8 enabled on AMD ROCm (#50068), fused CUDA post-conv MTP decode kernel for Qwen3.5 GDN (#51674), GDN gates aligned with speculative tokens (#51812), and Qwen3.5 fixes for text-only (#50068, #51674).
- **Technical change**: Speculative decoding: DSpark confidence-scheduled verification (#47808), top-k DSpark Markov projection (#49969), DFlash2 with local convolution and a candidate selector (#52816), async scheduling (#47808, #49969).
- **Technical change**: Speculative decoding coverage: EAGLE3 support declared on KimiLinear (#52171), Qwen3.6 dSpark acceptance coverage (#51310) (#52171, #51310).
- **Operational impact**: Accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth
### 3. Low-Precision Quantization Kernels (NVFP4, MXFP4, MXFP8, FP8 & Humming) ([#50833](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50833), [#51411](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51411), [#51038](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51038), [#51419](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51419))
- **Previously**: Prior to v0.28.0, teams operating low-precision quantization kernels relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA Blackwell (SM100 NVFP4), Hopper (SM90 FP8), and AMD MI350/MI355X.
- **Technical change**: Fixes: dynamic INT8 W8A8 MoE config no longer built as W8A16 (#50833) and a TritonExperts crash (#51411), MXFP4 conversion for FlashInfer CUTLASS (#51038), fp32 weight scales and per-expert (#50833, #51411).
- **Technical change**: New models: Muse Glimmer (#51655), Ling 3.0 Flash with BF16, MTP, and parser support (#51045) plus an FP8 variant (#51265) and hybrid MXFP4 routed experts (#52114), Dots3 NOTE native multimodal (#51655, #51045).
- **Technical change**: Correctness: MiniMax-M3 NVFP4 inference (#48929) and compressed-tensors FP8 MoE SwiGLU params (#46845), Gemma3n/Gemma4 variable-length audio batch padding (#50958), Gemma 4 compatibility with the (#48929, #46845).
- **Technical change**: Intel XPU: a torch linear backend including blockwise GEMM (#49664, #50826), MXFP8 linear weights for the INC DeepSeek V4 model (#48476), async-scheduling PP sampled-token broadcast overlapped with.
- **Operational impact**: Halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput
### 4. Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend ([#38390](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38390), [#50390](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50390), [#52697](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52697), [#50275](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50275))

- **Technical change**: Hybrid/Mamba: prefix caching on by default (#50991), the final part of the Mamba attention module refactor (#44857), 3D-grid tiling of the state-copy Triton kernels (#49436), and Mamba alignment (#50991, #44857).
- **Technical change**: RL workflows: stateful trainer send over NCCL and sparse NCCL (#50902), `CuMemAllocator.discard()` for tag-selective GPU memory release (#52514), level-2 sleep/wake/reload fixed with LoRA enabled (#50902, #52514).

- **Technical change**: `reasoning_content` output removal is documented as a breaking client change (#50624).
- **Technical change**: ROCm: torch 2.12, triton 3.7, torchaudio, torchvision (#50607).
- **Technical change**: New capabilities: request priority parsed from an HTTP header (#51089), session ID plumbing into requests (#48048), `count_reasoning_tokens` in the streaming parser engine (#45802), `content_parts` (#51089, #48048).
- **Operational impact**: Enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code
### 6. Breaking Changes & Deprecations Enhancements ([#49389](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49389), [#48684](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48684), [#51078](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51078), [#43529](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43529))

high_level_changes.headline: Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.

high_level_changes.headline: Low-Precision Quantization Kernels
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.

high_level_changes.headline: Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves day-0 model architectures, multimodal vision/audio & transformers backend for newly released foundation models, vision-language (vlm), speech/asr (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and multi-lora adapters running on standard single-node and multi-node gpu inference pools, delivering consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet.

high_level_changes.headline: Next-Gen Speculative Decoding
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves next-gen speculative decoding for interactive coding assistants, agent loops, and low-batch-size real-time inference running on nvidia hopper/blackwell, amd mi300x/mi355x, and cpu/xpu draft runners, delivering accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth.

high_level_changes.headline: Model Runner V2
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves model runner v2 for all production gpu deployments, latency-sensitive streaming apps, and custom logits processors running on all cuda and rocm gpu fleets running vllm's v2 execution engine, delivering cuts CPU dispatch overhead and lowers inter-token latency (ITL) by 3–15% while simplifying engine maintenance.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.

jargon_glossary.meaning: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.

jargon_glossary.term: Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)
jargon_glossary.meaning: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.

jargon_glossary.meaning: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP).
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.

jargon_glossary.term: TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)
jargon_glossary.meaning: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.

# What's New in vLLM v0.27.0

## High-Level Explanation
vLLM v0.27.0 focuses on Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, Low-Precision Quantization Kernels, and Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend. For operators, this release translates 42 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups**: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.
- **Low-Precision Quantization Kernels**: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **Extensible KV Cache**: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction. Why it matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.
- **Model Runner V2 (MRV2)**: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding. Why it matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.
- **Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)**: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass. Why it matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.
- **MLA & Sparse-MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention)**: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing. Why it matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.
- **NVFP4 / MXFP4 / FP8 Quantization**: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores. Why it matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.
- **P/D Disaggregation (Prefill/Decode Split & NIXL)**: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL. Why it matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.
- **DCP & PCP (Decode / Prefill Context Parallelism)**: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP). Why it matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.
- **MoE / MegaMoE & Expert Parallelism (EP / DeepGEMM)**: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs. Why it matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.
- **Piecewise & Breakable CUDA Graphs**: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token. Why it matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.
- **TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)**: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream. Why it matters: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.
- **Tiered KV Offloading & Prefix Caching**: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts. Why it matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.

vllm_guides.positioning: vLLM v0.26.0 focuses on Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, Next-Gen Speculative Decoding, and Low-Precision Quantization Kernels. For operators, this release translates 42 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.
vllm_guides.high_level_explanation: vLLM v0.26.0 focuses on Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, Next-Gen Speculative Decoding, and Low-Precision Quantization Kernels. For operators, this release translates 42 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.
vllm_guides.verdict: UPGRADE WITH CONFIG CHECK — High-ROI throughput/stability gains, but review breaking flag/API removals first

high_level_changes.headline: Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.

high_level_changes.headline: Next-Gen Speculative Decoding
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves next-gen speculative decoding for interactive coding assistants, agent loops, and low-batch-size real-time inference running on nvidia hopper/blackwell, amd mi300x/mi355x, and cpu/xpu draft runners, delivering accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth.

high_level_changes.headline: Low-Precision Quantization Kernels
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.

high_level_changes.headline: Disaggregated Serving
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves disaggregated serving for planet-scale distributed inference clusters, serverless gpu autoscalers, and openai responses api clients running on multi-node rdma / infiniband / aws efa clusters and kubernetes inference gateways, delivering eliminates full-cluster restarts when a single GPU rank dies and cuts autoscaling cold-start time via CRIU restore.

high_level_changes.headline: Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves day-0 model architectures, multimodal vision/audio & transformers backend for newly released foundation models, vision-language (vlm), speech/asr (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and multi-lora adapters running on standard single-node and multi-node gpu inference pools, delivering consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.

jargon_glossary.meaning: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.

jargon_glossary.term: Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)
jargon_glossary.meaning: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.

jargon_glossary.meaning: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP).
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.

jargon_glossary.term: TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)
jargon_glossary.meaning: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.

# What's New in vLLM v0.26.0

## High-Level Explanation
vLLM v0.26.0 focuses on Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, Next-Gen Speculative Decoding, and Low-Precision Quantization Kernels. For operators, this release translates 42 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups**: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.
- **Next-Gen Speculative Decoding**: Improves next-gen speculative decoding for interactive coding assistants, agent loops, and low-batch-size real-time inference running on nvidia hopper/blackwell, amd mi300x/mi355x, and cpu/xpu draft runners, delivering accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth.
- **Low-Precision Quantization Kernels**: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.
- **Disaggregated Serving**: Improves disaggregated serving for planet-scale distributed inference clusters, serverless gpu autoscalers, and openai responses api clients running on multi-node rdma / infiniband / aws efa clusters and kubernetes inference gateways, delivering eliminates full-cluster restarts when a single GPU rank dies and cuts autoscaling cold-start time via CRIU restore.
- **Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend**: Improves day-0 model architectures, multimodal vision/audio & transformers backend for newly released foundation models, vision-language (vlm), speech/asr (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and multi-lora adapters running on standard single-node and multi-node gpu inference pools, delivering consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)
| Workload / Team | Models / Services | GPUs / Hardware | Practical Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups (DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3)** | Frontier Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) reasoning and agentic models (DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3/K3.1, MiniMax-M3.1) | NVIDIA Blackwell (GB200/GB300/B200), Hopper (H100/H200), and multi-node Expert Parallel (EP) clusters | Delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens |
| **Next-Gen Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3, DSpark, DFlash, MTP & Suffix)** | Interactive coding assistants, agent loops, and low-batch-size real-time inference | NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell, AMD MI300X/MI355X, and CPU/XPU draft runners | Accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth |
| **Low-Precision Quantization Kernels (NVFP4, MXFP4, MXFP8, FP8 & Humming)** | 100B–1T+ parameter models (Mistral Large 4, DeepSeek-V4, Qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit | NVIDIA Blackwell (SM100 NVFP4), Hopper (SM90 FP8), and AMD MI350/MI355X | Halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput |
| **Disaggregated Serving (P/D, DCP/PCP), Fault Tolerance & Fast Checkpoint/Restore** | Planet-scale distributed inference clusters, serverless GPU autoscalers, and OpenAI Responses API clients | Multi-node RDMA / InfiniBand / AWS EFA clusters and Kubernetes inference gateways | Eliminates full-cluster restarts when a single GPU rank dies and cuts autoscaling cold-start time via CRIU restore |
| **Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend** | Newly released foundation models, Vision-Language (VLM), Speech/ASR (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and Multi-LoRA adapters | Standard single-node and multi-node GPU inference pools | Consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet |
| **Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling (AMD ROCm 10 / MI355X, TPU & XPU)** | Cross-vendor LLM fleets running DeepSeek, Qwen, Llama, and MiniMax outside CUDA-only clouds | AMD Instinct MI300X/MI350/MI355X (ROCm 10.0), Intel XPU, and Google Cloud TPU | Enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code |
| **Model Runner V2 (MRV2) Consolidation & Breakable CUDA Graphs** | All production GPU deployments, latency-sensitive streaming apps, and custom logits processors | All CUDA and ROCm GPU fleets running vLLM's V2 execution engine | Cuts CPU dispatch overhead and lowers inter-token latency (ITL) by 3–15% while simplifying engine maintenance |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **Extensible KV Cache**: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction. Why it matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.
- **Model Runner V2 (MRV2)**: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding. Why it matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.
- **Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)**: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass. Why it matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.
- **MLA & Sparse-MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention)**: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing. Why it matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.
- **NVFP4 / MXFP4 / FP8 Quantization**: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores. Why it matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.
- **P/D Disaggregation (Prefill/Decode Split & NIXL)**: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL. Why it matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.
- **DCP & PCP (Decode / Prefill Context Parallelism)**: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP). Why it matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.
- **MoE / MegaMoE & Expert Parallelism (EP / DeepGEMM)**: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs. Why it matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.
- **Piecewise & Breakable CUDA Graphs**: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token. Why it matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.
- **TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)**: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream. Why it matters: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.
- **Tiered KV Offloading & Prefix Caching**: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts. Why it matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.

## 4. Should I Upgrade?
**Verdict**: UPGRADE WITH CONFIG CHECK — High-ROI throughput/stability gains, but review breaking flag/API removals first
- **Before You Upgrade**: Models removed: TeleChat (#47989), Persimmon and Fuyu (#48096). -> Action: Check deprecation/removal impact before upgrading. ([#47989](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47989), [#48096](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48096))
- **Security**: Add resource-bounds validation to derender endpoints (#47260). sanitize server file paths from validation error responses (#46415). ([#47260](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47260), [#46415](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46415))
- **Security**: Replace diskcache to eliminate pickle deserialization (#44549). ([#44549](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44549))
- **Security**: Fix a concurrent sparse-invariant race that bypassed CVE remediation (#48583). ([#48583](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48583))
