### 2. Next-Gen Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3, DSpark, DFlash, MTP & Suffix) ([#46090](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46090), [#40714](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40714), [#48289](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48289), [#47321](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47321))
- **Previously**: Prior to v0.26.0, teams operating next-gen speculative decoding relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell, AMD MI300X/MI355X, and CPU/XPU draft runners.
- **Technical change**: CPU: DFlash speculative decoding for GDN models on CPU (#46090), s390x NUMA topology (#40714), native macOS arm64 CPU wheel builds (#48289); POWER VSX math function optimization (#47321) and IBM (#46090, #40714).
- **Technical change**: Reasoning: optimize TPOT for thinking budget when used with speculative decoding (#46662).
- **Technical change**: Speculative decoding: runtime draft weight update (#46725), hybrid (SWA + full attention) DFlash drafters (#47914), SWA support for qwen-eagle3 (#47568), Gemma4-12B DSpark draft model (#47216), DSv4 (#46725, #47914).
- **Technical change**: XPU: batch-invariant kernels (#41934), HND KV layout support (#47975), DSpark spec decode for DSv4 (#47677), nightly/release image publishing (#47880, #48126) (#41934, #47975).
- **Operational impact**: Accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth
### 3. Low-Precision Quantization Kernels (NVFP4, MXFP4, MXFP8, FP8 & Humming) ([#48688](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48688), [#47718](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47718), [#48519](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48519), [#48788](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48788))
- **Previously**: Prior to v0.26.0, teams operating low-precision quantization kernels relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA Blackwell (SM100 NVFP4), Hopper (SM90 FP8), and AMD MI350/MI355X.
- **Technical change**: ROCm: fp32 `head_dtype` `torch.mm` fast path (#48688), DSv4 two-stage compressor kernel (#47718), sparse decode/prefill optimizations (#48519, #48788, #46275), DSv3.2 sparse MLA KV-split heuristic (#48688, #47718).
- **Technical change**: NVFP4/MXFP4: `nvfp4_per_token` online MoE quantization (#48538), CuTe-DSL FlashInfer MXFP4 quantization (#48417); bounded peak memory when repacking FP4 MoE weights for Marlin (#47851) and for NVFP4 (#48538, #48417).
- **Technical change**: ROCm: HybridW4A16 linear kernel (#40977).
- **Technical change**: Humming w[2-7]a[4,8] weight-only inference with compressed-tensors (#46390). int4 quantization for the emulation MoE backend (#48451) (#46390, #48451).
- **Operational impact**: Halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput
### 4. Disaggregated Serving (P/D, DCP/PCP), Fault Tolerance & Fast Checkpoint/Restore ([#48012](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48012), [#48011](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48011), [#44455](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44455), [#46570](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46570))
- **Previously**: Prior to v0.26.0, teams operating disaggregated serving relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on Multi-node RDMA / InfiniBand / AWS EFA clusters and Kubernetes inference gateways.
- **Technical change**: Attention: select a different attention backend per KV-cache group (#48012). sliding-window as an explicit backend capability (#48011) (#48012, #48011).
- **Technical change**: Build/autotune: arm64 Blackwell SM10x/SM110 image builds (#48041); skip CuTeDSL fp4_gemm autotuning by default (#48268) (#48041, #48268).
- **Technical change**: PD disaggregation: NIXL pipeline-parallel prefill in push mode (#45880).
- **Operational impact**: Eliminates full-cluster restarts when a single GPU rank dies and cuts autoscaling cold-start time via CRIU restore
### 5. Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend ([#46998](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46998), [#47006](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47006), [#48350](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48350), [#47546](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47546))
- **Previously**: Prior to v0.26.0, teams operating day-0 model architectures, multimodal vision/audio & transformers backend relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on Standard single-node and multi-node GPU inference pools.
- **Technical change**: Qwen: fuse more RMSNorm + all-reduce in Qwen3.5 (#46998), replace MoE all-reduce with reduce-scatter (#47006), Qwen3.5 H20 optimization (#48350), expand Triton warmup coverage (#47546) (#46998, #47006).
- **Technical change**: New models: Inkling family (#48799, #48822, #48858, #48869, #48884, #48990), BertForMaskedLM (#48463), RobertaForTokenClassification / XLMRobertaForTokenClassification (#47991), LongCat-Flash-Lite.
- **Technical change**: LoRA: FlashInfer MoE LoRA for BF16 models (#48632), LoRA for tower/connector in LlavaNextVideo (#48594), fp32 `lm_head` on the LoRA path (#48525), optimized `TrtLlmLoRAExperts` (#48759) (#48632, #48594).
- **Technical change**: Transformers backend migrations: Olmo/Olmo2 (#48100), MistralLarge3 to AutoWeightsLoader (#48153), HunyuanVL native transformers processor for transformers 5.13 (#47872) (#48100, #48153).
- **Operational impact**: Consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet
### 6. Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling (AMD ROCm 10 / MI355X, TPU & XPU) ([#47973](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47973), [#48335](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48335), [#42562](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42562), [#45182](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45182))
- **Previously**: Prior to v0.26.0, teams operating multi-vendor accelerator scaling relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on AMD Instinct MI300X/MI350/MI355X (ROCm 10.0), Intel XPU, and Google Cloud TPU.
- **Technical change**: MoE router GEMMs: BF16x3 router GEMM (#47973), FP32 router GEMV (#48335), generic CuteDSL LL BF16 router GEMM (#42562). TRTLLM BF16 MoE modular kernel (#45182) (#47973, #48335).
- **Technical change**: Transformers 5.13.0 (#47867), FlashInfer 0.6.14 (#47669), NIXL 1.3.1 (#47559), tpu-inference v0.24.0 (#47835), nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.6.0 (#47442), vllm_xpu_kernels v0.1.11.1 (#48942) (#47867, #47669).
- **Operational impact**: Enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code

vllm_guides.positioning: vLLM v0.25.0 focuses on Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, Low-Precision Quantization Kernels, and Model Runner V2. For operators, this release translates 49 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.
vllm_guides.high_level_explanation: vLLM v0.25.0 focuses on Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, Low-Precision Quantization Kernels, and Model Runner V2. For operators, this release translates 49 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

high_level_changes.headline: Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.

high_level_changes.headline: Low-Precision Quantization Kernels
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.

high_level_changes.headline: Model Runner V2
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves model runner v2 for all production gpu deployments, latency-sensitive streaming apps, and custom logits processors running on all cuda and rocm gpu fleets running vllm's v2 execution engine, delivering cuts CPU dispatch overhead and lowers inter-token latency (ITL) by 3–15% while simplifying engine maintenance.

high_level_changes.headline: Next-Gen Speculative Decoding
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves next-gen speculative decoding for interactive coding assistants, agent loops, and low-batch-size real-time inference running on nvidia hopper/blackwell, amd mi300x/mi355x, and cpu/xpu draft runners, delivering accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth.

high_level_changes.headline: Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves day-0 model architectures, multimodal vision/audio & transformers backend for newly released foundation models, vision-language (vlm), speech/asr (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and multi-lora adapters running on standard single-node and multi-node gpu inference pools, delivering consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.

jargon_glossary.meaning: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.

jargon_glossary.term: Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)
jargon_glossary.meaning: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.

jargon_glossary.meaning: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP).
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.

jargon_glossary.term: TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)
jargon_glossary.meaning: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Compiling vLLM's custom C++/CUDA kernels against PyTorch's binary-stable application interface rather than internal C++ symbols.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Lets you upgrade PyTorch versions or security patches without rebuilding vLLM's entire CUDA kernel suite from source.

technical_deep_dive.theme: Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups (DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3)
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v0.25.0, teams operating frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA Blackwell (GB200/GB300/B200), Hopper (H100/H200), and multi-node Expert Parallel (EP) clusters.
tech_bullets: GLM-5.2 / DeepSeek: `fused_indexer_q_rope_quant` Triton kernel (1.9–3.3% E2E throughput) (#46862), reduce-scatter MoE all-reduce (3.1–3.2% E2E) (#46635), op fusion for GLM5/DSV3.2 (#46876) (#46862, #46635).
AMD/ROCm: moved to torch 2.11 stable ABI (#47128). AITER FlashAttention MLA prefill backend `ROCM_AITER_FA` (#45033) (#47128, #45033).

NVIDIA/Blackwell: FlashInfer fused all-reduce tuned for world_size=16 on GB300 (#46392), restored NVFP4 swizzled-scale zero-init to recover Blackwell decode throughput (#45739), CuTeDSL/FA4-MLA (#46392, #45739).
GLM-5 family: GLM-5 / DeepSeek-V3.2 added to the model zoo (#46808), GLM-5.2 FP32 gate (#47410), GLM MTP post-final-norm fix (#47448), GLM4V startup fix (#47155) (#46808, #47410).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens

technical_deep_dive.theme: Low-Precision Quantization Kernels (NVFP4, MXFP4, MXFP8, FP8 & Humming)
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v0.25.0, teams operating low-precision quantization kernels relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA Blackwell (SM100 NVFP4), Hopper (SM90 FP8), and AMD MI350/MI355X.
tech_bullets: Deprecated the old FP8 online MoE quantization class (#44514). legacy `api_server.py` moved to the examples directory (#46783) (#44514, #46783).
ROCm: stabilized high-throughput DBO for DP+EP (#46990), EPLB for Quark OCP MXFP4 MoE (#47220) (#46990, #47220).
FP8: weights padding for per-block online quantization (#44763); deprecated the old FP8 online MoE quantization class (#44514) (#44763, #44514).

Fixes: W8A8 int-quant scheme-selection regression (#46860), tied quantized embeddings for ModelOpt Gemma4 (#45544), NVFP4+MTP crash on Qwen3Next (#46316), ModelOpt mixed-precision for sparse configs (#46860, #45544).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput

technical_deep_dive.theme: Model Runner V2 (MRV2) Consolidation & Breakable CUDA Graphs

tech_bullets: Transformers backend: now as fast as native vLLM (#47187), FP8 MoE fix (#46820), embed scaling + CUDA graph fix (#48010), GPTBigCode/Starcoder2 (#30966) and RoBERTa (#47452) migration, M-RoPE (#47187, #46820).

Model Runner V2: default for all dense models (#44443); EVS (#46535), realtime embeddings (#46762), Mamba hybrid prefix caching (#42406), multimodal-prefix bidirectional attention (#46942) (#44443, #46535).

Intel XPU: W8A8 FP8 linear kernel with multi-granularity quant (#43645), pipeline-parallel accuracy fix (#47253), uniform-batch CUDA graph for FA2 (#46555), route mm_prefix models to Triton attention (#43645, #47253).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Cuts CPU dispatch overhead and lowers inter-token latency (ITL) by 3–15% while simplifying engine maintenance

technical_deep_dive.theme: Next-Gen Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3, DSpark, DFlash, MTP & Suffix)

# What's New in vLLM v0.25.0

## High-Level Explanation
vLLM v0.25.0 focuses on Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, Low-Precision Quantization Kernels, and Model Runner V2. For operators, this release translates 49 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups**: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.
- **Low-Precision Quantization Kernels**: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.
- **Model Runner V2**: Improves model runner v2 for all production gpu deployments, latency-sensitive streaming apps, and custom logits processors running on all cuda and rocm gpu fleets running vllm's v2 execution engine, delivering cuts CPU dispatch overhead and lowers inter-token latency (ITL) by 3–15% while simplifying engine maintenance.
- **Next-Gen Speculative Decoding**: Improves next-gen speculative decoding for interactive coding assistants, agent loops, and low-batch-size real-time inference running on nvidia hopper/blackwell, amd mi300x/mi355x, and cpu/xpu draft runners, delivering accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth.
- **Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend**: Improves day-0 model architectures, multimodal vision/audio & transformers backend for newly released foundation models, vision-language (vlm), speech/asr (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and multi-lora adapters running on standard single-node and multi-node gpu inference pools, delivering consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)
| Workload / Team | Models / Services | GPUs / Hardware | Practical Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups (DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3)** | Frontier Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) reasoning and agentic models (DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3/K3.1, MiniMax-M3.1) | NVIDIA Blackwell (GB200/GB300/B200), Hopper (H100/H200), and multi-node Expert Parallel (EP) clusters | Delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens |
| **Low-Precision Quantization Kernels (NVFP4, MXFP4, MXFP8, FP8 & Humming)** | 100B–1T+ parameter models (Mistral Large 4, DeepSeek-V4, Qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit | NVIDIA Blackwell (SM100 NVFP4), Hopper (SM90 FP8), and AMD MI350/MI355X | Halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput |
| **Model Runner V2 (MRV2) Consolidation & Breakable CUDA Graphs** | All production GPU deployments, latency-sensitive streaming apps, and custom logits processors | All CUDA and ROCm GPU fleets running vLLM's V2 execution engine | Cuts CPU dispatch overhead and lowers inter-token latency (ITL) by 3–15% while simplifying engine maintenance |
| **Next-Gen Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3, DSpark, DFlash, MTP & Suffix)** | Interactive coding assistants, agent loops, and low-batch-size real-time inference | NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell, AMD MI300X/MI355X, and CPU/XPU draft runners | Accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth |
| **Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend** | Newly released foundation models, Vision-Language (VLM), Speech/ASR (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and Multi-LoRA adapters | Standard single-node and multi-node GPU inference pools | Consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet |
| **Extensible KV Cache, Memory Budgeting & Tiered Offloading** | High-concurrency chat APIs, long-context coding agents (32K–128K+), and multi-turn RAG workloads | NVIDIA Hopper (H100/H200), Blackwell (B200/GB200), and AMD Instinct (MI300X/MI355X) + host DRAM/NVMe tiers | Expands effective KV capacity by 25–55% per GPU, serving more concurrent users per rack without adding hardware |
| **Deprecations & Removals Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **Extensible KV Cache**: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction. Why it matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.
- **Model Runner V2 (MRV2)**: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding. Why it matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.
- **Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)**: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass. Why it matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.
- **MLA & Sparse-MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention)**: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing. Why it matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.
- **NVFP4 / MXFP4 / FP8 Quantization**: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores. Why it matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.
- **P/D Disaggregation (Prefill/Decode Split & NIXL)**: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL. Why it matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.
- **DCP & PCP (Decode / Prefill Context Parallelism)**: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP). Why it matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.
- **MoE / MegaMoE & Expert Parallelism (EP / DeepGEMM)**: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs. Why it matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.
- **Piecewise & Breakable CUDA Graphs**: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token. Why it matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.
- **TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)**: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream. Why it matters: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.
- **Tiered KV Offloading & Prefix Caching**: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts. Why it matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.
- **LibTorch Stable ABI**: Compiling vLLM's custom C++/CUDA kernels against PyTorch's binary-stable application interface rather than internal C++ symbols. Why it matters: Lets you upgrade PyTorch versions or security patches without rebuilding vLLM's entire CUDA kernel suite from source.

vllm_guides.positioning: vLLM v0.24.0 focuses on Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling, Low-Precision Quantization Kernels, and Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend. For operators, this release translates 42 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

high_level_changes.headline: Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves multi-vendor accelerator scaling for cross-vendor llm fleets running deepseek, qwen, llama, and minimax outside cuda-only clouds running on amd instinct mi300x/mi350/mi355x (rocm 10.0), intel xpu, and google cloud tpu, delivering enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code.

high_level_changes.headline: Low-Precision Quantization Kernels
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.

high_level_changes.headline: Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves day-0 model architectures, multimodal vision/audio & transformers backend for newly released foundation models, vision-language (vlm), speech/asr (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and multi-lora adapters running on standard single-node and multi-node gpu inference pools, delivering consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet.

high_level_changes.headline: Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.

high_level_changes.headline: Disaggregated Serving
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves disaggregated serving for planet-scale distributed inference clusters, serverless gpu autoscalers, and openai responses api clients running on multi-node rdma / infiniband / aws efa clusters and kubernetes inference gateways, delivering eliminates full-cluster restarts when a single GPU rank dies and cuts autoscaling cold-start time via CRIU restore.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.

jargon_glossary.meaning: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.

jargon_glossary.term: Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)
jargon_glossary.meaning: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.

jargon_glossary.meaning: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP).
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Compiling vLLM's custom C++/CUDA kernels against PyTorch's binary-stable application interface rather than internal C++ symbols.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Lets you upgrade PyTorch versions or security patches without rebuilding vLLM's entire CUDA kernel suite from source.

# What's New in vLLM v0.24.0

## High-Level Explanation
vLLM v0.24.0 focuses on Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling, Low-Precision Quantization Kernels, and Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend. For operators, this release translates 42 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling**: Improves multi-vendor accelerator scaling for cross-vendor llm fleets running deepseek, qwen, llama, and minimax outside cuda-only clouds running on amd instinct mi300x/mi350/mi355x (rocm 10.0), intel xpu, and google cloud tpu, delivering enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code.
- **Low-Precision Quantization Kernels**: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.
- **Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend**: Improves day-0 model architectures, multimodal vision/audio & transformers backend for newly released foundation models, vision-language (vlm), speech/asr (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and multi-lora adapters running on standard single-node and multi-node gpu inference pools, delivering consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet.
- **Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups**: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.
- **Disaggregated Serving**: Improves disaggregated serving for planet-scale distributed inference clusters, serverless gpu autoscalers, and openai responses api clients running on multi-node rdma / infiniband / aws efa clusters and kubernetes inference gateways, delivering eliminates full-cluster restarts when a single GPU rank dies and cuts autoscaling cold-start time via CRIU restore.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)
| Workload / Team | Models / Services | GPUs / Hardware | Practical Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling (AMD ROCm 10 / MI355X, TPU & XPU)** | Cross-vendor LLM fleets running DeepSeek, Qwen, Llama, and MiniMax outside CUDA-only clouds | AMD Instinct MI300X/MI350/MI355X (ROCm 10.0), Intel XPU, and Google Cloud TPU | Enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **Extensible KV Cache**: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction. Why it matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.
- **Model Runner V2 (MRV2)**: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding. Why it matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.
- **Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)**: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass. Why it matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.
- **MLA & Sparse-MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention)**: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing. Why it matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.
- **NVFP4 / MXFP4 / FP8 Quantization**: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores. Why it matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.
- **P/D Disaggregation (Prefill/Decode Split & NIXL)**: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL. Why it matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.
- **DCP & PCP (Decode / Prefill Context Parallelism)**: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP). Why it matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.
- **MoE / MegaMoE & Expert Parallelism (EP / DeepGEMM)**: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs. Why it matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.
- **Piecewise & Breakable CUDA Graphs**: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token. Why it matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.
- **Tiered KV Offloading & Prefix Caching**: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts. Why it matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.
- **LibTorch Stable ABI**: Compiling vLLM's custom C++/CUDA kernels against PyTorch's binary-stable application interface rather than internal C++ symbols. Why it matters: Lets you upgrade PyTorch versions or security patches without rebuilding vLLM's entire CUDA kernel suite from source.

vllm_guides.positioning: vLLM v0.23.0 focuses on Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, Low-Precision Quantization Kernels, and Disaggregated Serving. For operators, this release translates 40 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.
vllm_guides.high_level_explanation: vLLM v0.23.0 focuses on Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, Low-Precision Quantization Kernels, and Disaggregated Serving. For operators, this release translates 40 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.
vllm_guides.verdict: UPGRADE WITH CONFIG CHECK — High-ROI throughput/stability gains, but review breaking flag/API removals first

high_level_changes.headline: Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.

high_level_changes.headline: Low-Precision Quantization Kernels
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.

high_level_changes.headline: Disaggregated Serving
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves disaggregated serving for planet-scale distributed inference clusters, serverless gpu autoscalers, and openai responses api clients running on multi-node rdma / infiniband / aws efa clusters and kubernetes inference gateways, delivering eliminates full-cluster restarts when a single GPU rank dies and cuts autoscaling cold-start time via CRIU restore.

high_level_changes.headline: Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves day-0 model architectures, multimodal vision/audio & transformers backend for newly released foundation models, vision-language (vlm), speech/asr (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and multi-lora adapters running on standard single-node and multi-node gpu inference pools, delivering consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet.

high_level_changes.headline: Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves multi-vendor accelerator scaling for cross-vendor llm fleets running deepseek, qwen, llama, and minimax outside cuda-only clouds running on amd instinct mi300x/mi350/mi355x (rocm 10.0), intel xpu, and google cloud tpu, delivering enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.

jargon_glossary.meaning: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.

jargon_glossary.term: Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)
jargon_glossary.meaning: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.

jargon_glossary.meaning: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP).
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Compiling vLLM's custom C++/CUDA kernels against PyTorch's binary-stable application interface rather than internal C++ symbols.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Lets you upgrade PyTorch versions or security patches without rebuilding vLLM's entire CUDA kernel suite from source.

# What's New in vLLM v0.23.0

## High-Level Explanation
vLLM v0.23.0 focuses on Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, Low-Precision Quantization Kernels, and Disaggregated Serving. For operators, this release translates 40 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups**: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.
- **Low-Precision Quantization Kernels**: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.
- **Disaggregated Serving**: Improves disaggregated serving for planet-scale distributed inference clusters, serverless gpu autoscalers, and openai responses api clients running on multi-node rdma / infiniband / aws efa clusters and kubernetes inference gateways, delivering eliminates full-cluster restarts when a single GPU rank dies and cuts autoscaling cold-start time via CRIU restore.
- **Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend**: Improves day-0 model architectures, multimodal vision/audio & transformers backend for newly released foundation models, vision-language (vlm), speech/asr (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and multi-lora adapters running on standard single-node and multi-node gpu inference pools, delivering consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet.
- **Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling**: Improves multi-vendor accelerator scaling for cross-vendor llm fleets running deepseek, qwen, llama, and minimax outside cuda-only clouds running on amd instinct mi300x/mi350/mi355x (rocm 10.0), intel xpu, and google cloud tpu, delivering enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)
| Workload / Team | Models / Services | GPUs / Hardware | Practical Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups (DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3)** | Frontier Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) reasoning and agentic models (DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3/K3.1, MiniMax-M3.1) | NVIDIA Blackwell (GB200/GB300/B200), Hopper (H100/H200), and multi-node Expert Parallel (EP) clusters | Delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens |
| **Low-Precision Quantization Kernels (NVFP4, MXFP4, MXFP8, FP8 & Humming)** | 100B–1T+ parameter models (Mistral Large 4, DeepSeek-V4, Qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit | NVIDIA Blackwell (SM100 NVFP4), Hopper (SM90 FP8), and AMD MI350/MI355X | Halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput |
| **Disaggregated Serving (P/D, DCP/PCP), Fault Tolerance & Fast Checkpoint/Restore** | Planet-scale distributed inference clusters, serverless GPU autoscalers, and OpenAI Responses API clients | Multi-node RDMA / InfiniBand / AWS EFA clusters and Kubernetes inference gateways | Eliminates full-cluster restarts when a single GPU rank dies and cuts autoscaling cold-start time via CRIU restore |
| **Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend** | Newly released foundation models, Vision-Language (VLM), Speech/ASR (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and Multi-LoRA adapters | Standard single-node and multi-node GPU inference pools | Consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet |
| **Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling (AMD ROCm 10 / MI355X, TPU & XPU)** | Cross-vendor LLM fleets running DeepSeek, Qwen, Llama, and MiniMax outside CUDA-only clouds | AMD Instinct MI300X/MI350/MI355X (ROCm 10.0), Intel XPU, and Google Cloud TPU | Enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code |
| **Extensible KV Cache, Memory Budgeting & Tiered Offloading** | High-concurrency chat APIs, long-context coding agents (32K–128K+), and multi-turn RAG workloads | NVIDIA Hopper (H100/H200), Blackwell (B200/GB200), and AMD Instinct (MI300X/MI355X) + host DRAM/NVMe tiers | Expands effective KV capacity by 25–55% per GPU, serving more concurrent users per rack without adding hardware |
| **Model Runner V2 (MRV2) Consolidation & Breakable CUDA Graphs** | All production GPU deployments, latency-sensitive streaming apps, and custom logits processors | All CUDA and ROCm GPU fleets running vLLM's V2 execution engine | Cuts CPU dispatch overhead and lowers inter-token latency (ITL) by 3–15% while simplifying engine maintenance |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **Extensible KV Cache**: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction. Why it matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.
- **Model Runner V2 (MRV2)**: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding. Why it matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.
- **Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)**: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass. Why it matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.
- **MLA & Sparse-MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention)**: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing. Why it matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.
- **NVFP4 / MXFP4 / FP8 Quantization**: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores. Why it matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.
- **P/D Disaggregation (Prefill/Decode Split & NIXL)**: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL. Why it matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.
- **DCP & PCP (Decode / Prefill Context Parallelism)**: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP). Why it matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.
- **MoE / MegaMoE & Expert Parallelism (EP / DeepGEMM)**: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs. Why it matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.
- **Piecewise & Breakable CUDA Graphs**: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token. Why it matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.
- **Tiered KV Offloading & Prefix Caching**: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts. Why it matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.
- **LibTorch Stable ABI**: Compiling vLLM's custom C++/CUDA kernels against PyTorch's binary-stable application interface rather than internal C++ symbols. Why it matters: Lets you upgrade PyTorch versions or security patches without rebuilding vLLM's entire CUDA kernel suite from source.

## 4. Should I Upgrade?
**Verdict**: UPGRADE WITH CONFIG CHECK — High-ROI throughput/stability gains, but review breaking flag/API removals first
- **Before You Upgrade**: Deprecate `JAISLMHeadModel` (#43784). -> Action: Check deprecation/removal impact before upgrading. ([#43784](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43784))
- **Before You Upgrade**: Begin the deprecation cycle for the NixlConnector `kv_both` role (#43874). -> Action: Check deprecation/removal impact before upgrading. ([#43874](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43874))
- **Before You Upgrade**: Remove functions previously scheduled for deprecation in v0.21.0 (#43358). -> Action: Check deprecation/removal impact before upgrading. ([#43358](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43358))
- **Security**: Parameter validation: Reject invalid `thinking_token_budget` values (#43402), non-positive `ParallelConfig` integer knobs (#44057), zero-valued config fields (#43794), and out-of-range. ([#43402](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43402), [#44057](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44057))
- **Security**: Untrusted-input hardening: Reject out-of-vocabulary token IDs before they reach the GPU logprob path (#44042) and fix a UTF-8 char-boundary panic in the Rust incremental detokenizer on malformed input. ([#44042](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44042), [#44620](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44620))
- **Security**: Transport encryption: SSL/TLS support for the data-parallel supervisor (#43688). ([#43688](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43688))

## 5. Technical Deep Dive (What's the Big Deal Under the Hood?)
### 1. Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups (DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3) ([#43361](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43361), [#43717](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43717), [#44013](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44013), [#44334](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44334))
- **Previously**: Prior to v0.23.0, teams operating frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA Blackwell (GB200/GB300/B200), Hopper (H100/H200), and multi-node Expert Parallel (EP) clusters.
- **Technical change**: torch stable ABI: Continued migration of kernels to the libtorch stable ABI — merge_attn_states/mamba/sampler [8/n] (#43361), attention/cache kernels [9/n] (#43717), header files (#44013) (#43361, #43717).
- **Technical change**: Model fixes & enhancements: Qwen3-VL/Qwen3-omni-thinker deepstack accuracy under `torch.compile` (#43617), EVS for Qwen3-VL (#44205), GLM-5.1 PP loading (#42944), GLM-4.1V processor logits (#43575) (#43617, #44205).
- **Technical change**: Attention & hybrid/Mamba: FlexAttention/FlashAttention num-blocks-first layouts (#42095), OOT MLA prefill backend registration (#43325), FlashAttention upstream sync (#44065), Mamba LINEAR (#42095, #43325).
- **Technical change**: Intel XPU: vllm-xpu-kernel v0.1.7 (#41019), `block_fp8_moe` (#42139), block-scaled W8A8 FP8 path (#39968), WNA16 oracle for GPTQ sym-int4 (#41426), rms_norm/act quant fusions (#43963), GDN-attention (#41019, #42139).
- **Operational impact**: Delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens
### 2. Low-Precision Quantization Kernels (NVFP4, MXFP4, MXFP8, FP8 & Humming) ([#38065](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38065), [#44220](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44220), [#43706](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43706), [#43014](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43014))
- **Previously**: Prior to v0.23.0, teams operating low-precision quantization kernels relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA Blackwell (SM100 NVFP4), Hopper (SM90 FP8), and AMD MI350/MI355X.
- **Technical change**: NVIDIA / kernels: FP8 FlashInfer attention for ViT (#38065), Triton MoE backend on Hopper by default (#44220), CUTLASS FP8 scaled-mm padding bypass (+20%) (#43706), MoE-permute buffer pre-allocation (#38065, #44220).
- **Technical change**: Kernels & backends: Triton W4A16 as CUDA fallback for non-Marlin-aligned shapes (#43731), Marlin MoE on SM 12.x (#40923), Machete W4A16 tests (#35450), fail-fast for unsupported NVFP4 KV-cache-dtype (#43731, #40923).
- **Technical change**: compressed-tensors: WNA8O8Int linears and WNInt embeddings (#44340), asymmetric MoE WNA16 Marlin (#44025), single-class NVFP4 linear refactor (#42443) (#44340, #44025).
- **Technical change**: MoE refactor (oracle): Migrated ModelOpt MXFP8 (#42768), W4A8-int8 (#42789), and WNA16 backend selection (#42553) into the modular-kernel oracle; removed `supports_expert_map` (#43108) and the (#42768, #42789).
- **Operational impact**: Halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput
### 3. Disaggregated Serving (P/D, DCP/PCP), Fault Tolerance & Fast Checkpoint/Restore ([#43720](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43720), [#44560](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44560), [#42554](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42554), [#43874](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43874))
- **Previously**: Prior to v0.23.0, teams operating disaggregated serving relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on Multi-node RDMA / InfiniBand / AWS EFA clusters and Kubernetes inference gateways.
- **Technical change**: KV connectors / disaggregated serving: PP-aware handshake aggregation and intermediate-PP output plumbing (#43720), multiple-async-KV-load deadlock fix (#44560), Nixl Mamba prefix-caching mode (#43720, #44560).
- **Technical change**: EPLB: Async EPLB by default (#43219), EPLB for DeepSeek-V4 Mega-MoE (#43339), Nixl zero-copy EPLB transfers (#41633) (#43219, #43339).
- **Technical change**: Begin the deprecation cycle for the NixlConnector `kv_both` role (#43874).
- **Technical change**: OpenAI / Responses API: `system_fingerprint` field (#40537), streaming tool/function calling with `required` (#40700), `chat_template_kwargs` in Responses (#43761), developer-to-system conversion in (#40537, #40700).
- **Operational impact**: Eliminates full-cluster restarts when a single GPU rank dies and cuts autoscaling cold-start time via CRIU restore

### 6. Extensible KV Cache, Memory Budgeting & Tiered Offloading ([#41968](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41968), [#41847](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41847), [#44287](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44287), [#43205](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43205))
- **Previously**: Prior to v0.23.0, teams operating extensible kv cache, memory budgeting & tiered offloading relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA Hopper (H100/H200), Blackwell (B200/GB200), and AMD Instinct (MI300X/MI355X) + host DRAM/NVMe tiers.
- **Technical change**: KV cache offloading: Object-store secondary tier (#41968), HMA on by default for capable connectors (#41847) and tiering (#44287), per-request offloading policy (`on_new_request`) (#43205) and (#41968, #41847).
- **Technical change**: KV cache & scheduler: Pluggable `KVCacheSpec` (#37505), `scheduler_block_size` threaded into KVCacheManager/Coordinator (#44165), `max_concurrent_batches` moved to `VllmConfig` (#44274), config (#37505, #44165).
- **Operational impact**: Expands effective KV capacity by 25–55% per GPU, serving more concurrent users per rack without adding hardware

high_level_changes.headline: Low-Precision Quantization Kernels
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.

high_level_changes.headline: Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.

high_level_changes.headline: Disaggregated Serving
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves disaggregated serving for planet-scale distributed inference clusters, serverless gpu autoscalers, and openai responses api clients running on multi-node rdma / infiniband / aws efa clusters and kubernetes inference gateways, delivering eliminates full-cluster restarts when a single GPU rank dies and cuts autoscaling cold-start time via CRIU restore.

high_level_changes.headline: Model Runner V2
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves model runner v2 for all production gpu deployments, latency-sensitive streaming apps, and custom logits processors running on all cuda and rocm gpu fleets running vllm's v2 execution engine, delivering cuts CPU dispatch overhead and lowers inter-token latency (ITL) by 3–15% while simplifying engine maintenance.

high_level_changes.headline: Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves multi-vendor accelerator scaling for cross-vendor llm fleets running deepseek, qwen, llama, and minimax outside cuda-only clouds running on amd instinct mi300x/mi350/mi355x (rocm 10.0), intel xpu, and google cloud tpu, delivering enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.

jargon_glossary.meaning: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.

jargon_glossary.term: Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)
jargon_glossary.meaning: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.

jargon_glossary.meaning: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP).
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.

jargon_glossary.term: TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)
jargon_glossary.meaning: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Compiling vLLM's custom C++/CUDA kernels against PyTorch's binary-stable application interface rather than internal C++ symbols.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Lets you upgrade PyTorch versions or security patches without rebuilding vLLM's entire CUDA kernel suite from source.

CPU / RISC-V: RVV-optimized attention kernels for RISC-V Vector Extension (#40119) with VLEN=256 (#42943), fused GDN for AMX CPU (#42707), MXFP4 W4A16 MoE (#41922), experimental Triton + MRv2 on CPU (#40119, #42943).

Intel XPU: GPTQ int4 support (#37844), mxfp8 MoE (#41918), FP8 block-scaled quantization (#42952), custom-op collective behavior (#41354), multiple sparse-attention kernels (#37888), MoE topk routing (#37844, #41918).

# What's New in vLLM v0.22.0

## High-Level Explanation
vLLM v0.22.0 focuses on Low-Precision Quantization Kernels, Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, and Disaggregated Serving. For operators, this release translates 50 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Low-Precision Quantization Kernels**: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.
- **Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups**: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.
- **Disaggregated Serving**: Improves disaggregated serving for planet-scale distributed inference clusters, serverless gpu autoscalers, and openai responses api clients running on multi-node rdma / infiniband / aws efa clusters and kubernetes inference gateways, delivering eliminates full-cluster restarts when a single GPU rank dies and cuts autoscaling cold-start time via CRIU restore.
- **Model Runner V2**: Improves model runner v2 for all production gpu deployments, latency-sensitive streaming apps, and custom logits processors running on all cuda and rocm gpu fleets running vllm's v2 execution engine, delivering cuts CPU dispatch overhead and lowers inter-token latency (ITL) by 3–15% while simplifying engine maintenance.
- **Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling**: Improves multi-vendor accelerator scaling for cross-vendor llm fleets running deepseek, qwen, llama, and minimax outside cuda-only clouds running on amd instinct mi300x/mi350/mi355x (rocm 10.0), intel xpu, and google cloud tpu, delivering enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)
| Workload / Team | Models / Services | GPUs / Hardware | Practical Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Low-Precision Quantization Kernels (NVFP4, MXFP4, MXFP8, FP8 & Humming)** | 100B–1T+ parameter models (Mistral Large 4, DeepSeek-V4, Qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit | NVIDIA Blackwell (SM100 NVFP4), Hopper (SM90 FP8), and AMD MI350/MI355X | Halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput |
| **Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups (DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3)** | Frontier Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) reasoning and agentic models (DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3/K3.1, MiniMax-M3.1) | NVIDIA Blackwell (GB200/GB300/B200), Hopper (H100/H200), and multi-node Expert Parallel (EP) clusters | Delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens |
| **Disaggregated Serving (P/D, DCP/PCP), Fault Tolerance & Fast Checkpoint/Restore** | Planet-scale distributed inference clusters, serverless GPU autoscalers, and OpenAI Responses API clients | Multi-node RDMA / InfiniBand / AWS EFA clusters and Kubernetes inference gateways | Eliminates full-cluster restarts when a single GPU rank dies and cuts autoscaling cold-start time via CRIU restore |
| **Model Runner V2 (MRV2) Consolidation & Breakable CUDA Graphs** | All production GPU deployments, latency-sensitive streaming apps, and custom logits processors | All CUDA and ROCm GPU fleets running vLLM's V2 execution engine | Cuts CPU dispatch overhead and lowers inter-token latency (ITL) by 3–15% while simplifying engine maintenance |
| **Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling (AMD ROCm 10 / MI355X, TPU & XPU)** | Cross-vendor LLM fleets running DeepSeek, Qwen, Llama, and MiniMax outside CUDA-only clouds | AMD Instinct MI300X/MI350/MI355X (ROCm 10.0), Intel XPU, and Google Cloud TPU | Enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code |
| **Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend** | Newly released foundation models, Vision-Language (VLM), Speech/ASR (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and Multi-LoRA adapters | Standard single-node and multi-node GPU inference pools | Consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet |
| **Deprecations & Removals Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **Extensible KV Cache**: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction. Why it matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.
- **Model Runner V2 (MRV2)**: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding. Why it matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.
- **Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)**: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass. Why it matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.
- **MLA & Sparse-MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention)**: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing. Why it matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.
- **NVFP4 / MXFP4 / FP8 Quantization**: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores. Why it matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.
- **P/D Disaggregation (Prefill/Decode Split & NIXL)**: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL. Why it matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.
- **DCP & PCP (Decode / Prefill Context Parallelism)**: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP). Why it matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.
- **MoE / MegaMoE & Expert Parallelism (EP / DeepGEMM)**: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs. Why it matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.
- **Piecewise & Breakable CUDA Graphs**: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token. Why it matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.
- **TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)**: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream. Why it matters: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.
- **Tiered KV Offloading & Prefix Caching**: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts. Why it matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.
- **LibTorch Stable ABI**: Compiling vLLM's custom C++/CUDA kernels against PyTorch's binary-stable application interface rather than internal C++ symbols. Why it matters: Lets you upgrade PyTorch versions or security patches without rebuilding vLLM's entire CUDA kernel suite from source.

## 4. Should I Upgrade?
**Verdict**: UPGRADE WITH CONFIG CHECK — High-ROI throughput/stability gains, but review breaking flag/API removals first
