should_i_upgrade.text: DRA ResourceSlice controller: Added optional `ReconcilePoolWithName` to allow per-pool reconciliation without setting `NodeName` on slices, so the scheduler can use `NodeSelector` or `allNodes` for node-owned, cluster-visible resources (e.g. network-shared devices). "All nodes" is no longer the default. When publishing devices for the entire cluster, it must be set explicitly. ([#137365](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137365), [@yaroslavborbat](https://github.com/yaroslavborbat)) [SIG Node and Testing]

Client-go: Default informer behavior now updates store state with all the objects in a list or relist before calling handler `OnDelete`, `OnAdd`, or `OnUpdate` methods for individual items which were deleted, added, or removed. This ensures that the store state which can be inspected by handlers corresponds to a set of objects that existed at a particular resource version on the server. This behavior is guarded by the `AtomicFIFO` feature gate, which is enabled by default in `v1.36` but can be disabled if needed to temporarily regain the previous behavior. ([#135462](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135462), [@michaelasp](https://github.com/michaelasp)) [SIG API Machinery]

Added the PlacementScore extension point to the scheduler for scoring placements in placement-based PodGroup scheduling, guarded by the `TopologyAwareWorkloadScheduling` feature gate. Deprecated `MinNodeScore` and `MaxNodeScore` in favor of `MinScore` and `MaxScore`. ([#137201](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137201), [@brejman](https://github.com/brejman)) [SIG Scheduling]

Removed the in-tree Portworx volume plugin, completing the migration to CSI. Removed the GA `CSIMigrationPortworx` feature gate (locked since `v1.33`) and alpha `InTreePluginPortworxUnregister` feature gate, with all operations now redirected to CSI. ([#135322](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135322), [@carlory](https://github.com/carlory)) [SIG API Machinery, Apps, Auth, Node, Scalability, Scheduling, Storage and Testing]
sigs: API Machinery, Apps, Auth, Node, Scalability, Scheduling, Storage and Testing

kubernetes_guides.markdown:
# What's New in Kubernetes v1.36

## High-Level Explanation
Kubernetes v1.36 focuses on Dynamic Resource Allocation, Feature Enhancements, and Workload-Aware & Gang Scheduling. For operators, this release translates 347 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Dynamic Resource Allocation**: Improves dynamic resource allocation for ai/ml training, llm inference pods, fractional/multi-gpu workloads, and nic/fpga consumers running on nvidia/amd gpu nodes, multi-nic rdma clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools, delivering higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting.
- **Feature Enhancements**: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **Workload-Aware & Gang Scheduling**: Improves workload-aware & gang scheduling for distributed ai training, multi-node batch jobs, ray/spark clusters, and mpi workloads running on high-density gpu/cpu batch pools and `kube-scheduler` queues, delivering prevents partial-allocation deadlocks where expensive GPU nodes sit idle waiting for peer workers.
- **API Change Enhancements**: Improves api change enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale**: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)
| Workload / Team | Models / Services | GPUs / Hardware | Practical Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) & GPU/Accelerator Management** | AI/ML training, LLM inference pods, fractional/multi-GPU workloads, and NIC/FPGA consumers | NVIDIA/AMD GPU nodes, multi-NIC RDMA clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools | Higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting |
| **Feature Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **Workload-Aware & Gang Scheduling (`PodGroup` / `Job` / Queueing)** | Distributed AI training, multi-node batch jobs, Ray/Spark clusters, and MPI workloads | High-density GPU/CPU batch pools and `kube-scheduler` queues | Prevents partial-allocation deadlocks where expensive GPU nodes sit idle waiting for peer workers |
| **API Change Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale** | Operator-heavy platforms, Argo CD / Flux GitOps controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ CRDs/Pods | Control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) CPU and memory footprint | Cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages |
| **CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies** | Platform security guardrails, multi-tenant compliance policies, and default resource injectors | In-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments) | Removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts |
| **In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling (Zero-Restart Resource Resize)** | Stateful microservices, warm inference engines, JVMs, and suspended Batch Jobs needing CPU/RAM adjustments | Linux worker nodes and kubelet resource allocation loops | Eliminates over-provisioning buffer and avoids expensive pod restart cold-starts during traffic spikes |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **DRA (Dynamic Resource Allocation)**: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins. Why it matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.
- **In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling (Resize)**: Changing a running Pod's CPU or memory requests/limits dynamically without killing and recreating the container. Why it matters: Eliminates cold-start restarts and dropped connections when scaling stateful services, databases, or warm AI model servers.
- **Gang Scheduling (`Workload` / `PodGroup`)**: An 'all-or-nothing' scheduling guarantee where a group of cooperating Pods (like a multi-node training or distributed inference job) only starts when capacity exists for the entire group. Why it matters: Prevents expensive GPUs from sitting idle in deadlocked partial allocations when a cluster is near capacity.
- **Native Sidecar Containers (`initContainers` with `restartPolicy: Always`)**: First-class lifecycle support for helper containers (log shippers, service mesh proxies) so they start before the main app and terminate automatically after Batch Jobs finish. Why it matters: Fixes the classic Kubernetes bug where a finished Job hangs forever because an Istio/Envoy sidecar stays alive.
- **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy & MutatingAdmissionPolicy (CEL)**: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers. Why it matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.
- **Linux User Namespaces (`hostUsers: false`)**: Maps the `root` user inside a container to an unprivileged non-root UID on the host node kernel. Why it matters: Dramatically reduces container-escape blast radius even for legacy workloads that require running as `root` inside the container.
- **WatchList & Snapshottable Watch Cache**: Streaming object lists from `kube-apiserver` memory cache snapshots instead of assembling giant one-shot payloads from `etcd`. Why it matters: Slashes API server RAM spikes and protects `etcd` from OOM crashes during controller restarts on large clusters.
- **nftables `kube-proxy` Backend**: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains. Why it matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.
- **HPA Scale-to-Zero (`minReplicas: 0`)**: Allows `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` to scale external/queue-driven workloads all the way down to 0 replicas when idle and wake them when queue depth rises. Why it matters: Directly cuts cloud compute and GPU bills for bursty batch/inference workers during off-peak hours.
- **CSI (Container Storage Interface)**: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers. Why it matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.

high_level_changes.headline: Dynamic Resource Allocation
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves dynamic resource allocation for ai/ml training, llm inference pods, fractional/multi-gpu workloads, and nic/fpga consumers running on nvidia/amd gpu nodes, multi-nic rdma clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools, delivering higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting.

high_level_changes.headline: API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.

high_level_changes.headline: Feature Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

high_level_changes.headline: Workload-Aware & Gang Scheduling
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves workload-aware & gang scheduling for distributed ai training, multi-node batch jobs, ray/spark clusters, and mpi workloads running on high-density gpu/cpu batch pools and `kube-scheduler` queues, delivering prevents partial-allocation deadlocks where expensive GPU nodes sit idle waiting for peer workers.

high_level_changes.headline: API Change Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves api change enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Changing a running Pod's CPU or memory requests/limits dynamically without killing and recreating the container.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates cold-start restarts and dropped connections when scaling stateful services, databases, or warm AI model servers.

jargon_glossary.meaning: An 'all-or-nothing' scheduling guarantee where a group of cooperating Pods (like a multi-node training or distributed inference job) only starts when capacity exists for the entire group.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Prevents expensive GPUs from sitting idle in deadlocked partial allocations when a cluster is near capacity.

jargon_glossary.meaning: First-class lifecycle support for helper containers (log shippers, service mesh proxies) so they start before the main app and terminate automatically after Batch Jobs finish.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Fixes the classic Kubernetes bug where a finished Job hangs forever because an Istio/Envoy sidecar stays alive.

jargon_glossary.meaning: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Maps the `root` user inside a container to an unprivileged non-root UID on the host node kernel.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically reduces container-escape blast radius even for legacy workloads that require running as `root` inside the container.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Streaming object lists from `kube-apiserver` memory cache snapshots instead of assembling giant one-shot payloads from `etcd`.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes API server RAM spikes and protects `etcd` from OOM crashes during controller restarts on large clusters.

jargon_glossary.meaning: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Built-in kubelet provisioning and rotation of X.509 mTLS identity certificates directly into Pods without third-party sidecars.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Simplifies zero-trust pod-to-pod mTLS without managing complex external webhook/cert-manager plumbing.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Allows `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` to scale external/queue-driven workloads all the way down to 0 replicas when idle and wake them when queue depth rises.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Directly cuts cloud compute and GPU bills for bursty batch/inference workers during off-peak hours.

jargon_glossary.meaning: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.

should_i_upgrade.text: ACTION REQUIRED: Removed the `--pod-infra-container-image` flag from `kubelet` command line. For `non-kubeadm` clusters, users must manually remove this flag from their `kubelet` configuration to prevent startup failures before upgrading `kubelet`. For `kubeadm` clusters, if users pass extra arguments to the `kubelet` like `--pod-infra-container-image`, it will be written to the `kubelet` env file during the `init` phase. `kubeadm` does not remove it during the `init` or `join` phase, so users must manually remove it from `extraArgs` in the `kubelet` configuration file. ([#133779](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133779), [@carlory](https://github.com/carlory))

ACTION REQUIRED: vendor: Updated `k8s.io/system-validators` to `v1.12.1`. The cgroups validator now throws an error instead of a warning if cgroups v1 is detected on the host and the provided KubeletVersion is `v1.35` or newer. kubeadm: Started using `k8s.io/system-validators` `v1.12.1` in `kubeadm` `v1.35`. During `kubeadm init`, `kubeadm join`, and `kubeadm upgrade`, the SystemVerification preflight check throws an error if cgroups v1 is detected and the detected `kubelet` version is `v1.35` or newer. For older versions of `kubelet`, a preflight warning is displayed. To allow cgroups v1 with `kubeadm` and `kubelet` version `v1.35` or newer, you must:
Ignore the error from the SystemVerification preflight check by `kubeadm`.

Edit the `kube-system/kubelet-config` ConfigMap and add the `failCgroupV1: false` field before upgrading. ([#134744](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134744), [@neolit123](https://github.com/neolit123)) [SIG Cluster Lifecycle and Node]

ACTION REQUIRED: `failCgroupV1` will be set to true from 1.35. This means that nodes will not start on a cgroup v1 by default. This puts cgroup v1 into a deprecated state. ([#134298](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134298), [@kannon92](https://github.com/kannon92))

Marked `ipvs` mode in kube-proxy as deprecated, which will be removed in a future version of Kubernetes. Users are encouraged to migrate to `nftables`. ([#134539](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134539), [@adrianmoisey](https://github.com/adrianmoisey))

Promoted the `JobManagedBy` feature to general availability. The `JobManagedBy` feature gate was locked to `true` and will be removed in a future Kubernetes release. ([#135080](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135080), [@dejanzele](https://github.com/dejanzele)) [SIG API Machinery, Apps and Testing]

Kubeadm: Graduated the kubeadm-specific feature gate `ControlPlaneKubeletLocalMode` to GA and locked it to enabled by default. To opt out, patch the `server` field in `/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf`. Deprecated the subphase of `kubeadm join phase control-plane-join` called `etcd`, which is now hidden and replaced by subphase with identical functionality `etcd-join`. The `etcd` subphase will be removed in a future release. The subphase `kubelet-wait-bootstrap` of `kubeadm join` is no longer experimental and will now always run. ([#134106](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134106), [@neolit123](https://github.com/neolit123))

Promoted the `EnvFiles` feature gate to beta and is enabled by default. Additionally, the syntax specification for environment variables has been restricted to a subset of POSIX shell syntax (all variable values must be wrapped in single quotes). ([#134414](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134414), [@HirazawaUi](https://github.com/HirazawaUi)) [SIG Node and Testing]

The `PreferSameZone` and `PreferSameNode` values for the Service `trafficDistribution` field graduated to general availability. The `PreferClose` value is now deprecated in favor of the more explicit `PreferSameZone`. ([#134457](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134457), [@danwinship](https://github.com/danwinship)) [SIG API Machinery, Apps, Network and Testing]
sigs: API Machinery, Apps, Network and Testing

technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v1.35, teams operating dynamic resource allocation relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA/AMD GPU nodes, multi-NIC RDMA clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools.
tech_bullets: DRA: The `DynamicResourceAllocation` feature gate for the core functionality (GA in `v1.34`) has now been locked to enabled-by-default and cannot be disabled anymore. (#134452).

The `PreferSameZone` and `PreferSameNode` values for the Service `trafficDistribution` field graduated to general availability. The `PreferClose` value is now deprecated in favor of the more explicit (#134457).

The DRA device taints and toleration feature received a separate feature gate, `DRADeviceTaintRules`, which controlled support for `DeviceTaintRules`. This allowed disabling it while keeping (#135068).

DRA device taints: `DeviceTaintRule` status provides information about the rule, including whether Pods still need to be evicted (`EvictionInProgress` condition). The newly added `None` effect can be (#134152).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting

tech_bullets: Kube-apiserver: Made the subresources `pods/exec`, `pods/attach`, and `pods/portforward` require `create` permission for both SPDY and Websocket API requests. Previously, SPDY requests required (#134577).

The Pod Certificates feature moved to beta. The `PodCertificateRequest` feature gate is set disabled by default. To use the feature, users must enable the certificates API groups in `v1beta1` and (#134624).

Added the `StorageVersionMigration` `v1beta1` API and removed the `v1alpha1` API. ACTION REQUIRED: The `v1alpha1` API is no longer supported. Users must remove any `v1alpha1` resources before (#134784).

# What's New in Kubernetes v1.35

## High-Level Explanation
Kubernetes v1.35 focuses on Dynamic Resource Allocation, API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale, and Feature Enhancements. For operators, this release translates 259 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Dynamic Resource Allocation**: Improves dynamic resource allocation for ai/ml training, llm inference pods, fractional/multi-gpu workloads, and nic/fpga consumers running on nvidia/amd gpu nodes, multi-nic rdma clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools, delivering higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting.
- **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale**: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.
- **Feature Enhancements**: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **Workload-Aware & Gang Scheduling**: Improves workload-aware & gang scheduling for distributed ai training, multi-node batch jobs, ray/spark clusters, and mpi workloads running on high-density gpu/cpu batch pools and `kube-scheduler` queues, delivering prevents partial-allocation deadlocks where expensive GPU nodes sit idle waiting for peer workers.
- **API Change Enhancements**: Improves api change enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)
| Workload / Team | Models / Services | GPUs / Hardware | Practical Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) & GPU/Accelerator Management** | AI/ML training, LLM inference pods, fractional/multi-GPU workloads, and NIC/FPGA consumers | NVIDIA/AMD GPU nodes, multi-NIC RDMA clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools | Higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting |
| **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale** | Operator-heavy platforms, Argo CD / Flux GitOps controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ CRDs/Pods | Control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) CPU and memory footprint | Cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages |
| **Feature Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **Workload-Aware & Gang Scheduling (`PodGroup` / `Job` / Queueing)** | Distributed AI training, multi-node batch jobs, Ray/Spark clusters, and MPI workloads | High-density GPU/CPU batch pools and `kube-scheduler` queues | Prevents partial-allocation deadlocks where expensive GPU nodes sit idle waiting for peer workers |
| **API Change Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies** | Platform security guardrails, multi-tenant compliance policies, and default resource injectors | In-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments) | Removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts |
| **Native Sidecar Containers, Checkpoint/Restore & Node Lifecycle** | Service-mesh pods, telemetry agents, fast-restoring stateful apps, and OCI artifact mounts | Kubelet CRI runtime (containerd / CRI-O) and Linux/Windows worker nodes | Stops zombie sidecars from holding batch nodes open after job completion |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **DRA (Dynamic Resource Allocation)**: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins. Why it matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.
- **In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling (Resize)**: Changing a running Pod's CPU or memory requests/limits dynamically without killing and recreating the container. Why it matters: Eliminates cold-start restarts and dropped connections when scaling stateful services, databases, or warm AI model servers.
- **Gang Scheduling (`Workload` / `PodGroup`)**: An 'all-or-nothing' scheduling guarantee where a group of cooperating Pods (like a multi-node training or distributed inference job) only starts when capacity exists for the entire group. Why it matters: Prevents expensive GPUs from sitting idle in deadlocked partial allocations when a cluster is near capacity.
- **Native Sidecar Containers (`initContainers` with `restartPolicy: Always`)**: First-class lifecycle support for helper containers (log shippers, service mesh proxies) so they start before the main app and terminate automatically after Batch Jobs finish. Why it matters: Fixes the classic Kubernetes bug where a finished Job hangs forever because an Istio/Envoy sidecar stays alive.
- **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy & MutatingAdmissionPolicy (CEL)**: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers. Why it matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.
- **Linux User Namespaces (`hostUsers: false`)**: Maps the `root` user inside a container to an unprivileged non-root UID on the host node kernel. Why it matters: Dramatically reduces container-escape blast radius even for legacy workloads that require running as `root` inside the container.
- **WatchList & Snapshottable Watch Cache**: Streaming object lists from `kube-apiserver` memory cache snapshots instead of assembling giant one-shot payloads from `etcd`. Why it matters: Slashes API server RAM spikes and protects `etcd` from OOM crashes during controller restarts on large clusters.
- **nftables `kube-proxy` Backend**: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains. Why it matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.
- **Pod Certificates (`PodCertificateRequest`)**: Built-in kubelet provisioning and rotation of X.509 mTLS identity certificates directly into Pods without third-party sidecars. Why it matters: Simplifies zero-trust pod-to-pod mTLS without managing complex external webhook/cert-manager plumbing.
- **HPA Scale-to-Zero (`minReplicas: 0`)**: Allows `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` to scale external/queue-driven workloads all the way down to 0 replicas when idle and wake them when queue depth rises. Why it matters: Directly cuts cloud compute and GPU bills for bursty batch/inference workers during off-peak hours.
- **CSI (Container Storage Interface)**: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers. Why it matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.

high_level_changes.headline: Dynamic Resource Allocation
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves dynamic resource allocation for ai/ml training, llm inference pods, fractional/multi-gpu workloads, and nic/fpga consumers running on nvidia/amd gpu nodes, multi-nic rdma clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools, delivering higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting.

high_level_changes.headline: API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.

high_level_changes.headline: Feature Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

high_level_changes.headline: API Change Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves api change enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

high_level_changes.headline: Networking, `nftables` Proxy & Traffic Observability
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves networking, `nftables` proxy & traffic observability for high-throughput east-west microservices and latency-sensitive ingress traffic running on linux dataplane (`nftables`/`ipvs`) and cloud load balancers, delivering lowers cross-AZ data transfer costs (`trafficDistribution`) and reduces node CPU spent on iptables rules.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Changing a running Pod's CPU or memory requests/limits dynamically without killing and recreating the container.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates cold-start restarts and dropped connections when scaling stateful services, databases, or warm AI model servers.

jargon_glossary.meaning: First-class lifecycle support for helper containers (log shippers, service mesh proxies) so they start before the main app and terminate automatically after Batch Jobs finish.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Fixes the classic Kubernetes bug where a finished Job hangs forever because an Istio/Envoy sidecar stays alive.

jargon_glossary.meaning: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Maps the `root` user inside a container to an unprivileged non-root UID on the host node kernel.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically reduces container-escape blast radius even for legacy workloads that require running as `root` inside the container.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Streaming object lists from `kube-apiserver` memory cache snapshots instead of assembling giant one-shot payloads from `etcd`.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes API server RAM spikes and protects `etcd` from OOM crashes during controller restarts on large clusters.

jargon_glossary.meaning: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Built-in kubelet provisioning and rotation of X.509 mTLS identity certificates directly into Pods without third-party sidecars.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Simplifies zero-trust pod-to-pod mTLS without managing complex external webhook/cert-manager plumbing.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Allows `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` to scale external/queue-driven workloads all the way down to 0 replicas when idle and wake them when queue depth rises.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Directly cuts cloud compute and GPU bills for bursty batch/inference workers during off-peak hours.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Concise Binary Object Representation (RFC 8949) as a compact binary alternative to JSON for Kubernetes API client-server serialization.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Reduces API server CPU spent on JSON parsing and lowers network bandwidth for custom resources (CRDs) that couldn't use Protobuf.

jargon_glossary.meaning: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.

should_i_upgrade.text: For metrics `apiserver_cache_list_fetched_objects_total`, `apiserver_cache_list_returned_objects_total`, `apiserver_cache_list_total` replace `resource_prefix` label with API `group` and `resource` labels. kubernetes_guides.markdown:
# What's New in Kubernetes v1.34

## High-Level Explanation
Kubernetes v1.34 focuses on Dynamic Resource Allocation, API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale, and Feature Enhancements. For operators, this release translates 333 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Dynamic Resource Allocation**: Improves dynamic resource allocation for ai/ml training, llm inference pods, fractional/multi-gpu workloads, and nic/fpga consumers running on nvidia/amd gpu nodes, multi-nic rdma clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools, delivering higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting.
- **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale**: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.
- **Feature Enhancements**: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **API Change Enhancements**: Improves api change enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **Networking, `nftables` Proxy & Traffic Observability**: Improves networking, `nftables` proxy & traffic observability for high-throughput east-west microservices and latency-sensitive ingress traffic running on linux dataplane (`nftables`/`ipvs`) and cloud load balancers, delivering lowers cross-AZ data transfer costs (`trafficDistribution`) and reduces node CPU spent on iptables rules.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)
| Workload / Team | Models / Services | GPUs / Hardware | Practical Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) & GPU/Accelerator Management** | AI/ML training, LLM inference pods, fractional/multi-GPU workloads, and NIC/FPGA consumers | NVIDIA/AMD GPU nodes, multi-NIC RDMA clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools | Higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting |
| **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale** | Operator-heavy platforms, Argo CD / Flux GitOps controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ CRDs/Pods | Control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) CPU and memory footprint | Cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages |
| **Feature Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **API Change Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **Networking, `nftables` Proxy & Traffic Observability** | High-throughput east-west microservices and latency-sensitive ingress traffic | Linux dataplane (`nftables`/`ipvs`) and cloud load balancers | Lowers cross-AZ data transfer costs (`trafficDistribution`) and reduces node CPU spent on iptables rules |
| **Workload Identity, User Namespaces & Fine-Grained Authz** | Multi-tenant SaaS workloads, zero-trust service meshes, and privileged container migrations | Linux kernel namespaces, kubelet endpoints, and CSI secret injection paths | Reduces security agent/sidecar overhead and shrinks blast radius of container compromises |
| **Native Sidecar Containers, Checkpoint/Restore & Node Lifecycle** | Service-mesh pods, telemetry agents, fast-restoring stateful apps, and OCI artifact mounts | Kubelet CRI runtime (containerd / CRI-O) and Linux/Windows worker nodes | Stops zombie sidecars from holding batch nodes open after job completion |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **DRA (Dynamic Resource Allocation)**: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins. Why it matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.
- **In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling (Resize)**: Changing a running Pod's CPU or memory requests/limits dynamically without killing and recreating the container. Why it matters: Eliminates cold-start restarts and dropped connections when scaling stateful services, databases, or warm AI model servers.
- **Native Sidecar Containers (`initContainers` with `restartPolicy: Always`)**: First-class lifecycle support for helper containers (log shippers, service mesh proxies) so they start before the main app and terminate automatically after Batch Jobs finish. Why it matters: Fixes the classic Kubernetes bug where a finished Job hangs forever because an Istio/Envoy sidecar stays alive.
- **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy & MutatingAdmissionPolicy (CEL)**: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers. Why it matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.
- **Linux User Namespaces (`hostUsers: false`)**: Maps the `root` user inside a container to an unprivileged non-root UID on the host node kernel. Why it matters: Dramatically reduces container-escape blast radius even for legacy workloads that require running as `root` inside the container.
- **WatchList & Snapshottable Watch Cache**: Streaming object lists from `kube-apiserver` memory cache snapshots instead of assembling giant one-shot payloads from `etcd`. Why it matters: Slashes API server RAM spikes and protects `etcd` from OOM crashes during controller restarts on large clusters.
- **nftables `kube-proxy` Backend**: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains. Why it matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.
- **Pod Certificates (`PodCertificateRequest`)**: Built-in kubelet provisioning and rotation of X.509 mTLS identity certificates directly into Pods without third-party sidecars. Why it matters: Simplifies zero-trust pod-to-pod mTLS without managing complex external webhook/cert-manager plumbing.
- **HPA Scale-to-Zero (`minReplicas: 0`)**: Allows `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` to scale external/queue-driven workloads all the way down to 0 replicas when idle and wake them when queue depth rises. Why it matters: Directly cuts cloud compute and GPU bills for bursty batch/inference workers during off-peak hours.
- **CBOR Encoding for Kubernetes API**: Concise Binary Object Representation (RFC 8949) as a compact binary alternative to JSON for Kubernetes API client-server serialization. Why it matters: Reduces API server CPU spent on JSON parsing and lowers network bandwidth for custom resources (CRDs) that couldn't use Protobuf.
- **CSI (Container Storage Interface)**: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers. Why it matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.

kubernetes_guides.positioning: Kubernetes v1.33 focuses on Native Sidecar Containers, Checkpoint/Restore & Node Lifecycle, API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale, and In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling. high_level_changes.headline: Native Sidecar Containers, Checkpoint/Restore & Node Lifecycle
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves native sidecar containers, checkpoint/restore & node lifecycle for service-mesh pods, telemetry agents, fast-restoring stateful apps, and oci artifact mounts running on kubelet cri runtime (containerd / cri-o) and linux/windows worker nodes, delivering stops zombie sidecars from holding batch nodes open after job completion.

high_level_changes.headline: API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.

high_level_changes.headline: In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves in-place pod vertical scaling for stateful microservices, warm inference engines, jvms, and suspended batch jobs needing cpu/ram adjustments running on linux worker nodes and kubelet resource allocation loops, delivering eliminates over-provisioning buffer and avoids expensive pod restart cold-starts during traffic spikes.

high_level_changes.headline: Feature Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

high_level_changes.headline: CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves cel-based validating & mutating admission policies for platform security guardrails, multi-tenant compliance policies, and default resource injectors running on in-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments), delivering removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Changing a running Pod's CPU or memory requests/limits dynamically without killing and recreating the container.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates cold-start restarts and dropped connections when scaling stateful services, databases, or warm AI model servers.

jargon_glossary.meaning: First-class lifecycle support for helper containers (log shippers, service mesh proxies) so they start before the main app and terminate automatically after Batch Jobs finish.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Fixes the classic Kubernetes bug where a finished Job hangs forever because an Istio/Envoy sidecar stays alive.

jargon_glossary.meaning: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Maps the `root` user inside a container to an unprivileged non-root UID on the host node kernel.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically reduces container-escape blast radius even for legacy workloads that require running as `root` inside the container.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Streaming object lists from `kube-apiserver` memory cache snapshots instead of assembling giant one-shot payloads from `etcd`.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes API server RAM spikes and protects `etcd` from OOM crashes during controller restarts on large clusters.

jargon_glossary.meaning: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Allows `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` to scale external/queue-driven workloads all the way down to 0 replicas when idle and wake them when queue depth rises.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Directly cuts cloud compute and GPU bills for bursty batch/inference workers during off-peak hours.

jargon_glossary.meaning: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.

should_i_upgrade.text: Added the ability to reduce both the initial delay and the maximum delay accrued between container restarts for a node for containers in `CrashLoopBackOff` across the cluster to the recommended values of `1s` initial delay and `60s` maximum delay. To set this for a node, turn on the feature gate `ReduceDefaultCrashLoopBackOffDecay`. If you are also using the feature gate `KubeletCrashLoopBackOffMax` with a configured per-node `CrashLoopBackOff.MaxContainerRestartPeriod`, the effective kubelet configuration will follow the conflict resolution policy described further in the documentation [here](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle/#reduced-container-restart-delay). ([#130711](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130711), [@lauralorenz](https://github.com/lauralorenz)) [SIG Node and Testing]

[Action Required] CSI drivers that call IsLikelyNotMountPoint should not assume false means that the path is a mount point. Each CSI driver needs to make sure correct usage of return value of IsLikelyNotMountPoint because if the file is an irregular file but not a mount point is acceptable ([#129370](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129370), [@andyzhangx](https://github.com/andyzhangx)) [SIG Storage and Windows]

Fixed the behavior of the `KUBE_PROXY_NFTABLES_SKIP_KERNEL_VERSION_CHECK` environment variable in the nftables proxier. The kernel version check is now skipped only when this variable is explicitly set to a non-empty value. To skip the check, set the `KUBE_PROXY_NFTABLES_SKIP_KERNEL_VERSION_CHECK` environment variable. ([#130401](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130401), [@ryota-sakamoto](https://github.com/ryota-sakamoto))

Renamed `UpdatePodTolerations` action type to `UpdatePodToleration`. Action required for custom plugin developers to update their code to follow the rename. ([#129023](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129023), [@zhifei92](https://github.com/zhifei92)) [SIG Scheduling and Testing]

The EndpointSlice `hints` field has graduated to GA. The beta annotation `service.kubernetes.io/topology-mode` is now considered deprecated and will not graduate to GA. It remains operational for backward compatibility. Users are encouraged to use the `spec.trafficDistribution` field in the Service API for topology-aware routing configuration. ([#130742](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130742), [@gauravkghildiyal](https://github.com/gauravkghildiyal)) [SIG Network]

The `StorageCapacityScoring` feature gate was added to score nodes by available storage capacity. It's in alpha and disabled by default. The `VolumeCapacityPriority` alpha feature was replaced with this, and the default behavior was changed. The `VolumeCapacityPriority` preferred a node with the least allocatable, but the `StorageCapacityScoring` preferred a node with the maximum allocatable. See [KEP-4049](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-storage/4049-storage-capacity-scoring-of-nodes-for-dynamic-provisioning/README.md) for details. ([#128184](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128184), [@cupnes](https://github.com/cupnes)) [SIG Scheduling, Storage and Testing]

The `WatchFromStorageWithoutResourceVersion` feature was deprecated and can no longer be enabled. ([#129930](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129930), [@serathius](https://github.com/serathius))

The pod `status.resize` field is now deprecated and will no longer be set. The status of a pod resize will be exposed under two new conditions: `PodResizeInProgress` and `PodResizePending` instead. ([#130733](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130733), [@natasha41575](https://github.com/natasha41575)) [SIG API Machinery, Apps, CLI, Node, Scheduling and Testing]
sigs: API Machinery, Apps, CLI, Node, Scheduling and Testing

should_i_upgrade.text: The v1 Endpoints API is now officially deprecated (though still fully supported). The API will not be removed, but all users should use the EndpointSlice API instead. ([#130098](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130098), [@danwinship](https://github.com/danwinship)) [SIG API Machinery and Network]

technical_deep_dive.theme: Native Sidecar Containers, Checkpoint/Restore & Node Lifecycle
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v1.33, teams operating native sidecar containers, checkpoint/restore & node lifecycle relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on Kubelet CRI runtime (containerd / CRI-O) and Linux/Windows worker nodes.
tech_bullets: The `SidecarContainers` feature has graduated to GA. 'SidecarContainers' feature gate was locked to default value and will be removed in v1.36. If you were setting this feature gate explicitly (#129731).

Introduced the `LegacySidecarContainers` feature gate enabling the legacy code path that predates the `SidecarContainers` feature. This temporary feature gate is disabled by default, only available (#130058).
Graduated image volume sources to beta:.
kubectl: Added alpha support for customizing kubectl behavior using preferences from a `kuberc` file, separate from `kubeconfig`. ([#125230](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/125230).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Stops zombie sidecars from holding batch nodes open after job completion

technical_deep_dive.theme: API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v1.33, teams operating api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on Control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) CPU and memory footprint.
tech_bullets: The `RemoteRequestHeaderUID` feature moves to beta and is now enabled by default. This makes the kube-apiserver propagate UIDs in the `X-Remote-Uid` header in requests to the aggregated API servers. (#130560).
kubeadm: removed the feature gate EtcdLearnerMode which graduated to GA in 1.32. ([#129589](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129589), [@neolit123](https://github.com/neolit123)) [SIG.
Graduated `BtreeWatchCache` feature gate to GA. ([#129934](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129934), [@serathius](https://github.com/serathius)).
kube-apiserver: Promoted the  `ServiceAccountTokenNodeBinding` feature gate general availability. It is now locked to enabled. ([#129591](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129591).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages

technical_deep_dive.theme: In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling (Zero-Restart Resource Resize)
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v1.33, teams operating in-place pod vertical scaling relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on Linux worker nodes and kubelet resource allocation loops.
tech_bullets: Promoted in-place Pod vertical scaling to beta. The `InPlacePodVerticalScaling` feature gate is now enabled by default. ([#130905](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130905).
For the `InPlacePodVerticalScaling` feature, the API server will no longer set the resize status to `Proposed` upon receiving a resize request. (#130574).

The feature gate `InPlacePodVerticalScalingAllocatedStatus` is deprecated and no longer used. The `AllocatedResources` field in `ContainerStatus` is now guarded by the `InPlacePodVerticalScaling` (#130880).
InPlacePodVerticalScaling: Memory limits cannot be decreased unless the memory resize restart policy is set to `RestartContainer`. Container resizePolicy is no longer mutable. (#130183).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Eliminates over-provisioning buffer and avoids expensive pod restart cold-starts during traffic spikes

technical_deep_dive.theme: Feature Enhancements
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v1.33, teams operating feature enhancements relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on Standard cluster nodes and runtime components.
tech_bullets: Graduated the `DisableNodeKubeProxyVersion` feature gate to enable by default, the kubelet no longer attempts to set the `.status.kubeProxyVersion` field for its associated Node. (#129713).

The `DeclarativeValidation` feature gate is enabled by default. When enabled, mismatches with existing hand written validation is reported via metrics. The `DeclarativeValidationTakeover` feature (#130728).

Added `SchedulerPopFromBackoffQ` feature gate that is in beta and enabled by default. Improved scheduling queue behavior by popping pods from the backoffQ when the activeQ is empty. This allows to (#130772).
Bumped `ProcMountType` feature to on by default beta ([#130798](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130798), [@haircommander](https://github.com/haircommander)) [SIG Node].
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil

technical_deep_dive.theme: CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v1.33, teams operating cel-based validating & mutating admission policies relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on In-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments).
tech_bullets: Graduated the `MultiCIDRServiceAllocator` feature gate to stable, and the `DisableAllocatorDualWrite` feature gate to beta (disabled by default). Action required for Kubernetes cluster administrators (#128971).
Added unit test helpers to validate CEL and patterns in CustomResourceDefinitions. ([#129028](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129028), [@sttts](https://github.com/sttts)).
`cel-go` has been bumped to `v0.23.2`. ([#129844](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129844), [@cici37](https://github.com/cici37)) [SIG API Machinery, Auth, Cloud Provider and Node].
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts

technical_deep_dive.theme: Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) & GPU/Accelerator Management
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v1.33, teams operating dynamic resource allocation relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA/AMD GPU nodes, multi-NIC RDMA clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools.
tech_bullets: `DRAResourceClaimDeviceStatus` is now turned on by default allowing DRA-Drivers to report device status data for each allocated device. (#130814).

The EndpointSlice `hints` field has graduated to GA. The beta annotation `service.kubernetes.io/topology-mode` is now considered deprecated and will not graduate to GA. It remains operational for (#130742).
Added feature gate `DRAPartitionableDevices`, when enabled, Dynamic Resource Allocation support partitionable devices allocation. ([#130764](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130764).

kubelet + DRA: For DRA driver plugins (and only for those!), the kubelet now supports a rolling update with `maxSurge > 0` in the driver's DaemonSet. A DRA driver must support this, which can be done (#129832).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting

wheres_the_proof.text: Graduated the `MultiCIDRServiceAllocator` feature gate to stable, and the `DisableAllocatorDualWrite` feature gate to beta (disabled by default). **Action required** for Kubernetes cluster administrators and for distributions that manage the cluster Service CIDR. Kubernetes now allows users to define the cluster Service CIDR via an API object: ServiceCIDR. Distributions or administrators of Kubernetes may want to control that new Service CIDRs added to the cluster do not overlap with other networks on the cluster, that only belong to a specific range of IPs. Administrators may also prefer to retain the existing behavior of only having one ServiceCIDR per cluster. You can use `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` to achieve this. ([#128971](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128971), [@aojea](https://github.com/aojea)) [SIG Apps, Architecture, Auth, CLI, Etcd, Network, Release and Testing]
sigs: Apps, Architecture, Auth, CLI, Etcd, Network, Release and Testing

wheres_the_proof.text: The `SidecarContainers` feature has graduated to GA. 'SidecarContainers' feature gate was locked to default value and will be removed in v1.36. If you were setting this feature gate explicitly, please remove it now. ([#129731](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129731), [@gjkim42](https://github.com/gjkim42)) [SIG Apps, Node, Scheduling and Testing]

Promoted in-place Pod vertical scaling to beta. The `InPlacePodVerticalScaling` feature gate is now enabled by default. ([#130905](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130905), [@tallclair](https://github.com/tallclair)) [SIG Node]

The `RemoteRequestHeaderUID` feature moves to beta and is now enabled by default. This makes the kube-apiserver propagate UIDs in the `X-Remote-Uid` header in requests to the aggregated API servers. The header is not honored by default for incoming requests, but that can be enabled by setting the `--requestheader-uid-headers` flag explicitly. ([#130560](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130560), [@stlaz](https://github.com/stlaz)) [SIG API Machinery, Auth and Testing]

Graduated the `DisableNodeKubeProxyVersion` feature gate to enable by default, the kubelet no longer attempts to set the `.status.kubeProxyVersion` field for its associated Node. ([#129713](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129713), [@HirazawaUi](https://github.com/HirazawaUi)) [SIG Node]

kubeadm: removed the feature gate EtcdLearnerMode which graduated to GA in 1.32. ([#129589](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129589), [@neolit123](https://github.com/neolit123)) [SIG Cluster Lifecycle]

KEP-3619: fine-grained supplemental groups policy is graduated to Beta. Note that kubelet now rejects pods with `.spec.securityContext.supplementalGroupsPolicy: Strict` when scheduled to the node that does not support the feature (`.status.features.supplementalGroupsPolicy: false`). ([#130210](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130210), [@everpeace](https://github.com/everpeace)) [SIG Apps, Node and Testing]

Kubernetes components that accepted X.509 client certificate authentication now read the user UID from a certificate subject name RDN with object ID `1.3.6.1.4.1.57683.2`. An RDN with this object ID had to contain a string value and appear no more than once in the certificate subject. Reading the user UID from this RDN could be disabled by setting the beta feature gate `AllowParsingUserUIDFromCertAuth` to `false`(until the feature gate graduated to GA). ([#127897](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/127897), [@modulitos](https://github.com/modulitos)) [SIG API Machinery, Auth and Testing]

Promoted the Job's `JobBackoffLimitPerIndex` feature-gate to stable. ([#130061](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130061), [@mimowo](https://github.com/mimowo)) [SIG API Machinery, Apps, Architecture and Testing]
sigs: API Machinery, Apps, Architecture and Testing

wheres_the_proof.text: Added `SchedulerPopFromBackoffQ` feature gate that is in beta and enabled by default. Improved scheduling queue behavior by popping pods from the backoffQ when the activeQ is empty. This allows to process potentially schedulable pods ASAP, eliminating a penalty effect of the backoff queue. # What's New in Kubernetes v1.33

## High-Level Explanation
Kubernetes v1.33 focuses on Native Sidecar Containers, Checkpoint/Restore & Node Lifecycle, API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale, and In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling. For operators, this release translates 261 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Native Sidecar Containers, Checkpoint/Restore & Node Lifecycle**: Improves native sidecar containers, checkpoint/restore & node lifecycle for service-mesh pods, telemetry agents, fast-restoring stateful apps, and oci artifact mounts running on kubelet cri runtime (containerd / cri-o) and linux/windows worker nodes, delivering stops zombie sidecars from holding batch nodes open after job completion.
- **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale**: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.
- **In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling**: Improves in-place pod vertical scaling for stateful microservices, warm inference engines, jvms, and suspended batch jobs needing cpu/ram adjustments running on linux worker nodes and kubelet resource allocation loops, delivering eliminates over-provisioning buffer and avoids expensive pod restart cold-starts during traffic spikes.
- **Feature Enhancements**: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies**: Improves cel-based validating & mutating admission policies for platform security guardrails, multi-tenant compliance policies, and default resource injectors running on in-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments), delivering removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)
| Workload / Team | Models / Services | GPUs / Hardware | Practical Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Native Sidecar Containers, Checkpoint/Restore & Node Lifecycle** | Service-mesh pods, telemetry agents, fast-restoring stateful apps, and OCI artifact mounts | Kubelet CRI runtime (containerd / CRI-O) and Linux/Windows worker nodes | Stops zombie sidecars from holding batch nodes open after job completion |
| **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale** | Operator-heavy platforms, Argo CD / Flux GitOps controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ CRDs/Pods | Control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) CPU and memory footprint | Cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages |
| **In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling (Zero-Restart Resource Resize)** | Stateful microservices, warm inference engines, JVMs, and suspended Batch Jobs needing CPU/RAM adjustments | Linux worker nodes and kubelet resource allocation loops | Eliminates over-provisioning buffer and avoids expensive pod restart cold-starts during traffic spikes |
| **Feature Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies** | Platform security guardrails, multi-tenant compliance policies, and default resource injectors | In-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments) | Removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts |
| **Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) & GPU/Accelerator Management** | AI/ML training, LLM inference pods, fractional/multi-GPU workloads, and NIC/FPGA consumers | NVIDIA/AMD GPU nodes, multi-NIC RDMA clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools | Higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting |
| **API Change Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **DRA (Dynamic Resource Allocation)**: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins. Why it matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.
- **In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling (Resize)**: Changing a running Pod's CPU or memory requests/limits dynamically without killing and recreating the container. Why it matters: Eliminates cold-start restarts and dropped connections when scaling stateful services, databases, or warm AI model servers.
- **Native Sidecar Containers (`initContainers` with `restartPolicy: Always`)**: First-class lifecycle support for helper containers (log shippers, service mesh proxies) so they start before the main app and terminate automatically after Batch Jobs finish. Why it matters: Fixes the classic Kubernetes bug where a finished Job hangs forever because an Istio/Envoy sidecar stays alive.
- **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy & MutatingAdmissionPolicy (CEL)**: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers. Why it matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.
- **Linux User Namespaces (`hostUsers: false`)**: Maps the `root` user inside a container to an unprivileged non-root UID on the host node kernel. Why it matters: Dramatically reduces container-escape blast radius even for legacy workloads that require running as `root` inside the container.
- **WatchList & Snapshottable Watch Cache**: Streaming object lists from `kube-apiserver` memory cache snapshots instead of assembling giant one-shot payloads from `etcd`. Why it matters: Slashes API server RAM spikes and protects `etcd` from OOM crashes during controller restarts on large clusters.
- **nftables `kube-proxy` Backend**: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains. Why it matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.
- **HPA Scale-to-Zero (`minReplicas: 0`)**: Allows `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` to scale external/queue-driven workloads all the way down to 0 replicas when idle and wake them when queue depth rises. Why it matters: Directly cuts cloud compute and GPU bills for bursty batch/inference workers during off-peak hours.
- **CSI (Container Storage Interface)**: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers. Why it matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.

For operators, this release translates 298 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

high_level_changes.headline: Dynamic Resource Allocation
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves dynamic resource allocation for ai/ml training, llm inference pods, fractional/multi-gpu workloads, and nic/fpga consumers running on nvidia/amd gpu nodes, multi-nic rdma clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools, delivering higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting.

high_level_changes.headline: API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.

high_level_changes.headline: API Change Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves api change enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

high_level_changes.headline: Feature Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

high_level_changes.headline: Workload-Aware & Gang Scheduling
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves workload-aware & gang scheduling for distributed ai training, multi-node batch jobs, ray/spark clusters, and mpi workloads running on high-density gpu/cpu batch pools and `kube-scheduler` queues, delivering prevents partial-allocation deadlocks where expensive GPU nodes sit idle waiting for peer workers.
