who_benefits.capability: In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling (Zero-Restart Resource Resize)
who_benefits.models_workloads: Stateful microservices, warm inference engines, JVMs, and suspended Batch Jobs needing CPU/RAM adjustments
who_benefits.gpus_infra: Linux worker nodes and kubelet resource allocation loops
who_benefits.bill_impact: Eliminates over-provisioning buffer and avoids expensive pod restart cold-starts during traffic spikes

jargon_glossary.meaning: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Changing a running Pod's CPU or memory requests/limits dynamically without killing and recreating the container.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates cold-start restarts and dropped connections when scaling stateful services, databases, or warm AI model servers.

jargon_glossary.meaning: An 'all-or-nothing' scheduling guarantee where a group of cooperating Pods (like a multi-node training or distributed inference job) only starts when capacity exists for the entire group.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Prevents expensive GPUs from sitting idle in deadlocked partial allocations when a cluster is near capacity.

jargon_glossary.meaning: First-class lifecycle support for helper containers (log shippers, service mesh proxies) so they start before the main app and terminate automatically after Batch Jobs finish.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Fixes the classic Kubernetes bug where a finished Job hangs forever because an Istio/Envoy sidecar stays alive.

jargon_glossary.meaning: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Streaming object lists from `kube-apiserver` memory cache snapshots instead of assembling giant one-shot payloads from `etcd`.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes API server RAM spikes and protects `etcd` from OOM crashes during controller restarts on large clusters.

jargon_glossary.meaning: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Concise Binary Object Representation (RFC 8949) as a compact binary alternative to JSON for Kubernetes API client-server serialization.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Reduces API server CPU spent on JSON parsing and lowers network bandwidth for custom resources (CRDs) that couldn't use Protobuf.

jargon_glossary.meaning: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.

should_i_upgrade.text: Reverted the `DisableNodeKubeProxyVersion` feature gate to default-off to give a full year from deprecation announcement in 1.29 to clearing the field by default, per the [Kubernetes deprecation policy](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-policy/). ([#126720](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/126720), [@liggitt](https://github.com/liggitt)) [SIG Architecture and Node]

ServiceAccount metadata.annotations[kubernetes.io/enforce-mountable-secrets]: deprecated since v1.32; no removal deadline. Prefer separate namespaces to isolate access to mounted secrets. ([#128396](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128396), [@ritazh](https://github.com/ritazh)) [SIG API Machinery, Apps, Auth, CLI and Testing]
sigs: API Machinery, Apps, Auth, CLI and Testing

should_i_upgrade.text: DRA: the `DeviceRequestAllocationResult` struct now has an "AdminAccess" field which should be used instead of the corresponding field in the `DeviceRequest` field when dealing with an allocation. If a device is only allocated for admin access, allocating it again for normal usage is now supported, as originally intended. To allow admin access, starting with 1.32 the `DRAAdminAccess` feature gate must be enabled. ([#127266](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/127266), [@pohly](https://github.com/pohly)) [SIG API Machinery, Apps, Auth, Etcd, Network, Node, Scheduling and Testing]
sigs: API Machinery, Apps, Auth, Etcd, Network, Node, Scheduling and Testing

should_i_upgrade.text: Removed all support for _classic_ dynamic resource allocation (DRA). The `DRAControlPlaneController` feature gate, formerly alpha, is no longer available. Kubernetes now only uses the _structured parameters_ model (also alpha) for allocating dynamic resources to Pods. if and only if classic DRA was enabled in a cluster, remove all workloads (pods, app deployments, etc. ) which depend on classic DRA and make sure that all PodSchedulingContext resources are gone before upgrading. PodSchedulingContext resources cannot be removed through the apiserver after an upgrade and workloads would not work properly. ([#128003](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128003), [@pohly](https://github.com/pohly)) [SIG API Machinery, Apps, Auth, Etcd, Node, Scheduling and Testing]
sigs: API Machinery, Apps, Auth, Etcd, Node, Scheduling and Testing

should_i_upgrade.text: Added the feature gate CBORServingAndStorage to allow CBOR as the encoding for API request and response bodies, and as the storage encoding for custom resources. Clients must opt in; programs built with client-go can do this using the client-go feature gates ClientsAllowCBOR and ClientsPreferCBOR. ([#128539](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128539), [@benluddy](https://github.com/benluddy)) [SIG API Machinery, Etcd and Testing]

kube-scheduler removed `AzureDiskLimits` ,`CinderLimits` `EBSLimits` and `GCEPDLimits` plugin. Given the corresponding CSI driver reports how many volumes a node can handle in NodeGetInfoResponse, the kubelet stores this limit in CSINode and the scheduler then knows the limit of the driver on the node. Removed plugins AzureDiskLimits, CinderLimits, EBSLimits and GCEPDLimits if you explicitly enabled them in the scheduler config. ([#124003](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/124003), [@carlory](https://github.com/carlory)) [SIG Scheduling, Storage and Testing]

Promoted `CustomResourceFieldSelectors` to stable; the feature was enabled by default. The `--feature-gates=CustomResourceFieldSelectors=true` flag was no longer needed on kube-apiserver binaries and would be removed in a future release. ([#127673](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/127673), [@jpbetz](https://github.com/jpbetz)) [SIG API Machinery and Testing]

Promoted `RetryGenerateName` to stable; the feature is enabled by default. `--feature-gates=RetryGenerateName=true` not needed on kube-apiserver binaries and will be removed in a future release. ([#127093](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/127093), [@jpbetz](https://github.com/jpbetz)) [SIG API Machinery]

kube-apiserver: Promoted `AuthorizeWithSelectors` feature to beta, which includes field and label selector information from requests in webhook authorization calls. Promoted `AuthorizeNodeWithSelectors` feature to beta, which changes node authorizer behavior to limit requests from node API clients, so that each Node can only get / list / watch its own Node API object, and can also only get / list / watch Pod API objects bound to that node. Clients using kubelet credentials to read other nodes or unrelated pods must change their authentication credentials (recommended), adjust their usage, or obtain broader read access independent of the node authorizer. ([#128168](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128168), [@liggitt](https://github.com/liggitt)) [SIG API Machinery, Auth and Testing]

The Job controller now considers sidecar container restart counts when removing pods. ([#124952](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/124952), [@AxeZhan](https://github.com/AxeZhan)) [SIG Apps and CLI]

technical_deep_dive.theme: Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) & GPU/Accelerator Management
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v1.32, teams operating dynamic resource allocation relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA/AMD GPU nodes, multi-NIC RDMA clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools.
tech_bullets: DRA: the `DeviceRequestAllocationResult` struct now has an "AdminAccess" field which should be used instead of the corresponding field in the `DeviceRequest` field when dealing with an allocation. If (#127266).

Removed all support for _classic_ dynamic resource allocation (DRA). The `DRAControlPlaneController` feature gate, formerly alpha, is no longer available. Kubernetes now only uses the _structured (#128003).

The core functionality of Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) got promoted to beta. No action is required when *upgrading*, the previous v1alpha3 API is still supported, so existing deployments and DRA (#127511).

DRA: scheduling pods is up to 16x faster, depending on the scenario. Scheduling throughput depends a lot on cluster utilization. It is higher for lightly loaded clusters with free resources and gets (#127277).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting

technical_deep_dive.theme: API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v1.32, teams operating api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on Control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) CPU and memory footprint.
tech_bullets: Graduated the `WatchList` feature gate to Beta for kube-apiserver and enabled `WatchListClient` for KCM. ([#128053](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128053).

Added the feature gate CBORServingAndStorage to allow CBOR as the encoding for API request and response bodies, and as the storage encoding for custom resources. Clients must opt in; programs built (#128539).
kube-apiserver: Promoted the `StructuredAuthorizationConfiguration` feature gate to GA. The `--authorization-config` flag now accepts `AuthorizationConfiguration` in version (#128172).

Promoted `CustomResourceFieldSelectors` to stable; the feature was enabled by default. The `--feature-gates=CustomResourceFieldSelectors=true` flag was no longer needed on kube-apiserver binaries and (#127673).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages

technical_deep_dive.theme: API Change Enhancements
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v1.32, teams operating api change enhancements relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on Standard cluster nodes and runtime components.
tech_bullets: kube-scheduler removed `AzureDiskLimits` ,`CinderLimits` `EBSLimits` and `GCEPDLimits` plugin. Given the corresponding CSI driver reports how many volumes a node can handle in NodeGetInfoResponse (#124003).

ACTION REQUIRED for custom scheduler plugin developers: `PodEligibleToPreemptOthers` in the `preemption` interface now includes `ctx` in the parameters. Please update your plugins' implementation (#126465).

Implemented a new, alpha `seLinuxChangePolicy` field within a Pod-level `securityContext`, under SELinuxChangePolicy feature gate. This field allows for opting out from mounting Pod volumes with (#127981).
Added the ability to change the maximum backoff delay accrued between container restarts for a node for containers in `CrashLoopBackOff`. To set this for a node, turn on the feature gate (#128374).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil

technical_deep_dive.theme: Feature Enhancements
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v1.32, teams operating feature enhancements relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on Standard cluster nodes and runtime components.
tech_bullets: Graduated `SchedulerQueueingHints` to beta; the feature gate is now enabled by default. ([#128472](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128472), [@sanposhiho](https://github.com/sanposhiho)).
Promoted the `RelaxedEnvironmentVariableValidation` feature gate to beta and is enabled by default. ([#126897](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/126897).
Graduated the AnonymousAuthConfigurableEndpoints feature gate to beta and enable by default to allow configurable endpoints for anonymous authentication. (#127009).
Promoted `SizeMemoryBackedVolumes` to stable. ([#126981](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/126981), [@kannon92](https://github.com/kannon92)) [SIG Node, Storage and Testing].
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil

technical_deep_dive.theme: Workload-Aware & Gang Scheduling (`PodGroup` / `Job` / Queueing)
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v1.32, teams operating workload-aware & gang scheduling relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on High-density GPU/CPU batch pools and `kube-scheduler` queues.
tech_bullets: Graduated Job's `ManagedBy` field to beta. ([#127402](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/127402), [@mimowo](https://github.com/mimowo)) [SIG API Machinery, Apps and Testing].
The Job controller now considers sidecar container restart counts when removing pods. ([#124952](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/124952), [@AxeZhan](https://github.com/AxeZhan)) [SIG.
Annotation `batch.kubernetes.io/cronjob-scheduled-timestamp` added to Job objects scheduled from CronJobs is promoted to stable. ([#128336](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128336).

Label `apps.kubernetes.io/pod-index` added to Pod from StatefulSets is promoted to stable Label `batch.kubernetes.io/job-completion-index` added to Pods from Indexed Jobs is promoted to stable (#128387).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Prevents partial-allocation deadlocks where expensive GPU nodes sit idle waiting for peer workers

technical_deep_dive.theme: CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v1.32, teams operating cel-based validating & mutating admission policies relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on In-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments).
tech_bullets: Introduced `v1alpha1` API for mutating admission policies, enabling extensible #     admission control via CEL expressions (KEP  3962: Mutating Admission Policies). #     To use, enable the (#127134).
The resource/v1alpha3.ResourceSliceList filed which should have been named "metadata" but was instead named "listMeta" is now properly "metadata". (#126749).
Introduced a new metric `kubelet_admission_rejections_total` to track the number of pods rejected during admission. ([#128556](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128556).

Pods were allowed to use the `net.ipv4.tcp_rmem` and `net.ipv4.tcp_wmem` sysctl by default when the kernel version was 4.15 or higher. With the kernel 4.15 the sysctl became namespaced. Pod Security (#127489).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts

# What's New in Kubernetes v1.32

## High-Level Explanation
Kubernetes v1.32 focuses on Dynamic Resource Allocation, API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale, and API Change Enhancements. For operators, this release translates 298 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Dynamic Resource Allocation**: Improves dynamic resource allocation for ai/ml training, llm inference pods, fractional/multi-gpu workloads, and nic/fpga consumers running on nvidia/amd gpu nodes, multi-nic rdma clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools, delivering higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting.
- **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale**: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.
- **API Change Enhancements**: Improves api change enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **Feature Enhancements**: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **Workload-Aware & Gang Scheduling**: Improves workload-aware & gang scheduling for distributed ai training, multi-node batch jobs, ray/spark clusters, and mpi workloads running on high-density gpu/cpu batch pools and `kube-scheduler` queues, delivering prevents partial-allocation deadlocks where expensive GPU nodes sit idle waiting for peer workers.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)

| **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale** | Operator-heavy platforms, Argo CD / Flux GitOps controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ CRDs/Pods | Control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) CPU and memory footprint | Cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages |
| **API Change Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **Feature Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |

| **CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies** | Platform security guardrails, multi-tenant compliance policies, and default resource injectors | In-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments) | Removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts |
| **In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling (Zero-Restart Resource Resize)** | Stateful microservices, warm inference engines, JVMs, and suspended Batch Jobs needing CPU/RAM adjustments | Linux worker nodes and kubelet resource allocation loops | Eliminates over-provisioning buffer and avoids expensive pod restart cold-starts during traffic spikes |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **DRA (Dynamic Resource Allocation)**: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins. Why it matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.
- **In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling (Resize)**: Changing a running Pod's CPU or memory requests/limits dynamically without killing and recreating the container. Why it matters: Eliminates cold-start restarts and dropped connections when scaling stateful services, databases, or warm AI model servers.
- **Gang Scheduling (`Workload` / `PodGroup`)**: An 'all-or-nothing' scheduling guarantee where a group of cooperating Pods (like a multi-node training or distributed inference job) only starts when capacity exists for the entire group. Why it matters: Prevents expensive GPUs from sitting idle in deadlocked partial allocations when a cluster is near capacity.
- **Native Sidecar Containers (`initContainers` with `restartPolicy: Always`)**: First-class lifecycle support for helper containers (log shippers, service mesh proxies) so they start before the main app and terminate automatically after Batch Jobs finish. Why it matters: Fixes the classic Kubernetes bug where a finished Job hangs forever because an Istio/Envoy sidecar stays alive.
- **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy & MutatingAdmissionPolicy (CEL)**: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers. Why it matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.
- **WatchList & Snapshottable Watch Cache**: Streaming object lists from `kube-apiserver` memory cache snapshots instead of assembling giant one-shot payloads from `etcd`. Why it matters: Slashes API server RAM spikes and protects `etcd` from OOM crashes during controller restarts on large clusters.
- **nftables `kube-proxy` Backend**: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains. Why it matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.
- **CBOR Encoding for Kubernetes API**: Concise Binary Object Representation (RFC 8949) as a compact binary alternative to JSON for Kubernetes API client-server serialization. Why it matters: Reduces API server CPU spent on JSON parsing and lowers network bandwidth for custom resources (CRDs) that couldn't use Protobuf.
- **CSI (Container Storage Interface)**: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers. Why it matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.

high_level_changes.headline: API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.

high_level_changes.headline: Workload Identity, User Namespaces & Fine-Grained Authz
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves workload identity, user namespaces & fine-grained authz for multi-tenant saas workloads, zero-trust service meshes, and privileged container migrations running on linux kernel namespaces, kubelet endpoints, and csi secret injection paths, delivering reduces security agent/sidecar overhead and shrinks blast radius of container compromises.

high_level_changes.headline: Feature Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

high_level_changes.headline: API Change Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves api change enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

high_level_changes.headline: Networking, `nftables` Proxy & Traffic Observability
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves networking, `nftables` proxy & traffic observability for high-throughput east-west microservices and latency-sensitive ingress traffic running on linux dataplane (`nftables`/`ipvs`) and cloud load balancers, delivering lowers cross-AZ data transfer costs (`trafficDistribution`) and reduces node CPU spent on iptables rules.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: An 'all-or-nothing' scheduling guarantee where a group of cooperating Pods (like a multi-node training or distributed inference job) only starts when capacity exists for the entire group.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Prevents expensive GPUs from sitting idle in deadlocked partial allocations when a cluster is near capacity.

jargon_glossary.meaning: First-class lifecycle support for helper containers (log shippers, service mesh proxies) so they start before the main app and terminate automatically after Batch Jobs finish.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Fixes the classic Kubernetes bug where a finished Job hangs forever because an Istio/Envoy sidecar stays alive.

jargon_glossary.meaning: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Maps the `root` user inside a container to an unprivileged non-root UID on the host node kernel.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically reduces container-escape blast radius even for legacy workloads that require running as `root` inside the container.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Streaming object lists from `kube-apiserver` memory cache snapshots instead of assembling giant one-shot payloads from `etcd`.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes API server RAM spikes and protects `etcd` from OOM crashes during controller restarts on large clusters.

jargon_glossary.meaning: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.

jargon_glossary.meaning: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.

should_i_upgrade.text: Added support to the scheduler to start using QueueingHint registered for Pod/Updated event to determine whether unschedulable Pods update make them schedulable, when the feature gate `SchedulerQueueingHints` is enabled. Previously, when unschedulable Pods are updated, the scheduler always put Pods back to activeQ/backoffQ. But, actually not all updates to Pods make Pods schedulable, especially considering many scheduling constraints nowadays are immutable. Now, when unschedulable Pods are updated, the scheduling queue checks with QueueingHint(s) whether the update may make the pods schedulable, and requeues them to activeQ/backoffQ **only when** at least one QueueingHint(s) return Queue. Action required for custom scheduler plugin developers: Plugins **have to** implement a QueueingHint for Pod/Update event if the rejection from them could be resolved by updating unscheduled Pods themselves. Example: suppose you develop a custom plugin that denies Pods that have a `schedulable=false` label. Given Pods with a `schedulable=false` label will be schedulable if the `schedulable=false` label is removed, this plugin would implement QueueingHint for Pod/Update event that returns Queue when such label changes are made in unscheduled Pods. ([#122234](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122234), [@AxeZhan](https://github.com/AxeZhan)) [SIG Scheduling and Testing]

Kubelet flag `--keep-terminated-pod-volumes` was removed.  This flag was deprecated in 2017. ([#122082](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122082), [@carlory](https://github.com/carlory)) [SIG Apps, Node, Storage and Testing]

Reduced state change noise when volume expansion fails. Also mark certain failures as infeasible. ACTION REQUIRED:  If you are using the `RecoverVolumeExpansionFailure` alpha feature gate then after upgrading to this release, you need to update some objects. For any existing PersistentVolumeClaimss with `status.allocatedResourceStatus` set to either "ControllerResizeFailed" or "NodeResizeFailed", clear the `status.allocatedResourceStatus`. ([#126108](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/126108), [@gnufied](https://github.com/gnufied)) [SIG Apps, Auth, Node, Storage and Testing]

CephFS volume plugin ( `kubernetes.io/cephfs`) was removed in this release and the `cephfs` volume type became non-functional. Alternative is to use CephFS CSI driver (https://github.com/ceph/ceph-csi/) in your Kubernetes Cluster. A re-deployment of your application is required to use the new driver if you were using `kubernetes.io/cephfs` volume plugin before upgrading cluster version to 1.31+. ([#124544](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/124544), [@carlory](https://github.com/carlory)) [SIG Node, Scalability, Storage and Testing]

Alternative is to use RBD CSI driver (https://github.com/ceph/ceph-csi/) in your Kubernetes Cluster. A re-deployment of your application is required to use the new driver if you were using `kubernetes.io/rbd` volume plugin before upgrading cluster version to 1.31+. ([#124546](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/124546), [@carlory](https://github.com/carlory)) [SIG Node, Scalability, Scheduling, Storage and Testing]

# What's New in Kubernetes v1.31

## High-Level Explanation
Kubernetes v1.31 focuses on API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale, Workload Identity, User Namespaces & Fine-Grained Authz, and Feature Enhancements. For operators, this release translates 333 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale**: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.
- **Workload Identity, User Namespaces & Fine-Grained Authz**: Improves workload identity, user namespaces & fine-grained authz for multi-tenant saas workloads, zero-trust service meshes, and privileged container migrations running on linux kernel namespaces, kubelet endpoints, and csi secret injection paths, delivering reduces security agent/sidecar overhead and shrinks blast radius of container compromises.
- **Feature Enhancements**: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **API Change Enhancements**: Improves api change enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **Networking, `nftables` Proxy & Traffic Observability**: Improves networking, `nftables` proxy & traffic observability for high-throughput east-west microservices and latency-sensitive ingress traffic running on linux dataplane (`nftables`/`ipvs`) and cloud load balancers, delivering lowers cross-AZ data transfer costs (`trafficDistribution`) and reduces node CPU spent on iptables rules.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)
| Workload / Team | Models / Services | GPUs / Hardware | Practical Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale** | Operator-heavy platforms, Argo CD / Flux GitOps controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ CRDs/Pods | Control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) CPU and memory footprint | Cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages |
| **Workload Identity, User Namespaces & Fine-Grained Authz** | Multi-tenant SaaS workloads, zero-trust service meshes, and privileged container migrations | Linux kernel namespaces, kubelet endpoints, and CSI secret injection paths | Reduces security agent/sidecar overhead and shrinks blast radius of container compromises |
| **Feature Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **API Change Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **Networking, `nftables` Proxy & Traffic Observability** | High-throughput east-west microservices and latency-sensitive ingress traffic | Linux dataplane (`nftables`/`ipvs`) and cloud load balancers | Lowers cross-AZ data transfer costs (`trafficDistribution`) and reduces node CPU spent on iptables rules |
| **Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) & GPU/Accelerator Management** | AI/ML training, LLM inference pods, fractional/multi-GPU workloads, and NIC/FPGA consumers | NVIDIA/AMD GPU nodes, multi-NIC RDMA clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools | Higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting |
| **Workload-Aware & Gang Scheduling (`PodGroup` / `Job` / Queueing)** | Distributed AI training, multi-node batch jobs, Ray/Spark clusters, and MPI workloads | High-density GPU/CPU batch pools and `kube-scheduler` queues | Prevents partial-allocation deadlocks where expensive GPU nodes sit idle waiting for peer workers |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **DRA (Dynamic Resource Allocation)**: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins. Why it matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.
- **Gang Scheduling (`Workload` / `PodGroup`)**: An 'all-or-nothing' scheduling guarantee where a group of cooperating Pods (like a multi-node training or distributed inference job) only starts when capacity exists for the entire group. Why it matters: Prevents expensive GPUs from sitting idle in deadlocked partial allocations when a cluster is near capacity.
- **Native Sidecar Containers (`initContainers` with `restartPolicy: Always`)**: First-class lifecycle support for helper containers (log shippers, service mesh proxies) so they start before the main app and terminate automatically after Batch Jobs finish. Why it matters: Fixes the classic Kubernetes bug where a finished Job hangs forever because an Istio/Envoy sidecar stays alive.
- **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy & MutatingAdmissionPolicy (CEL)**: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers. Why it matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.
- **Linux User Namespaces (`hostUsers: false`)**: Maps the `root` user inside a container to an unprivileged non-root UID on the host node kernel. Why it matters: Dramatically reduces container-escape blast radius even for legacy workloads that require running as `root` inside the container.
- **WatchList & Snapshottable Watch Cache**: Streaming object lists from `kube-apiserver` memory cache snapshots instead of assembling giant one-shot payloads from `etcd`. Why it matters: Slashes API server RAM spikes and protects `etcd` from OOM crashes during controller restarts on large clusters.
- **nftables `kube-proxy` Backend**: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains. Why it matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.
- **CSI (Container Storage Interface)**: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers. Why it matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.

## 4. Should I Upgrade?
**Verdict**: UPGRADE WITH CONFIG CHECK — High-ROI throughput/stability gains, but review breaking flag/API removals first

([#122234](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122234))
- **Urgent Upgrade Notes**: Kubelet flag `--keep-terminated-pod-volumes` was removed.  This flag was deprecated in 2017. - **Urgent Upgrade Notes**: Reduced state change noise when volume expansion fails. Also mark certain failures as infeasible. - **Deprecation**: 'kubeadm: marked the sub-phase of ''init kubelet-finilize'' called ''experimental-cert-rotation'' as deprecated and print a warning if it is used directly; it will be removed in a future release. Add a. ([#124419](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/124419))

high_level_changes.headline: API Change Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves api change enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

high_level_changes.headline: Feature Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

high_level_changes.headline: Native Sidecar Containers, Checkpoint/Restore & Node Lifecycle
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves native sidecar containers, checkpoint/restore & node lifecycle for service-mesh pods, telemetry agents, fast-restoring stateful apps, and oci artifact mounts running on kubelet cri runtime (containerd / cri-o) and linux/windows worker nodes, delivering stops zombie sidecars from holding batch nodes open after job completion.

high_level_changes.headline: API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.

high_level_changes.headline: CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves cel-based validating & mutating admission policies for platform security guardrails, multi-tenant compliance policies, and default resource injectors running on in-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments), delivering removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: First-class lifecycle support for helper containers (log shippers, service mesh proxies) so they start before the main app and terminate automatically after Batch Jobs finish.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Fixes the classic Kubernetes bug where a finished Job hangs forever because an Istio/Envoy sidecar stays alive.

jargon_glossary.meaning: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Maps the `root` user inside a container to an unprivileged non-root UID on the host node kernel.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically reduces container-escape blast radius even for legacy workloads that require running as `root` inside the container.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Streaming object lists from `kube-apiserver` memory cache snapshots instead of assembling giant one-shot payloads from `etcd`.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes API server RAM spikes and protects `etcd` from OOM crashes during controller restarts on large clusters.

jargon_glossary.meaning: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Allows `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` to scale external/queue-driven workloads all the way down to 0 replicas when idle and wake them when queue depth rises.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Directly cuts cloud compute and GPU bills for bursty batch/inference workers during off-peak hours.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Concise Binary Object Representation (RFC 8949) as a compact binary alternative to JSON for Kubernetes API client-server serialization.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Reduces API server CPU spent on JSON parsing and lowers network bandwidth for custom resources (CRDs) that couldn't use Protobuf.

should_i_upgrade.text: kubectl: Removed the deprecated flag `prune-whitelist` for apply. Please use the flag `prune-allowlist` instead. ([#120246](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120246), [@pacoxu](https://github.com/pacoxu))

The deprecated `SecurityContextDeny` admission plugin, which has been deprecated since `v1.27`, has been removed. It is recommended to use the Pod Security Admission plugin instead, which has been available since v1.25. Refer to the [Kubernetes documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/admission-controllers/#securitycontextdeny) for more information. ([#122612](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122612), [@mtardy](https://github.com/mtardy))

To disable RemoteCommand over WebSockets for kubectl, the environment variable feature gate must be explicitly set to `false`: `KUBECTL_REMOTE_COMMAND_WEBSOCKETS=false`. ([#123281](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123281), [@seans3](https://github.com/seans3))

AppArmor profiles can now be configured through fields on the `PodSecurityContext` and container `SecurityContext`. The beta AppArmor annotations are deprecated, and AppArmor status is no longer included in the node ready condition. ([#123435](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123435), [@tallclair](https://github.com/tallclair))

kubectl `port-forward` over websockets (tunneling SPDY) can now be enabled using an `Alpha` feature flag environment variable: KUBECTL_PORT_FORWARD_WEBSOCKETS=true. The API Server being communicated to must *also* have an `Alpha` feature flag enabled: PortForwardWebsockets. ([#123413](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123413), [@seans3](https://github.com/seans3))

When configuring a JWT authenticator: If `username.expression` used 'claims.email', then 'claims.email_verified' must have been used in `username.expression` or `extra[*].valueExpression` or `claimValidationRules[*].expression`. An example claim validation rule expression that matches the validation automatically applied when `username.claim` is set to 'email' is 'claims.?email_verified.orValue(true) == true'. ([#123737](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123737), [@enj](https://github.com/enj))

Added audienceMatchPolicy field to AuthenticationConfiguration and support for configuring multiple audiences. The "audienceMatchPolicy" can be empty (or unset) when a single audience is specified in the "audiences" field. The "audienceMatchPolicy" must be set to "MatchAny" when multiple audiences are specified in the "audiences" field. ([#123165](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123165), [@aramase](https://github.com/aramase))

Added the `disable-force-detach` CLI option for `kube-controller-manager`. By default, it's set to `false`. When enabled, it prevents force detaching volumes based on maximum unmount time and node status. If activated, the non-graceful node shutdown feature must be used to recover from node failure. Additionally, if a pod needs to be forcibly terminated at the risk of corruption, the appropriate VolumeAttachment object must be deleted. ([#120344](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120344), [@rohitssingh](https://github.com/rohitssingh))

Removed note that `hostAliases` are not supported on hostNetwork Pods from the PodSpec API. The feature has been supported since v1.8. ([#122422](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122422), [@neolit123](https://github.com/neolit123))

The kubernetes repo now uses Go workspaces.  This should not impact end users at all, but does have impact for developers of downstream projects.  Switching to workspaces caused some breaking changes in the flags to the various k8s.io/code-generator tools.  Downstream consumers should look at staging/src/k8s.io/code-generator/kube_codegen.sh to see the changes. ([#123529](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123529), [@thockin](https://github.com/thockin))

# What's New in Kubernetes v1.30

## High-Level Explanation
Kubernetes v1.30 focuses on API Change Enhancements, Feature Enhancements, and Native Sidecar Containers, Checkpoint/Restore & Node Lifecycle. For operators, this release translates 254 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **API Change Enhancements**: Improves api change enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **Feature Enhancements**: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **Native Sidecar Containers, Checkpoint/Restore & Node Lifecycle**: Improves native sidecar containers, checkpoint/restore & node lifecycle for service-mesh pods, telemetry agents, fast-restoring stateful apps, and oci artifact mounts running on kubelet cri runtime (containerd / cri-o) and linux/windows worker nodes, delivering stops zombie sidecars from holding batch nodes open after job completion.
- **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale**: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.
- **CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies**: Improves cel-based validating & mutating admission policies for platform security guardrails, multi-tenant compliance policies, and default resource injectors running on in-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments), delivering removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)
| Workload / Team | Models / Services | GPUs / Hardware | Practical Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **API Change Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **Feature Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **Native Sidecar Containers, Checkpoint/Restore & Node Lifecycle** | Service-mesh pods, telemetry agents, fast-restoring stateful apps, and OCI artifact mounts | Kubelet CRI runtime (containerd / CRI-O) and Linux/Windows worker nodes | Stops zombie sidecars from holding batch nodes open after job completion |
| **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale** | Operator-heavy platforms, Argo CD / Flux GitOps controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ CRDs/Pods | Control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) CPU and memory footprint | Cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages |
| **CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies** | Platform security guardrails, multi-tenant compliance policies, and default resource injectors | In-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments) | Removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts |
| **Networking, `nftables` Proxy & Traffic Observability** | High-throughput east-west microservices and latency-sensitive ingress traffic | Linux dataplane (`nftables`/`ipvs`) and cloud load balancers | Lowers cross-AZ data transfer costs (`trafficDistribution`) and reduces node CPU spent on iptables rules |
| **Workload Identity, User Namespaces & Fine-Grained Authz** | Multi-tenant SaaS workloads, zero-trust service meshes, and privileged container migrations | Linux kernel namespaces, kubelet endpoints, and CSI secret injection paths | Reduces security agent/sidecar overhead and shrinks blast radius of container compromises |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **DRA (Dynamic Resource Allocation)**: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins. Why it matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.
- **Native Sidecar Containers (`initContainers` with `restartPolicy: Always`)**: First-class lifecycle support for helper containers (log shippers, service mesh proxies) so they start before the main app and terminate automatically after Batch Jobs finish. Why it matters: Fixes the classic Kubernetes bug where a finished Job hangs forever because an Istio/Envoy sidecar stays alive.
- **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy & MutatingAdmissionPolicy (CEL)**: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers. Why it matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.
- **Linux User Namespaces (`hostUsers: false`)**: Maps the `root` user inside a container to an unprivileged non-root UID on the host node kernel. Why it matters: Dramatically reduces container-escape blast radius even for legacy workloads that require running as `root` inside the container.
- **WatchList & Snapshottable Watch Cache**: Streaming object lists from `kube-apiserver` memory cache snapshots instead of assembling giant one-shot payloads from `etcd`. Why it matters: Slashes API server RAM spikes and protects `etcd` from OOM crashes during controller restarts on large clusters.
- **nftables `kube-proxy` Backend**: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains. Why it matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.
- **HPA Scale-to-Zero (`minReplicas: 0`)**: Allows `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` to scale external/queue-driven workloads all the way down to 0 replicas when idle and wake them when queue depth rises. Why it matters: Directly cuts cloud compute and GPU bills for bursty batch/inference workers during off-peak hours.
- **CBOR Encoding for Kubernetes API**: Concise Binary Object Representation (RFC 8949) as a compact binary alternative to JSON for Kubernetes API client-server serialization. Why it matters: Reduces API server CPU spent on JSON parsing and lowers network bandwidth for custom resources (CRDs) that couldn't use Protobuf.

## 4. Should I Upgrade?
**Verdict**: UPGRADE WITH CONFIG CHECK — High-ROI throughput/stability gains, but review breaking flag/API removals first
- **Deprecation**: kubectl: Removed the deprecated flag `prune-whitelist` for apply. Please use the flag `prune-allowlist` instead. ([#120246](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120246). ([#120246](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120246))
- **Deprecation**: The deprecated `SecurityContextDeny` admission plugin, which has been deprecated since `v1.27`, has been removed. It is recommended to use the Pod Security Admission plugin instead, which has been available. ([#122612](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122612))
- **Feature**: To disable RemoteCommand over WebSockets for kubectl, the environment variable feature gate must be explicitly set to `false`: `KUBECTL_REMOTE_COMMAND_WEBSOCKETS=false`.. ([#123281](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123281))

high_level_changes.headline: Feature Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

high_level_changes.headline: API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.

high_level_changes.headline: Dynamic Resource Allocation
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves dynamic resource allocation for ai/ml training, llm inference pods, fractional/multi-gpu workloads, and nic/fpga consumers running on nvidia/amd gpu nodes, multi-nic rdma clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools, delivering higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting.

high_level_changes.headline: Networking, `nftables` Proxy & Traffic Observability
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves networking, `nftables` proxy & traffic observability for high-throughput east-west microservices and latency-sensitive ingress traffic running on linux dataplane (`nftables`/`ipvs`) and cloud load balancers, delivering lowers cross-AZ data transfer costs (`trafficDistribution`) and reduces node CPU spent on iptables rules.

high_level_changes.headline: API Change Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves api change enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Changing a running Pod's CPU or memory requests/limits dynamically without killing and recreating the container.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates cold-start restarts and dropped connections when scaling stateful services, databases, or warm AI model servers.

jargon_glossary.meaning: An 'all-or-nothing' scheduling guarantee where a group of cooperating Pods (like a multi-node training or distributed inference job) only starts when capacity exists for the entire group.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Prevents expensive GPUs from sitting idle in deadlocked partial allocations when a cluster is near capacity.

jargon_glossary.meaning: First-class lifecycle support for helper containers (log shippers, service mesh proxies) so they start before the main app and terminate automatically after Batch Jobs finish.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Fixes the classic Kubernetes bug where a finished Job hangs forever because an Istio/Envoy sidecar stays alive.

jargon_glossary.meaning: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Maps the `root` user inside a container to an unprivileged non-root UID on the host node kernel.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically reduces container-escape blast radius even for legacy workloads that require running as `root` inside the container.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Streaming object lists from `kube-apiserver` memory cache snapshots instead of assembling giant one-shot payloads from `etcd`.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes API server RAM spikes and protects `etcd` from OOM crashes during controller restarts on large clusters.

jargon_glossary.meaning: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.

jargon_glossary.meaning: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.

should_i_upgrade.text: Stopped accepting component configuration for `kube-proxy` and `kubelet` during `kubeadm upgrade plan --config`. This was a legacy behavior that was not well supported for upgrades and could be used only at the plan stage to determine if the configuration for these components stored in the cluster needs manual version migration. In the future, `kubeadm` will attempt alternative component config migration approaches. ([#120788](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120788), [@chendave](https://github.com/chendave))

`kubeadm`: a separate "super-admin.conf" file is now deployed. The User in `admin.conf` is now bound to a new RBAC Group `kubeadm:cluster-admins` that has `cluster-admin` `ClusterRole` access. The User in `super-admin.conf` is now bound to the `system:masters` built-in super-powers / break-glass Group that can bypass RBAC. Before this change, the default `admin.conf` was bound to `system:masters` Group, which was undesired. Executing `kubeadm init phase kubeconfig all` or just `kubeadm init` will now generate the new `super-admin.conf` file. The cluster admin can then decide to keep the file present on a node host or move it to a safe location. `kubadm certs renew` will renew the certificate in `super-admin.conf` to one year if the file exists; if it does not exist a "MISSING" note will be printed. `kubeadm upgrade apply` for this release will migrate this particular node to the two file setup. Subsequent kubeadm releases will continue to optionally renew the certificate in `super-admin.conf` if the file exists on disk and if renew on upgrade is not disabled. `kubeadm join --control-plane` will now generate only an `admin.conf` file that has the less privileged User. ([#121305](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121305), [@neolit123](https://github.com/neolit123))

technical_deep_dive.theme: Feature Enhancements
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v1.29, teams operating feature enhancements relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on Standard cluster nodes and runtime components.
tech_bullets: `kube-controller-manager`: The `LegacyServiceAccountTokenCleanUp` feature gate is now `beta` and enabled by default. When enabled, legacy auto-generated service account token secrets are auto-labeled (#120682).
The KMSv2 features with feature gates `KMSv2` and `KMSv2KDF` are promoted to `GA`.  The `KMSv1` feature gate is now disabled by default. (#121485).
Priority and Fairness feature is now `stable`, the feature gate will be removed in `v1.31`. ([#121638](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121638), [@tkashem](https://github.com/tkashem)).
Changed the `KMSv2KDF` feature gate to be enabled by default. ([#120433](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120433), [@enj](https://github.com/enj)) [SIG API Machinery, Auth and Testing].
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil

technical_deep_dive.theme: API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v1.29, teams operating api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on Control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) CPU and memory footprint.
tech_bullets: `kubeadm`: promoted feature gate `EtcdLearnerMode` to `beta`. Learner mode for joining `etcd` members is now enabled by default. ([#120228](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120228).
Added `apiserver_watch_list_duration_seconds` metrics which will measure response latency distribution in seconds for watchlist requests broken by group, version, resource and scope. (#120490).

`kube-apiserver`: added `--authorization-config` flag for reading a configuration file containing an `apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1alpha1 AuthorizationConfiguration` object. The `--authorization-config` (#120154).

`PriorityLevelConfiguration`: the `.spec.limited.nominalConcurrencyShares` field defaults to `30` only if the field is omitted (v1beta3 also defaulted an explicit `0` value to `30`). Specifying an (#121089).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages

technical_deep_dive.theme: Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) & GPU/Accelerator Management
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v1.29, teams operating dynamic resource allocation relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA/AMD GPU nodes, multi-NIC RDMA clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools.
tech_bullets: `DevicePluginCDIDevices` feature has been graduated to `beta` and enabled by default in the kubelet. ([#121254](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121254).

Added `kubectl node drain` helper callbacks `OnPodDeletionOrEvictionStarted` and `OnPodDeletionOrEvictionFailed`; people extending `kubectl` can use these new callbacks for more granularity. (#117502).
`dra`: the scheduler plugin now avoids additional scheduling attempts in some cases by falling back to SSA after a conflict. ([#120534](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120534).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting

technical_deep_dive.theme: Networking, `nftables` Proxy & Traffic Observability
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v1.29, teams operating networking, `nftables` proxy & traffic observability relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on Linux dataplane (`nftables`/`ipvs`) and cloud load balancers.
tech_bullets: `kube-proxy` now has a new nftables-based mode, available by running `kube-proxy --feature-gates NFTablesProxyMode=true --proxy-mode nftables` This is currently an alpha-level feature and while it (#121046).
Added a new `ipMode` field to the `.status` of Services where `type` is set to `LoadBalancer`. The new field is behind the `LoadBalancerIPMode` feature gate. (#119937).
The `CloudDualStackNodeIPs` feature is now `beta`, meaning that when using an external cloud provider that has been updated to support the feature, you can pass comma-separated dual-stack (#120275).
Added a new `ServiceCIDR` type that allows to dynamically configure the cluster range used to allocate `Service ClusterIPs` addresses. (#116516).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Lowers cross-AZ data transfer costs (`trafficDistribution`) and reduces node CPU spent on iptables rules

technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v1.29, teams operating api change enhancements relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on Standard cluster nodes and runtime components.
tech_bullets: `CSINodeExpandSecret` feature has been promoted to `GA` in this release and is enabled by default. The CSI drivers can make use of the `secretRef` values passed in `NodeExpansion` request optionally (#121303).
'`kube-scheduler` component config (`KubeSchedulerConfiguration`) `kubescheduler.config.k8s.io/v1beta3` is removed in `v1.29`. Migrated `kube-scheduler` configuration files to (#119994).

Promoted `PodReadyToStartContainers` condition to `beta`. ([#119659](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119659), [@kannon92](https://github.com/kannon92)).

technical_deep_dive.theme: CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v1.29, teams operating cel-based validating & mutating admission policies relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on In-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments).
tech_bullets: `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` type checking now supports CRDs and API extensions types. ([#119109](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119109), [@jiahuif](https://github.com/jiahuif)).
`ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` now preserves types of composition variables, and raises type-related errors early. ([#121001](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121001).
CEL cost estimator no longer treats enums as unbounded strings when determining its length. Instead, the length is set to the longest possible enum value. (#121085).
CEL can now correctly handle a CRD `openAPIV3Schema` that has neither `Properties` nor `AdditionalProperties`. ([#121459](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121459).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts

`ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` now preserves types of composition variables, and raises type-related errors early. ([#121001](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121001).
CEL cost estimator no longer treats enums as unbounded strings when determining its length. Instead, the length is set to the longest possible enum value. (#121085).

wheres_the_proof.text: Added `UserNamespacesPodSecurityStandards` feature gate to enable user namespace support for Pod Security Standards. Enabling this feature will modify all Pod Security Standard rules to allow setting: `spec[.*].securityContext.[runAsNonRoot,runAsUser]`. This feature gate should only be enabled if all nodes in the cluster support the user namespace feature and have it enabled. The feature gate will not graduate or be enabled by default in future Kubernetes releases. ([#118760](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118760), [@saschagrunert](https://github.com/saschagrunert)) [SIG API Machinery, Auth, Node and Release]

wheres_the_proof.text: Added new feature gate called `RuntimeClassInImageCriApi` to address `kubelet` changes needed for KEP 4216. Noteable changes: 1. Populate new `RuntimeHandler` field in CRI's `ImageSpec` struct during image pulls from container runtimes. 2. Pass `runtimeHandler` field in `RemoveImage()` call to container runtime in `kubelet`'s image garbage collection. ([#121456](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121456), [@kiashok](https://github.com/kiashok))

`kube-controller-manager`: The `LegacyServiceAccountTokenCleanUp` feature gate is now `beta` and enabled by default. When enabled, legacy auto-generated service account token secrets are auto-labeled with a `kubernetes.io/legacy-token-invalid-since` label if the credentials have not been used in the time specified by `--legacy-service-account-token-clean-up-period` (defaulting to one year), **and** are referenced from the `.secrets` list of a ServiceAccount object, **and**  are not referenced from pods. This label causes the authentication layer to reject use of the credentials. After being labeled as invalid, if the time specified by `--legacy-service-account-token-clean-up-period` (defaulting to one year) passes without the credential being used, the secret is automatically deleted. Secrets labeled as invalid which have not been auto-deleted yet can be re-activated by removing the `kubernetes.io/legacy-token-invalid-since` label. ([#120682](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120682), [@yt2985](https://github.com/yt2985))
Priority and Fairness feature is now `stable`, the feature gate will be removed in `v1.31`. ([#121638](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121638), [@tkashem](https://github.com/tkashem))
`PersistentVolumeLastPhaseTransitionTime` is now beta and enabled by default. ([#120627](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120627), [@RomanBednar](https://github.com/RomanBednar))
Graduated the `ReadWriteOncePod` feature gate to `GA`. ([#121077](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121077), [@chrishenzie](https://github.com/chrishenzie))
The `SidecarContainers` feature has graduated to `beta` and is enabled by default. ([#121579](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121579), [@gjkim42](https://github.com/gjkim42))

`DevicePluginCDIDevices` feature has been graduated to `beta` and enabled by default in the kubelet. ([#121254](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121254), [@bart0sh](https://github.com/bart0sh))

`kubeadm`: promoted feature gate `EtcdLearnerMode` to `beta`. Learner mode for joining `etcd` members is now enabled by default. ([#120228](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120228), [@pacoxu](https://github.com/pacoxu))

Added `apiserver_watch_list_duration_seconds` metrics which will measure response latency distribution in seconds for watchlist requests broken by group, version, resource and scope. ([#120490](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120490), [@p0lyn0mial](https://github.com/p0lyn0mial))
Graduated `Job BackoffLimitPerIndex` feature to `beta`. ([#121356](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121356), [@mimowo](https://github.com/mimowo))

The `volume_zone` plugin will consider `beta` labels as `GA` labels during the scheduling process. Therefore, if the values of the labels are the same, PVs with `beta` labels can also be scheduled to nodes with `GA` labels. ([#118923](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118923), [@AxeZhan](https://github.com/AxeZhan))

`kube-apiserver`: added `--authorization-config` flag for reading a configuration file containing an `apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1alpha1 AuthorizationConfiguration` object. The `--authorization-config` flag is mutually exclusive with `--authorization-modes` and `--authorization-webhook-*` flags. The `alpha` `StructuredAuthorizationConfiguration` feature flag must be enabled for `--authorization-config` to be specified. ([#120154](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120154), [@palnabarun](https://github.com/palnabarun))

`kube-proxy` now has a new nftables-based mode, available by running `kube-proxy --feature-gates NFTablesProxyMode=true --proxy-mode nftables` This is currently an alpha-level feature and while it probably will not eat your data, it may nibble at it a bit. (It passes e2e testing but has not yet seen real-world use.) At this point it should be functionally mostly identical to the iptables mode, except that it does not (and will not) support Service NodePorts on 127.0.0.1. (Also note that there are currently no command-line arguments for the nftables-specific config; you will need to use a config file if you want to set the equivalent of any of the `--iptables-xxx` options.) As this code is still very new, it has not been heavily optimized yet; while it is expected to _eventually_ have better performance than the iptables backend, very little performance testing has been done so far. ([#121046](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121046), [@danwinship](https://github.com/danwinship))
